thread.label: Genesis 2:18
thread.text: And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.

classes.title: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.label: Genesis 3:16
precepts.why:
“I will make him an help meet for him.” To help is to give assistance or support to someone, to provide something useful or necessary in achieving an end. Meet means suitable for him. So the help is the one who assists in making what the husband wants happen. Sometimes the help thinks she is supposed to lead, or thinks she is supposed to guide, but that is not what a help is.

Genesis 3:16 comes after the transgression: “thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” Some have taken this to mean it was only at this point that the woman was supposed to listen to her husband. No. She was told she was the help back in Genesis 2; Genesis 3:16 confirms the rule after the fall.

So why do we feel today that being a help is a bad thing? Sisters, the help is the greatest thing you are ever going to be. The moment you decide being the help is not the greatest thing you can be, or think you are supposed to be something outside of the help, you are going to destroy your marriage.

It cuts both ways. Brothers, the moment you decide not to provide, not to leave the house and work, not to be the man God told you to be, watch what happens to your household: your marriage will crumble and your life will be in shambles. It is a domino effect. And headship is maintenance, a routine thing a husband has to keep doing. A wife will never say she is trying to overthrow you, but it is in her spirit, the same way a man wants to do things his own way when he gets orders from those ranked above him. So you will have to remind her: I am the head, you have to listen to me.

precepts.label: Isaiah 3:12
precepts.why:
Write this down: women were never designed to lead men. God made the woman “an help meet” for the man, and when that order is turned around, Isaiah 3:12 calls it what it is: “As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.”

That is a curse. It is not a good thing; it shows things out of order, not how God set it up. A woman's body alone shows she was not made to lead men into danger: her cycle comes, she is pregnant for nine months, and she is supposed to lead you somewhere?

Women ruling over you is a curse, brothers. Some of you are scared to lead your house and have let her lead. If you are passive, scared, afraid of confrontation, she is going to walk all over you. It is not a secret; everyone sees it, and other men see it in your demeanor. You have to change the way you think. Stand up and take your place back.

The women were designed to be a help to their husbands. When they step outside of that, and when the brothers allow it, chaos follows. That is why there is dysfunction in our nation right now: because the men do not want to lead.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 31:22
precepts.why:
“How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man.” A new thing: women being over men was never heard of. It is not natural, and it is not the natural state of a man to be run by a woman. But you allow it.

God did not set it up that way. In Genesis 2 he made the woman a help meet for the man. When she compasses him instead, the order is upside down.

Cases come up where a brother does not know what is going on in his own house. His wife pays all the bills while he is on the couch playing video games, and he cannot understand why his home is in confusion. It is because his wife is running things. She has been the breadwinner from day one, so she looks at it as normal, and he is used to it. He did not want a wife; he wanted a mama.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 34:31
precepts.why:
“And ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men, and I am your God, saith the Lord God.” The Lord uses men to lead. It has always been that way and it is never going to change. You will not change the order of things just because you are weak, or scared of your wife.

Sisters, the beta men on social media are influencing you, making you think the man is supposed to worship the ground you walk on. That will not influence the men in purple and gold. We are not worried about being called names, narcissist or misogynist. The question is, do you want a man or do you want a boy?

When your husband gets around the brothers and comes home acting different, he is supposed to. He examines himself, sees he is lacking, and comes home on fire to fix his house, with a little more pep in his step and a little more to say. The same goes when he has been rebuked for adultery or for not dealing with his wife the right way: he is supposed to move different. It works in every area if he truly believes.

This is why there is an attack on the household. Satan and his people know that to destroy us they have to attack our foundation, and the foundation is the home. Paul warned that in the last days perilous times would come, with those “Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof”, and “of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts.” They get in through the phone and the conversations, whoever is influencing them. We are building a nation, and if we are not strong on the home front, we will not get off the ground.

thread.label: Genesis 6:1
thread.text: And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,

classes.title: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.label: Exodus 4:22
precepts.why:
Psalm 82 opens: “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” We are the mighty and we are the gods. Then: “How long will ye judge unjustly”? What did we do? Genesis 6:1 tells it: “And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them”. Nations were beginning to form on the earth. Then verse 2 speaks of “the sons of God”.

Who are the sons of God? Exodus 4:22: “And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn”. Now we know who the sons of God are. It is not talking about angels; it is talking about us, before we were called Israel. Before the flood, we were called the sons of God.

“That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” We started taking wives of the other nations, and there were laws on that. Deuteronomy 7:3-4: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them”, “For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods”. Joshua 23:13 warns that such nations “shall be snares and traps unto you, and scourges in your sides, and thorns in your eyes”. These nations, you marry them, and they are snares and traps unto you. Black women who said the white man is better than the black man were put to death by the men they chose. Sherrone Moore already had a white woman at home, but that was not good enough; he needed a young white woman, and he lost everything for a white coontang. That's a snare and a trap right there. Halle Berry has to pay $8,000 a month to that Edomite, and when she pays him, he says thank you, nigger, and walks away. You can't make this stuff up. Tobit 4:12 says to “take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe”, for “our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children”.

That was how we judged unjustly and accepted the persons of the wicked. God's son, his firstborn, broke the law he already had, and the Lord said, “My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.” He cut down our lifespan.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:1
precepts.why:
After Exodus 4:22, 1 John 3:1 confirms it: “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God”. We who? We Israelites. The sons of God of Genesis 6 are not angels; they are us.

So Genesis 6 is about our fathers: “when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.” Our sons became famous men. “And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” The man God was angry with was the sons of God. Once we broke the laws we already had and went in unto the daughters of men, our kids turned into the devil and started acting like the devil on the planet. That is why God had to bring the flood.

Psalm 82:6-7 says of us: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High. But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.” The flood came and we all died, and we came back through Noah's son Shem. And we still have not learned our lesson. Today the same snares catch our men and women who leave their own people for other nations, and it costs them everything.

precepts.label: Romans 8:19
precepts.why:
“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” All creation is waiting for the sons of God, Israel, to be revealed. The sons of God fell in Genesis 6 by judging unjustly, but the plan still stands.

Psalm 82:8: “Arise, O God, judge the earth: for thou shalt inherit all nations.” Psalm 2:8 says to Christ: “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.” And we are joint heirs: Romans 8:17, “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ”. What Christ gets, he gives to us. Revelation 2:26-27: “to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”, “even as I received of my Father.”

Christ has made us “kings and priests” (Revelation 1:6), and Paul says, “Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?” The saints are the children of Israel, as Psalm 148:14 says. “Know ye not that we shall judge angels?” The angels we will judge are not Michael or Gabriel; they are each other, the twelve tribes, as Christ promised the twelve would sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

That is the manifestation creation is waiting for. We may look like nobody now, but in time we will rule the nations with Christ. All we have to do is endure to the end.

thread.label: Genesis 9:25
thread.text: And he said, Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.

classes.title: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 6:54
precepts.why:
People like to say the Israelites stole the Canaanites' land. We stole nothing; the land was ours, and anything a slave owns belongs to his master. Noah gave the prophecy: “Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.” Then he is more specific: “Blessed be the Lord God of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.” Israel comes out of Shem, so the Canaanites shall be the servants of Israel. “God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem”. Whose tents would Japheth be living in? Shem's, the Israelites'. Everything belongs to Shem.

At Genesis 9 there were no twelve tribes yet. Israel does not come into being until Jacob's name is changed in Genesis 32, so Noah speaks in terms of Shem, Ham and Japheth. 2 Esdras 6:54 brings it forward to the chosen people: “And after these, Adam also, whom thou madest lord of all thy creatures: of him come we all, and the people also whom thou hast chosen.” Then the part that was wanted, verse 55: “All this have I spoken before thee, O Lord, because thou madest the world for our sakes”. God made the world for our sake.

Psalm 82 was read as going with Esdras and Daniel. “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” Verse 6: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” We are not the Most High, but we are the powers of this earth, the judges of the whole planet. The whole earth belongs to the Israelites.

Verse 5 shows it was always meant to be that way: “They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” All means everything. If the Israelites are not ruling the planet with God's commandments and laws, everything is out of line, out of the natural way God made it, and there is gross darkness among the people everywhere else. So Canaan being made a servant is part of God's whole plan: the world was made for the chosen, and everything goes back to them.

precepts.label: Daniel 7:27
precepts.why:
After Esdras showed that God made the world for our sakes, Daniel 7:27 gives the next prophecy: “And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High”. What is under the whole heaven is the planet earth. The earth shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High.

Psalm 148:14 shows who the saints are: “He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”. Even means indeed: indeed the children of Israel. The Israelites are the saints. Everything on this planet is going back to the Israelites, including the planet itself.

Daniel goes on: “whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.” Everybody is going to obey Christ. “Hitherto is the end of the matter”: that is the whole plan of God. “As for me Daniel, my cogitations much troubled me”, meaning his thoughts troubled him, “and my countenance changed in me: but I kept the matter in my heart.”

This is the end of what began with Noah's words over Canaan. Canaan is a servant of servants and Japheth dwells in the tents of Shem, because the dominion under the whole heaven belongs to Shem's chosen seed. From there the class went to Jeremiah 34 to show what it cost Israel when we disobeyed the year of release and would not let our own brethren go free.

thread.label: Genesis 37:25-35
thread.text: And they sat down to eat bread: and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and, behold, a company of Ishmeelites came from Gilead with their camels bearing spicery and balm and myrrh, going to carry it down to Egypt.

classes.title: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.label: Genesis 25:1-4
precepts.why:
When Joseph’s brothers sat down to eat bread, they saw “a company of Ishmeelites came from Gilead with their camels bearing spicery and balm and myrrh, going to carry it down to Egypt.” Judah said, “What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood? Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites.” Then the verse changes names: “Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver.”

There are always questions about the Midianites and the Ishmaelites. Genesis 25 shows who the Midianites were: “Then again Abraham took a wife, and her name was Keturah. And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.” Keturah had six sons by Abraham, and Midian is one of them. The chapter goes on to his sons: “And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.”

So the Midianites are Abraham’s children through Keturah, just as the Ishmaelites are Abraham’s children through Hagar. They were working together and roaming the land together, all Abraham’s kids, and they looked very similar. That is why the story says Ishmaelites, then Midianites, then “the Midianites sold him into Egypt unto Potiphar,” and then in Genesis 39 Potiphar “bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites.” It is not a contradiction; these groups were together.

precepts.label: Genesis 25:12-16
precepts.why:
Genesis 37 names both groups in the sale of Joseph: the Midianites drew him out of the pit and “sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver,” and later “the Midianites sold him into Egypt unto Potiphar.” Genesis 25:12 shows who the Ishmaelites were: “Now these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s handmaid, bare unto Abraham.”

Abraham had Ishmael from Hagar, and Ishmael had sons as well: Nebajoth the firstborn, “and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam, And Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa, Hadar, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.” “These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their towns, and by their castles; twelve princes according to their nations.”

Abraham’s children from Keturah and Abraham’s children from Hagar always lived together and worked together. So when a company of Ishmaelites comes by carrying spices down to Egypt and Midianite merchantmen are among them, it is one caravan of Abraham’s other children traveling side by side.

Meanwhile the brothers, so envious of Joseph, dipped his coat of many colours in the blood of a kid of the goats and let Jacob believe “an evil beast hath devoured him.” Reuben had suggested the pit so he could come back and save him, and when he returned, “Joseph was not in the pit; and he rent his clothes.” Envy will have you do evil things. Remember Reuben’s character; it plays a part later.

thread.label: Genesis 38:26-30
thread.text: And Judah acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son. And he knew her again no more.

classes.title: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 25:5-6
precepts.why:
About three months after Judah went in to Tamar, she began to show, and word came to Judah that his daughter-in-law had played the harlot and was with child by whoredom. Her husband was dead and she was living in her father's house, so Judah said, “Bring her forth, and let her be burnt”: that was the law for a harlot. But she sent him his own signet, bracelets and staff, and “Judah acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son.” The child was his, and he was the one in the wrong.

Deuteronomy 25 shows what Judah and Onan owed her. Moses recites this law later, but our forefathers already had knowledge of it through oral tradition passed down from Adam. “If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her.” That is why it was wrong when Onan spilled his seed on the ground.

“the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.” To succeed in the name of the dead brother does not mean the child takes his actual name. It means the child inherits the dead man's possession, his land and his things, because he left no seed to inherit for him. The brother raises up a surrogate seed in honor of his dead brother, so the land stays in his brother's name and is not lost.

A brother who refuses is brought before the elders. His brother's wife shall “loose his shoe from off his foot, and spit in his face”, saying, “So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother’s house.” And “his name shall be called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.” He carries that humiliation forever, because he would not love his neighbor as himself. That is why the history of Ruth is so important. It is not about Ruth, the Moabite heathen woman; y'all make it about her because y'all love heathens.

So Tamar was more righteous than Judah: she kept her dead husband's name alive when Judah withheld Shelah. From her came twins. Zarah put out his hand first and the midwife bound a scarlet thread on it, but he drew it back and his brother broke forth: “this breach be upon thee: therefore his name was called Pharez.” Pharez means a breach, and the line of the kings runs through him.

thread.label: Genesis 39:1-6
thread.text: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites, which had brought him down thither.

classes.title: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.label: Luke 16:10
precepts.why:
Joseph was seventeen, a teenager, sold into Egypt: “Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites.” Yet “the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man.” His master “saw that the Lord was with him, and that the Lord made all that he did to prosper in his hand,” and made him overseer over his house, putting all that he had into his hand.

Luke 16:10 explains why: “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.” Joseph was in slavery, but he was faithful to Potiphar, and Potiphar raised him up.

It speaks to us today. Many brothers and sisters have jobs, and the Most High is observing us in whatever we do. The least that we are faithful in is these little jobs out here. Just as Joseph was in captivity, we are in captivity, but that does not mean we can steal, lie or rob. When you are on your jobs, do not steal; deal right. God is watching each and every one of us.

And look what faithfulness brought: “the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of the Lord was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.” The theme is the same as when Jacob worked for Laban all those years and Laban was blessed for Jacob’s sake. Faithful in little, Joseph was trusted with much, until his master “knew not ought he had, save the bread which he did eat.”

thread.label: Genesis 39:7-12
thread.text: And it came to pass after these things, that his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.

classes.title: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 21:2-3
precepts.why:
Potiphar’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph and said, “Lie with me.” Joseph refused, and he did not refuse half-heartedly: “how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?” Notice he was not blaming God that he was a slave in a strange land. His master had kept nothing back from him “but thee, because thou art his wife,” and Joseph would not touch her.

This was not a single moment. “she spake to Joseph day by day”; she was trying to wear him down day by day. And the Egyptians loved beautiful women; remember when Abraham went down into Egypt, Sarah was in danger because of her beauty. Potiphar’s wife was no ugly woman; she was good on the eyes, and Joseph, at 17 years old, still said no. When she finally “caught him by his garment,” “he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.”

Sirach gives the precept for what Joseph did: “Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest too near it, it will bite thee: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.” Joseph saw sin like a snake, and he ran like a rabbit. If a snake fell into the room right now, everybody would be out of there. That snake is your sin. “All iniquity is as a two edged sword, the wounds whereof cannot be healed.”

Everybody's demon is not the same. For some it is food; for most of the brothers it is sexual demons, and those demons will get you. Put yourself in Joseph's place and be honest about it: many have been put out for adultery two and three times. Take a page out of what our forefather Joseph did: don't stand there and reason with it, don't come near it. Flee.

thread.label: Genesis 39:13-20
thread.text: And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and was fled forth,

classes.title: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 28:14
precepts.why:
When Potiphar’s wife could not get her way, she lied. She called the men of her house and said, “See, he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us; he came in unto me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice.” Then “she laid up his garment by her, until his lord came home”: she kept his clothes as false evidence, and told her husband the same lie.

Sirach shows what that kind of tongue does: “A backbiting tongue hath disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: strong cities hath it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men.” Somebody that lies on you can do much destruction. Joseph was the greatest man in Potiphar's house, trusted with everything, and a lying tongue brought him down to the king's prison.

It is the same today. Many brothers have been locked up because a woman lied on them: an ex-wife or ex-girlfriend who wants his life to go down the tubes, who calls him over, is refused, and then threatens to tell the police he hurt her. Others are in jail because a woman started a fight and expected him to defend her. Don't deal with a woman like that; that is the kind of woman Joseph had over him.

And this same spirit met our people in slavery. A lot of us were put to death because of it. Emmett Till was put to death for the lying woman, and there are a lot of cases like that. What Potiphar's wife did to Joseph, a backbiting tongue has done to Israel again and again.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 28:18
precepts.why:
Sirach goes on: “Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue.” The tongue does a lot of evil, and that is exactly what Potiphar’s wife did to Joseph. She never lifted a sword against him; she only spoke, and her words did the work.

She told her husband, “The Hebrew servant, which thou hast brought unto us, came in unto me to mock me,” and “when his master heard the words of his wife,” “his wrath was kindled.” On nothing but her word, “Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were bound.” Remember how old Joseph is here: 17.

That is how our people have fallen too: brothers in prison on a lie, and in slavery times men like Emmett Till put to death because of a lying woman's words. More have fallen by the tongue than by the sword. Guard yourself from the kind of company that can destroy you with a word.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 2:1-4
precepts.why:
Joseph was 17, falsely accused, and thrown into the king's prison. Sirach tells you why this should not shock a servant of God: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” Joseph understood this, because his father Jacob taught him.

“Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.” Make not haste means don't leave this truth in your time of trouble. Satan will tell you, if you weren't in that Bible you wouldn't be going through half of what you're going through; you had it better when you served me. “Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end.”

“Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate.” Joseph's family was rich; Jacob was a wealthy man. Joseph was taken from all that, sold as a slave, and now he is in the midst of poverty, in prison, for a crime he refused to commit. That is a low estate, and he bore it without leaving God.

Just as it goes for us, it went for our father Joseph. Israel today has been brought down to a low estate, and the tests and trials come because we serve the Lord. Endure them, cleave unto him, and you will be increased at your last end, as Joseph was.

thread.label: Genesis 39:21-23
thread.text: But the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.

classes.title: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.label: Proverbs 16:7
precepts.why:
Even in prison, “the Lord was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.” The keeper “committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners that were in the prison,” and “looked not to any thing that was under his hand; because the Lord was with him, and that which he did, the Lord made it to prosper.”

Solomon gives the reason: “When a man’s ways please the Lord, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.” That is what happened with Joseph. He was a Hebrew slave, accused of attacking his master's wife, locked in the place where the king's prisoners were bound, and his very jailer became favourable to him and handed him the whole prison.

It is the same pattern all through Joseph's life: in Potiphar's house the Lord blessed the Egyptian's house “for Joseph’s sake,” just as Laban was blessed for Jacob's sake when Jacob worked for him. Joseph's ways pleased the Lord; he refused sin even when it cost him, and whatever he did, the Lord made it to prosper. Keep your ways pleasing to God, and he will make even those set over you in captivity to be at peace with you.

thread.label: Genesis 40:1-23
thread.text: And it came to pass after these things, that the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker had offended their lord the king of Egypt.

classes.title: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 34:1-3
precepts.why:
The butler and the baker of the king of Egypt offended their lord and were put in ward “the place where Joseph was bound.” “they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream in one night,” and in the morning they were sad, because “there is no interpreter of it.” Joseph answered, “Do not interpretations belong to God? tell me them, I pray you.”

Sirach speaks to dreams: “The hopes of a man void of understanding are vain and false: and dreams lift up fools.” “Whoso regardeth dreams is like him that catcheth at a shadow, and followeth after the wind.” Don't chase dreams; a man who lives by every dream is grasping at shadows.

But verse 3 gives a clue to understanding the dreams that come from God: “The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another, even as the likeness of a face to a face.” You may dream about somebody you know, say a man named Joe, and see Joe's face; but it is not Joe. It is someone similar to Joe, maybe in age or in what they do for a living. It could be Bob. You just have to know the people in your circle.

That is how the dreams in Genesis 40 work. The butler's vine with “three branches” and the baker's “three white baskets” were resemblances of one thing to another: the three branches and the three baskets were three days. The interpretation belonged to God, and Joseph gave it.

precepts.label: Lamentations 3:53
precepts.why:
After interpreting the butler's dream, Joseph asked him, “think on me when it shall be well with thee,” and “make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:” “For indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.” He wanted out of that dungeon.

Notice the prison is called a dungeon. Lamentations uses the same word: “They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me.” To cast a stone upon him means he would never get out. It is speaking of Israel in captivity.

That goes with our political prisoners, who have been in there for a long time, cut off in the dungeon with a stone cast over them. Joseph, stolen away and imprisoned though he had done nothing, is a picture of his people in captivity.

precepts.label: Job 3:3
precepts.why:
Joseph's interpretations came to pass “the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, that he made a feast unto all his servants.” On that birthday “he restored the chief butler unto his butlership again,” “But he hanged the chief baker: as Joseph had interpreted to them.”

Wherever you read of a birthday in scripture, Pharaoh's birthday, Herod's birthday, the birthday of one of the Greek kings, something bad happens. Here a man is hanged at a birthday feast. A birthday is a day of narcissism, a day of proclaiming yourself to be God.

Job shows how the Hebrews felt about the day of their birth: “Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived.” A righteous man did not exalt the day he was born; he wished it would perish. That is why we never celebrated birthdays.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 20:14
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says the same thing Job said: “Cursed be the day wherein I was born: let not the day wherein my mother bare me be blessed.” Two prophets, and neither one blessed the day of his birth. Put that together with Pharaoh's birthday in Genesis 40, where the baker was hanged at the feast.

We never celebrated birthdays. They are days of narcissism, days to put ourselves up above God. The custom came from the nations; it came through the white man, who got it from what they dug up in their archaeological digs, and then taught that we should be celebrating birthdays.

So stop celebrating that foolishness, even with the excuse that it's for the children. Shut up, you narcissist. It is not of God. It's of the devil. And after that birthday feast, “Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.”

thread.label: Genesis 41:1-57
thread.text: And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and, behold, he stood by the river.

classes.title: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.label: Proverbs 22:29
precepts.why:
“at the end of two full years” Pharaoh dreamed of seven fat kine eaten up by seven lean kine, and seven good ears devoured by seven thin ears “blasted with the east wind.” None of the magicians could interpret it, until the chief butler remembered his faults and told Pharaoh of the young Hebrew. “Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.”

Solomon wrote the precept: “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.” The business is God's business. Joseph was diligent in it in Potiphar's house and in the prison, and now a slave out of the dungeon stands before the king of Egypt. Even there he gave God the glory: “It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.”

And he did not come to Pharaoh with only a problem. He told him the dream is one, seven years of plenty and seven of famine, “because the thing is established by God,” and then he told him exactly what to do: appoint officers, take up the fifth part in the plenteous years, and lay up corn against the famine. To every problem, brothers, we must have a solution. Some spirits among us have a problem for every solution; stay away from brothers and sisters like that.

So Pharaoh said, “Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is?” He put his ring upon Joseph's hand, arrayed him in fine linen, made him ride in the second chariot, “and they cried before him, Bow the knee.” We are going to tell the nations that too: bow the knee. “Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh”; he went in at 17 and spent 13 years in servitude and prison before he stood before the king.

This is why you see Israel today meeting dignitaries across the world: because we have been diligent in God's business. Mean men are obscure men, bums on the internet with a handful of followers who want to debate you for clout, whose numbers go up as soon as they see the shirt. They are not worth your time. A man diligent in God's business stands before kings.

precepts.label: Romans 12:11
precepts.why:
Proverbs says “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings,” and Paul shows which business that is: “Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord.” That is the proof. The business is God's business, serving the Lord, and you must not be slothful when it comes to it.

That is the business Joseph was about. He served faithfully in Potiphar's house and in the prison, he gave God the credit before Pharaoh, and he was fervent, not asleep, when the answer was needed. He is the diligent man who stood before kings.

So don't be over there asleep in the things of God. Be fervent in spirit, serving the Lord, and God will set you before kings and not before mean men, as he did Joseph.

precepts.label: Genesis 43:32
precepts.why:
“And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph’s brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.” Our forefathers hated Joseph and sold him into slavery. He gained status in Egypt, Egypt got through the famine by his counsel, and now his brothers came to Egypt to buy food.

“And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.” If Joseph had been a German Jew, or from Holland, Ukraine or Poland, they would have known him: a white man in Egyptian clothes stands out among Egyptians, because the Egyptians are black. They could not recognize their brother because he was dressed in Egyptian garb, beard shaved, looking like an Egyptian. “for he spake unto them by an interpreter”: he acted the part, speaking Egyptian so they would not know him. Joseph passed for an African, a black man, just as Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were dark ancestors.

Then Genesis 43:32, at the meal: “And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which did eat with him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.” That is Jim Crow. The Hebrews sat over there and the Egyptians over here, because them sitting together was an abomination. Israel had its own land, Goshen, and Egypt was apart. It was still segregation, even though both were dark: same color, different nation.

The pictures shown from the history books said the same. The Egyptians are brown. The Israelites working in the granary under a taskmaster have afros. Pharaoh is black, and Tutankhamun is black. Nefertiti is black as hell, and the Nubians are black as hell. The sacrifice of Isaac in the mosaic of the Beth Alpha synagogue shows Abraham and Isaac as black. The sons of Ham, the Egyptians, Canaanites, Nubians and Libyans, are all dark; we fought the Canaanites in the land, and they are black too.

Moses passed for an Egyptian the same way. Jethro's daughters said, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds”. Moses married an Ethiopian woman, a daughter of Ham, and a Hamite would have known a white man was no Egyptian. Even Pharaoh's daughter knew the baby was a Hebrew only because he was circumcised, since both peoples were black.

thread.label: Genesis 43:1-10
thread.text: And the famine was sore in the land.

precepts.label: Acts 11:28
precepts.why:
“And the famine was sore in the land.” There have always been famines. The only difference now is that we think a famine could never happen, because we have grown accustomed to living here.

Luke records one: “there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Cesar.” It did not come to pass the moment Agabus signified it. He had it under Caligula; Caligula was put to death, and Claudius came in, some five to ten years later, and then the dearth came.

That is said for a reason. We are telling our people famine is coming, and some are preparing while some are not. The word does not fail just because it does not happen the next day. In Genesis 43 the corn from Egypt was eaten up, and Jacob had to send his sons back, Benjamin with them, with Judah saying, “that we may live, and not die, both we, and thou, and also our little ones.” The famine came, as Joseph said it would.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 16:19-22
precepts.why:
Ezra explains why famines come: “Behold, famine and plague, tribulation and anguish, are sent as scourges for amendment.” “But for all these things they shall not turn from their wickedness, nor be always mindful of the scourges.”

Scourges come, like what happened with George Floyd among us, and 9/11. But our people tend to forget. Civil rights came around 1964 and 1965, 62 years ago, and people said it could never happen again, the same way people in South Africa act like apartheid never happened. Now they are bringing back vagrancy laws under the 13th Amendment, where the homeless get arrested and prison labor becomes slavery again. They are redrawing district lines, as with the Texas map that moves Representative Jasmine Crockett's home out of her district, so black representatives lose their seats and our people lose their voice in Congress.

“Behold, victuals shall be so good cheap upon earth, that they shall think themselves to be in good case, and even then shall evils grow upon earth, sword, famine, and great confusion.” While food is cheap and everybody thinks things are fine, supermarkets are being moved out of our communities and our people are being priced off the cruise lines and airlines. The evils are growing behind the scenes.

And nobody has solutions. Idi Amin expelled the Asian and European merchants from Uganda and handed their businesses to Ugandans who had no experience in the imports and exports, and the stores collapsed. South Africa today beats and drives out legal migrants from Ghana, Nigeria and the ECOWAS region who own small stores, while about 90 percent of the businesses and the land belong to white people: they turn against their own brothers while the real owners of the country stand in front of them. Black people in America burn down stores in our own neighborhoods instead of saving our money and opening our own, and the white man's solution is jail time.

“For many of them that dwell upon earth shall perish of famine; and the other, that escape the hunger, shall the sword destroy.” The Bible is telling you famine is coming upon the earth, even though people say, never in America. Egypt had its famine in Joseph's day, and it will come again.

precepts.label: Isaiah 34:16
precepts.why:
Isaiah gives the rule for what belongs in the word of God: “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read: no one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate.” No prophecy shall fail, and every scripture has its mate. You cannot mate another book with the Bible.

Esau is now loading the Bible apps with additional books. Not the Apocrypha, which we read, but books like Enoch and Jasher. Read Jasher's account of the very events of Genesis 43 and 44, and it sounds strange, because it didn't happen that way: Judah threatening to slay all Egypt, throwing a stone of 400 shekels up to the heavens and sitting on it until it turned to dust, and Joseph's son Manasseh doing the same, when Manasseh and Ephraim were only little children at that time.

In Genesis the brothers go down to Egypt because of the famine, Judah pledges himself for Benjamin, “I will be surety for him,” and every piece of the story lines up with the rest of scripture. Jasher has no mate in the book of the Lord. That is why we stay away from those books.

thread.text: And Joseph made haste; for his bowels did yearn upon his brother: and he sought where to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there.

classes.title: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.label: Revelation 11:8
precepts.why:
When Joseph saw Benjamin, “his bowels did yearn upon his brother,” and he went into his chamber and wept. Then he washed his face and said, “Set on bread.” They set on for Joseph by himself, for his brethren by themselves, and for the Egyptians by themselves, “because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.”

That is here as evidence that America is Egypt. John wrote: “And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.” The great city is Babylon the Great. It is not the real Sodom or the real Egypt; it is spiritually Sodom and spiritually Egypt. On the dollar bill you have the pyramid with 1776 at the bottom and Novus Ordo Seclorum, New World Order; the obelisk stands in Washington, D.C. America knows it is a spiritual Egypt where tribes of Israel are held captive.

And like ancient Egypt, it counted eating with the Hebrews an abomination. In the Jim Crow era it was an abomination for Esau to sit with us or let us sit in their restaurants. The signs read: we serve whites only, no Spanish or Mexicans; no dogs and no Mexicans, El Paso, Texas, 1929; and across the South we were forbidden their restaurants, their toilets, even their water fountains. Issachar was included in that too, no matter how light their skin; afterwards many Mexicans petitioned to be classified as white, because they had been classified as Negroes. This is not only ancient history; it was just over 60 years ago.

We have had our 62 years since civil rights, and what have we done with them? The same as South Africa since apartheid ended in 1994: nothing. We have not organized; we still have no hospitals of our own, and we gave up the bus lines and institutions we had in order to integrate. Now Esau is taking the integration laws away.

And “where also our Lord was crucified”: our Lord was crucified in Jerusalem, so this is a spiritual Jerusalem as well. The same spirits that hated and murdered Christ are back again here, in Babylon the Great. They hate his image, and they hate his teachings.

precepts.label: Daniel 8:23
precepts.why:
“when money failed in the land of Egypt,” all the Egyptians came to Joseph and said, “Give us bread: for why should we die in thy presence? for the money faileth.” Listen to that: money failed. What good is money in a time of famine? It is useless. The first year they gave their cattle for bread. The second year there was “not ought left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands,” so they said, “buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants unto Pharaoh.” “so the land became Pharaoh’s.”

Don't think that can never happen again. The things written aforetime were written for our learning. The Agenda 21 plan is total collectivism: people dependent on the state for everything, no private property or land of their own, housed in high-rise apartments provided as a benefit, because anyone with a couple of acres, his own water and his own food is a threat to it. BlackRock and Blackstone are buying up housing across America and controlling the rents. It is Genesis 47 again: take care of us, and we will give up everything. And as KRS-One said, we never lost our lands, we lost our minds; the intellectuals stay quiet because the paycheck dictates what comes out of the mind.

Daniel shows the hour it is: “And in the latter time of their kingdom, when the transgressors are come to the full, a king of fierce countenance, and understanding dark sentences, shall stand up.” That is the era we are in now. There are people in this administration studying the scriptures, reading from sunup to sundown and taking notes. Psalms 64:6 says it: “they accomplish a diligent search.”

While you struggle to do your four chapters a day, they have made study their job. While the grocery stores move out of our communities and Section 8 is taken away, too many of our people are still playing with adultery and lies. God has no time for that.

precepts.label: Hosea 12:10
precepts.why:
“I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” God speaks in similitudes. What happened in Egypt under Joseph is not just a nice story; it is a likeness of what is coming.

The Egyptians, when money failed, gave up their cattle, then their bodies and their lands, and became servants unto Pharaoh. That is a similitude of a people today, in the spiritual Egypt, who will give up their property and their freedom to the government in exchange for bread. The plans are being made behind the scenes now.

The same is true of the scriptures that follow: when the prophets speak of Egypt, understand the similitude. The Egypt of Isaiah 19 is Babylon the Great, the great city “which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt.”

precepts.label: Isaiah 19:1-4
precepts.why:
“The burden of Egypt. Behold, the Lord rideth upon a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and the heart of Egypt shall melt in the midst of it.” This Egypt is Babylon the Great, the same great city of Revelation 11:8, spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.

“And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.” That is civil war. Don't be surprised if it is blue states against red states, Democrats against Republicans, and everybody picks a side. Already the government is paying the January 6th rioters, over a riot in which five people died.

“And the spirit of Egypt shall fail in the midst thereof”: that great American battle cry shall fail. “and I will destroy the counsel thereof: and they shall seek to the idols, and to the charmers, and to them that have familiar spirits, and to the wizards.”

“And the Egyptians will I give over into the hand of a cruel lord; and a fierce king shall rule over them, saith the Lord, the Lord of hosts.” That is this administration right now, the fierce king of Daniel 8:23. Egypt in Joseph's day sold itself to Pharaoh for bread; the spiritual Egypt will be given over into the hand of a cruel lord.

Jacob called his sons to tell them “that which shall befall you in the last days,” and of Judah he said, “thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies.” That says two things: Judah will be fighting his enemy, and Judah will be living in close proximity to his enemy, who today is Esau, Edom. Zechariah 2 is the scripture that proves Judah will be living with that enemy.

“Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord.” Then: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Zion is the city of Judah. The daughter of Babylon, as Psalms 137 shows, is Edom, the Caucasian race. So Zion is dwelling with the daughter of Babylon: Judah living in the land of the north, in the house of his enemy.

That is the picture of Genesis 49:8. Judah’s hand in the neck of his enemies is Judah living with him and contending with him. In the 1960s and 70s there was the Black Panthers, Martin Luther King, Malcolm X, and many movements where Judah rose up and fought the so-called white man. “he stooped down, he couched as a lion,” and at one point it looked like he was about to strike.

precepts.label: Psalms 83:3
precepts.why:
Jacob called his sons together in Egypt to tell them “that which shall befall you in the last days,” and highlight those last words: the last days. Of Joseph he said, “Joseph is a fruitful bough, even a fruitful bough by a well; whose branches run over the wall.” By a well: they would live by the waters, on islands, in the last days. The walls are forts like El Morro, built by the Spanish to keep the other European powers out of places like Puerto Rico. “The archers have sorely grieved him, and shot at him, and hated him”: the conquistadors sorely grieved him. “But his bow abode in strength.”

The Spaniards' own records, gathered in the book Lost Tribes and Promised Land, bear this out. Duran found Judaic customs in the old Aztec religion, unleavened bread on certain days and bathing for purification, and came to believe the Indians descended from the lost tribes of Israel. In 1644 an Indian guide named Francisco declared that his countrymen would be avenged upon the Spaniards in time by means of a people now hidden. Montesinos, a Judaizer imprisoned by the Inquisition, was reciting the formula of the New World Marranos, Blessed be the name of the Lord, who has not made me an idolater, a barbarian, a negro, an Indian, when he stopped and told himself, Those Indians, they are Hebrews. Indians later came to Antonio de Montesinos and recited the Shema in Hebrew, Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one, and told him they were of the tribe of Reuben, and that the tribe of Joseph lived on an island nearby. That is Puerto Rico, with Manasseh in Cuba.

That people now hidden is Judah, and the Psalm uses the same words the record used: “They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.” Israel is God's hidden people, and the nations have taken crafty counsel against them. The Spaniards' records, which they collected and kept, testify of the hidden ones the Bible speaks of.

precepts.label: Daniel 7:27
precepts.why:
The records of the Spanish explorers tell what the Indians' own sorcerers had said: that the God of these children of Israel is the true God, that everything inscribed on their tablets is true, that at the end of days they will be lords of all the nations of the earth, and that after one nation comes bringing many things to that land, these children of Israel will go forth from where they are and reign over the whole earth as they once did. That is what the nations don't want.

Daniel says the very same thing: “And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High, whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.” Under the whole heaven is the whole earth, exactly what the tablets said.

This is the blessing Jacob put on Joseph's head in Genesis 49. “The blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors”: what God promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob was not yet fulfilled in their day, Canaan was not yet theirs, but Joseph already ruled all Egypt. Joseph wore the crown before the kingdom came, a picture of the dominion that will be given to the saints in the last days.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 33:1
precepts.why:
“And this is the blessing, wherewith Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death.” Moses blessed the twelve tribes before he died, and his blessing of Joseph matches Jacob's in Genesis 49.

“And of Joseph he said, Blessed of the Lord be his land, for the precious things of heaven, for the dew, and for the deep that coucheth beneath.” That is Jacob's “blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that lieth under”: good climate and good weather, and the fish and treasures beneath the waters. “And for the precious fruits brought forth by the sun, and for the precious things put forth by the moon”: there are things on Cuba and Puerto Rico that only come forth by the moon, like the coquí frog that comes out in the time of the moon.

“and for the good will of him that dwelt in the bush”: that is Christ, whose spirit was in the bush. “let the blessing come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the top of the head of him that was separated from his brethren,” just as Jacob said the blessings “shall be on the head of Joseph, and on the crown of the head of him that was separate from his brethren.”

“His glory is like the firstling of his bullock”: that is Ephraim. “and his horns are like the horns of unicorns,” meaning the rhinoceros: “with them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth: and they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.” That is very important. Ephraim and Manasseh were used instrumentally by God to push the ten tribes from the eastern hemisphere to the western hemisphere.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 13:40-45
precepts.why:
Ezra explains how Ephraim and Manasseh pushed the people “to the ends of the earth”: “Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.”

“But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt,” “That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.” “And they entered into Euphrates by the narrow places of the river.” “For the most High then shewed signs for them, and held still the flood, till they were passed over.”

“For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half: and the same region is called Arsareth.” It took a year and a half to travel, and that region called Arsareth is the land now called America. That is how Joseph became the fruitful bough by a well in the western hemisphere, whose branches run over the wall.

precepts.label: Hosea 11:10
precepts.why:
“They shall walk after the Lord: he shall roar like a lion: when he shall roar, then the children shall tremble from the west.” The children of Israel are in the west when the Lord roars.

How did they get to the west? Deuteronomy 33:17 and 2 Esdras 13 just told you. Ephraim and Manasseh, with the horns of the unicorn, pushed the people together to the ends of the earth, and the ten tribes went a year and a half's journey into the region called Arsareth.

So the blessing of Joseph in Genesis 49, “in the last days,” is a blessing on a people in the western hemisphere, by the waters, on the islands. It is from the west that the children will tremble and come when the Lord roars.

precepts.label: Hosea 7:8-9
precepts.why:
“Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people; Ephraim is a cake not turned.” Some like to say that is not talking about mixing with other races. It is, and 1 Esdras 8:70 is the precept for it.

Ephraim today is like that: some are very light, extremely light, some able to pass for Esau, because they mixed with Esau; others who did not mix are very dark.

“Strangers have devoured his strength, and he knoweth it not”: the white man has devoured Ephraim's strength, and Ephraim does not realize it. “yea, gray hairs are here and there upon him, yet he knoweth not”: Ephraim grows old and does not know his own history. The fruitful bough of Genesis 49, blessed above his brethren, has been mixed and devoured and has forgotten who he is.

precepts.label: 1 Esdras 8:70
precepts.why:
To prove that Hosea's “Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people” speaks of intermarriage, Ezra gives the precept: “For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land; and from the beginning of this matter the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquity.”

The holy seed is mixed: that is the word. Israel married the daughters of the strange people of the land, and the scripture calls it iniquity. There is the precept for the mixing.

So when Hosea says Ephraim is “a cake not turned,” it is describing what that mixing produced: part of Ephraim very light from mixing with Esau, and part very dark because they did not mix.

precepts.label: Hosea 9:3
precepts.why:
“They shall not dwell in the Lord’s land; but Ephraim shall return to Egypt, and they shall eat unclean things in Assyria.”

Ephraim shall return to Egypt: that is the spiritual Egypt of Revelation 11:8, “the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt.” The Joseph who once ruled Egypt has returned to Egypt again, this time in captivity, in the western hemisphere.

And there they eat unclean things. Just like Ephraim, so all the tribes, as Ezekiel 4:13 shows. The same captivity and the same defiled bread fall on the whole house of Israel among the nations.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 4:13
precepts.why:
Hosea said Ephraim “shall eat unclean things in Assyria,” and Ezekiel shows it is not Ephraim alone: “And the Lord said, Even thus shall the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, whither I will drive them.”

Just like Ephraim, so all the tribes. Wherever God drove the children of Israel among the Gentiles, they would eat defiled bread there. That is the condition of the twelve tribes scattered in the lands of their captivity today, the spiritual Egypt.

precepts.label: Hosea 9:11-16
precepts.why:
“As for Ephraim, their glory shall fly away like a bird, from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception.” “Though they bring up their children, yet will I bereave them.”

“Ephraim, as I saw Tyrus, is planted in a pleasant place”: that pleasant place is what Moses and Jacob spoke of, the islands, the fruitful bough by a well. “but Ephraim shall bring forth his children to the murderer.” Ephraim would willingly give their children over to improve the race, as the doctrine of la raza taught: wanting children with straight hair, light skin and lighter eyes, not the nappy hair. That is what the Bible said Ephraim would do.

“Give them, O Lord: what wilt thou give? give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.” God says he will deal himself with the seed of the oppressor mixed in; so don't worry about it, brothers, just teach. “Ephraim is smitten, their root is dried up, they shall bear no fruit: yea, though they bring forth, yet will I slay even the beloved fruit of their womb.”

Joseph was blessed with “blessings of the breasts, and of the womb.” When Ephraim mixed with the murderer, that same blessing was turned: a miscarrying womb and dry breasts. The root of the fruitful bough is dried up because of the mixing.

precepts.label: Romans 8:28
precepts.why:
When Jacob died, Joseph's brethren were afraid: “Joseph will peradventure hate us, and will certainly requite us all the evil which we did unto him.” They sent a messenger begging forgiveness, “And Joseph wept when they spake unto him.” Then he said, “Fear not: for am I in the place of God?” “But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.”

Only a spiritual man can understand that. Joseph was on another level of understanding. He sat back and reflected on everything that happened to him, the pit, the slavery, the lie, the dungeon, and knew it was God's divine plan. He may not have understood it while he was in the midst of it, but going through the seven years of plenty and the seven years of famine he realized his purpose. God set that whole thing up.

Paul gives the precept: “And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.” We all go through things we don't understand while we are going through them, asking why God is doing this to me and nobody else. There is a purpose.

All things means all things: poverty, health problems, eviction, trials, tribulations, temptations, whatever it is. If you love God, you must endure it to the end, as Joseph did, and it will work together for good.

precepts.label: Job 42:10-15
precepts.why:
Endure to the end, and God shall restore everything. Job is the proof: “And the Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.”

His brethren and sisters and old acquaintances came and ate bread with him, “and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the Lord had brought upon him.” “So the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.” He had seven sons and three daughters, Jemima, Kezia and Keren-happuch, “And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job.”

Joseph's life ran the same way: sold, slandered, imprisoned, and then made ruler over Egypt, with his brethren falling down before his face. The latter end was greater than the beginning. Whatever you are suffering, endure it; God turns the captivity of those who hold on, and blesses their latter end more than their beginning.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 2:7-11
precepts.why:
Sirach speaks to those in the middle of the trial: “Ye that fear the Lord, wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest ye fall.” Don't go aside; don't say, I want to leave this truth and do something else. If you do, you will fall.

“Ye that fear the Lord, believe him; and your reward shall not fail.” “Ye that fear the Lord, hope for good, and for everlasting joy and mercy.”

“Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in the Lord, and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken?” Was Job confounded? No. Was Joseph forsaken? No; what his brethren meant for evil, God meant for good. “For the Lord is full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering, and very pitiful, and forgiveth sins, and saveth in time of affliction.”

That is the close of Joseph's story: wait on the Lord, go not aside, and he saves in the time of affliction.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:43-44
precepts.why:
Exodus 1:11 says “they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens.” Deuteronomy 28 names that as a curse: “The stranger that is within thee shall get up above thee very high; and thou shalt come down very low. He shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him: he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail.”

The strangers are the people that were amongst us. They get above us very high, and we come down very low. To be above us means they rule and tell us what to do, and another name for that is taskmaster.

That curse was on us in ancient Egypt: the Egyptians were over us, and we were on the bottom of society. It is the same way the so-called white man and the nations are above us today, and we are the bottom of society. The taskmasters today are the governors, the politicians, the police officers, the FBI agents, people set to keep us in check and keep us in order, with laws like Jim Crow and the black codes to keep us low. On the cotton field there was always a white overseer to make sure we did the work, or you got your ass whooped. Today your taskmaster is your boss.

What was done to us in ancient Egypt is what was done to us in America. That is why this place is spiritually called Egypt.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:30
precepts.why:
“And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.” We built cities in ancient Egypt, and it is the same thing here in America. Deuteronomy 28:30 lists it among the curses: “Thou shalt betroth a wife, and another man shall lie with her: thou shalt build an house, and thou shalt not dwell therein: thou shalt plant a vineyard, and shalt not gather the grapes thereof.”

In ancient Egypt we built cities and houses, and we did not build them for ourselves; we built them for the Egyptians. We were a commodity, and they did not look at us as human. America did the same.

What house did we build here in America and could not dwell in it? The White House. Construction began in 1792 in Washington D.C., and hundreds of enslaved people rented from plantation owners quarried the stone, cut the timber and laid the bricks, dawn to dusk, with no wages, whipped if they slowed down. Most are not even named in the records, just negro hired. When it was finished in 1800 and President Adams moved in, the enslaved workers were sent back to the plantations with no credit and no freedom, and for the next 65 years more enslaved people worked there. Some of you thought the white man built that.

We built cities in Egypt and did not dwell in them, and we built the White House and cannot dwell in it. The same curse, in ancient Egypt and in spiritual Egypt.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:16
precepts.why:
Exodus 1:14 says “they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field”. We were in the fields in ancient Egypt; we were not just building pyramids. They had us doing plantation work and cropping there too. Deuteronomy 28:16 is that curse: “Cursed shalt thou be in the city, and cursed shalt thou be in the field.”

The same way ancient Egypt made us slaves and worked us in the fields with all manner of service, in America that curse also fell upon us. We were cursed in the cotton field, in the sugar cane field, in the tobacco field, with five year olds and two year olds picking cotton. Our lives were made bitter, and that is why we eat the bitter herbs at Passover: they represent our lives being bitter in Egypt.

And all manner of service: we were their servants, cooking their food, watching their kids, entertaining them. Sing, this Hebrew got a good voice, sing me one of the songs of Zion. That is what we do here in Babylon. Some of you drive a bus, fix the road, drive a taxi cab: servant jobs, and you don't see it. We have been slaves so long we got comfortable with the jobs they give us. We are kings and priests; we are not supposed to serve any nation. Our job is to serve God.

Read the curses of Deuteronomy 28 and then read what happened to us in ancient Egypt, and you will see they are the same. America is spiritual Egypt.

precepts.label: Leviticus 26:17
precepts.why:
Exodus 1:12 says “the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.” No matter how much they afflicted us, we kept multiplying and growing. And what does it mean that the Egyptians were grieved because of us? They were mad; they were angry.

Leviticus 26:17 explains it: “And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you.” To be grieved because of the children of Israel means they hated us, and they that hated us reigned over us.

The same way the ancient Egyptians hated us, the so-called white man hated us when we were brought here as slaves. So “the Egyptians made the children of Israel to serve with rigour”: they did not play with us. In ancient Egypt they beat the hell out of us with whips, and in America the same: runaways caught and whooped, lynchings, and still lynching us. Not only America but all the lands we were scattered into are Egypt, but this is the main one, Mystery Babylon.

Pharaoh told the Hebrew midwives, “if it be a son, then ye shall kill him”. Where is that in Deuteronomy? “Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body, and the fruit of thy land”. What is the fruit of our body? Our children. That is why it says our children are going to be cursed.

precepts.label: Exodus 1:8
precepts.why:
“Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph”. This new king set taskmasters over Israel to afflict them with burdens, and then went further: “And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive”.

That is gator bait. They sacrificed our baby boys in the river to Sobek, the gator god. The white man did the exact same thing to us in the Florida Everglades: put our babies in a net, wait for the alligator to bite, pull the gator out and make shoes and bags out of him. Egypt did it to us first. They killed the males and kept the women alive, because the women do not produce the nation; the man does.

That decree is why Moses was hidden three months and laid in an ark of bulrushes by the river's brink, and why everything that follows was done in secret. When Pharaoh's daughter came down to the river in Exodus 2:5 and found the ark, she found one of the very sons her father had ordered cast into the river.

precepts.label: Numbers 12:1
precepts.why:
When Pharaoh's daughter opened the ark, “she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children”. How did she know? He was circumcised. You never read about Moses getting circumcised; he was already cut, because some of our forefathers retained that custom from our fathers. Outside of that, she would not have known the difference, because Egyptians and Hebrews were both black.

Then Moses fled to Midian and helped the seven daughters of the priest of Midian at the well, and they told their father Reuel, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds”. What did they call Moses? An Egyptian. The same way Joseph's brothers took Joseph for an Egyptian. Reuel, Jethro, gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.

Numbers 12:1 shows what that family was: “And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman”. She was Ethiopian, so Moses' father-in-law was an Ethiopian, a priest of Midian but not a Midianite. Ethiopians are children of Ham, Kushites, the family of the Egyptians. A Hamite would know a Hamite when he saw one, and they still took Moses for an Egyptian. If he had been a white man, they would have known he was no Egyptian.

Paul passed for one too: “Art not thou that Egyptian”, the chief captain asked, and Paul answered, “I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus”. Moses passed for an Egyptian, Joseph passed for an Egyptian, Paul passed for an Egyptian. These are black people. That's the point.

precepts.label: Exodus 13:3
precepts.why:
In Egypt the Lord told Moses and Aaron, “This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you”. Jump to verse 11 to see what holiday comes in that month: “ye shall eat it in haste: it is the Lord’s passover”. So Passover comes in the first month. But what is the name of that first month?

Exodus 13 tells us: “And Moses said unto the people, Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place: there shall no leavened bread be eaten. This day came ye out in the month Abib”.

Abib, or Aviv, means spring: the season when the young, tender barley ears first appear. It marks the start of the year, the time of Passover and the firstfruits, renewal and freedom from Egypt. So the first month, the month of Passover, is the spring month. Not January.

That matters, because the months of the year are all from Rome. January is named for Janus, the Roman god of beginnings, and America, exercising all the power of the first beast, has the whole earth keeping Rome's new year. The Most High set the beginning of months in the spring, the month we came out of the house of bondage.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 16:1
precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 16:1 is where Moses names the month again with the Passover. It joins the Passover and the month of Abib together, the same as Exodus 13, which says of the night we came out of Egypt, “This day came ye out in the month Abib”. The first month of Exodus 12:2, “the beginning of months”, is Abib, the spring month when the tender barley ears appear.

So the biblical new year does not begin in January. It begins in the spring, at Abib, and each month begins with the moon. January is from the Roman god Janus, who presided over doorways, time and new years.

Who changed it? Daniel 7:25 says the beast “shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws”. The great words are the lies Rome spoke against the Most High: a white man who died for the sins of everybody on the planet, that you must be dumped in the water to be saved, Lent, Christmas and December 25th. Wearing out the saints is the slavery. And changing times and laws is moving the beginning of the year from spring to January, and even daylight saving time. Keeping Abib is coming back to the Most High's times.

precepts.why:
Exodus 23 gives the seventh year release: work the land six years, “But the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still; that the poor of thy people may eat”. Leviticus 25 lays out the same law: “And the Lord spake unto Moses in mount Sinai, saying, Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye come into the land which I give you, then shall the land keep a sabbath unto the Lord”. He is telling us what to do when we enter the land, and we entered the land under Joshua, not under Moses.

“Six years thou shalt sow thy field, and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard, and gather in the fruit thereof; But in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land”. Don't farm the land that year. “That which groweth of its own accord of thy harvest thou shalt not reap”: whatever grows on its own during the seventh year, that is what you eat. “And the sabbath of the land shall be meat for you; for thee, and for thy servant, and for thy maid, and for thy hired servant, and for thy stranger that sojourneth with thee”.

The seventh year release is built on the seventh-day Sabbath. Exodus 23 says it right after the land: “Six days thou shalt do thy work, and on the seventh day thou shalt rest”. The Sabbath goes for the land as well; when you have property, you let your land rest.

And the question everybody asks is answered in verse 20: “What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase: Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years”. The sixth year covers you for three years. Brothers and sisters say, I got to work on the Sabbath because that's my money day. Then you don't believe what we just read. That was the same question in verse 20, and God answered it: work six, rest on the seventh, and he provides.
