precepts.label: Leviticus 25:23
precepts.why:
The whole Jubilee rests on this: “The land shall not be sold for ever: for the land is mine; for ye are strangers and sojourners with me.” Israel could sell the use of a field, but never the field itself, because the land belongs to the Most High. He is the owner, and he decides its proper use. That is why nobody in Israel was to heap up land for himself: it never really belonged to them.

That is also why the price of land was worked by the harvests left until the Jubilee. “According to the multitude of years thou shalt increase the price thereof, and according to the fewness of years thou shalt diminish the price of it: for according to the number of the years of the fruits doth he sell unto thee.” More years means more crops, so a higher price; one year left means one harvest, so the price has to be less. What was bought was the crops, not the land. And in the middle of it: “Ye shall not therefore oppress one another; but thou shalt fear thy God”.

Look at how black people chip each other and undercut each other today. That is why we have to come back to the Bible and apply these basic principles. When our own try to oppress one another in business, our people go to the Chinese man instead. God says don't oppress one another.

The Most High even provided for the year they could not farm. “What shall we eat the seventh year?” “Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years.” That answers everyone who says they have to break the Sabbath to make their money. It is connected to the seventh-day Sabbath, where what was needed was baked beforehand and laid up for the seventh; here it is the sixth year he increases. It is all spiritual.

Read on: “And in all the land of your possession ye shall grant a redemption for the land.” If a brother waxed poor and sold some of his possession, a kinsman could come and redeem what he had to sell away. If none could, and he later had the means himself, he counted the years and restored the overplus, the extra. And if he could not, the land stayed in the hand of the buyer only “until the year of jubile”, and then he returned to his possession, money or no money. Every fifty years it all goes back.

There is a spirit in the land. The woman who came to Esdras was Jerusalem, and the Most High wanted us to see that there is a connection between the people and the land. So when the trumpet sounds on the Day of Atonement in the fiftieth year and liberty is proclaimed, every man returns to his possession and his family, because the land was never anybody's to keep but the Lord's.

precepts.label: Leviticus 25:44
precepts.why:
After the law for a poor brother comes the distinction: “Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids.” Your bondmen and bondmaids shall be of the heathen, the other nations. A bondservant is like chattel slavery, and that is what Israel was never to make of a brother.

Keep reading: “Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are with you, which they begat in your land: and they shall be your possession.” Now the word stranger is talking about the heathen, as the verse above explained. “And ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever”. For how long? For ever. They got passed down from generation to generation, to your son and your daughter. The other nations were not released in the Jubilee; they remained slaves. That is what God said.

Then the stress on but: “but over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour.” There is the distinction. Your brother who waxes poor and is sold to you serves “as an hired servant, and as a sojourner”, what we call a job today; back then they called you a servant. He serves until the Jubilee, and then “shall he depart from thee, both he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family”. “For they are my servants, which I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen.” “Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour; but shalt fear thy God.” Rigour is hardship: busting him in the head, whooping him. Don't do that.

The word stranger in this chapter does not always mean another race. The stranger of verse 35, “though he be a stranger, or a sojourner”, is a brother of another tribe, like Judah living in the land of Simeon, a stranger there. Numbers 16:40 shows it: “no stranger, which is not of the seed of Aaron, come near to offer incense before the Lord”. Anyone not of the seed of Aaron, Judah, Benjamin, Manasseh, Ephraim, Gad, Reuben, was called a stranger. But in verses 44 and 45 the stranger is the heathen round about.

So the Jubilee's liberty was for Israel. The poor brother went free; the bondmen of the heathen did not. “For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt”. Verse 55 tells you plain: the Israelites are God's servants. Everybody on the planet is not God's servants.

precepts.label: Leviticus 25:48
precepts.why:
When a brother waxed poor and sold himself to a sojourner or stranger, it was not the end of him: “After that he is sold he may be redeemed again; one of his brethren may redeem him”. This is not saying we sold ourselves to the other nations. It is another tribe. A man of Judah whose land is jacked up goes among the tribe of Gad and says, I'm poor, I need to work for you, help me. Esau will use this chapter and try to cause confusion with that word stranger, saying see, the other nations. No. That is about Israel.

“Either his uncle, or his uncle’s son, may redeem him, or any that is nigh of kin unto him of his family may redeem him; or if he be able, he may redeem himself.” A kinsman could buy him back, and if he came into some money while he was working, he could say, I don't need this anymore, and redeem himself.

The price was reckoned the same way as the land: “from the year that he was sold to him unto the year of jubile: and the price of his sale shall be according unto the number of years, according to the time of an hired servant shall it be with him.” The price is according to the years left from now to the Jubilee. “If there be yet many years behind”, the price of his redemption is higher; “if there remain but few years unto the year of jubile”, it is lower. It is the same concept as the land.

“And as a yearly hired servant shall he be with him: and the other shall not rule with rigour over him in thy sight.” That goes back to verse 43. “And if he be not redeemed in these years, then he shall go out in the year of jubile, both he, and his children with him.” That goes back to verse 41.

Why? “For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.” A poor brother of Israel is never a bondservant for ever. He is the Lord's servant, he can always be redeemed, and in the Jubilee he goes free with his children.

precepts.label: Psalms 2:8-10

Leviticus 25:46 says of the heathen bondmen, “ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you”. Hold that, and hear Psalm 2: “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.”

The Lord is saying, don’t worry, it is going back to that. He is going to give us the heathen for our inheritance. Meaning what? We are going to own them. That is what it is saying right there. We were their possession, but they were originally our possession; we sinned against our God and became theirs, and it is going to go back to the way it is supposed to be.

“Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.” If they don’t want to get right, boom, upside the head. “Be wise now therefore, O ye kings: be instructed, ye judges of the earth.”

So the inheritance of Leviticus 25:46 and the inheritance of Psalm 2:8 are the same: the heathen given to Israel for an inheritance and a possession, ruled with a rod of iron.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 3:14
precepts.why:
Leviticus 25:46 says “they shall be your bondmen for ever”. For how long? Forever. Esau thinks he can change his judgment. No. No. You cannot change it. God said it, it is in writing, it is stamped. So that means you are going back into slavery.

“I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth it, that men should fear before him.” Whatever God does is forever. Nothing can be put to it to change it, nor anything taken from it. There it is: that men should fear before him.

Isaiah shows it coming to pass: “the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.” For servants and handmaids, because that is the role the Lord gave them, and for how long? Forever. The judgment of Leviticus 25:44-46 cannot be undone.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:48
precepts.why:
In the wilderness the children of Israel wept and said, “We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick”. What are they saying? Deuteronomy 28:48 explains it.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things: and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” Serving our enemies in hunger and in thirst is one of the curses that was upon us, and it was also a curse that was on us in ancient Egypt. We had to serve the Egyptians for the want of all things. It is the same today: you need money to buy food, and you have to serve for it.

Back then we had fish, because the Nile was abundant in fish, and we had melons. So brothers got delivered from oppression and started talking about going back to Egypt: even though we were oppressed, at least there we had some good food. It is the same thing with us here in America. A lot of you have food, you are full, you are comfortable. Well, for now.

precepts.label: Leviticus 18:3
precepts.why:
It was not just that the Egyptians fed us. Everything we learned, we learned from the Egyptians back then. So when we came out of Egypt, God said: “After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do: and after the doings of the land of Canaan, whither I bring you, shall ye not do”.

Why did God say not to do after the doings of Egypt? Because we learned the Egyptian customs while we were there, the Egyptian names of the week. It is the same way here in America: you talk about Monday and Tuesday and all of that, days named after their gods, and all that is idolatry.

So God says, everything you learned in Egypt, forget it. The people who longed for the fish and the melons of Egypt were still holding on to Egypt in their hearts. And it is going to be the same thing when we are delivered up out of here, out of spiritual Egypt: everything we learned from this land, we will have to leave behind.

precepts.label: Acts 5:35-37
precepts.why:
Korah, Dathan, Abiram and On “took men”, “two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown”. They were not nobodies; they had a name, and what they had was influence over the congregation. They used it against Moses and Aaron: “Ye take too much upon you”. And the results of those leaders: the earth “swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods”, and fire from the Lord “consumed the two hundred and fifty men that offered incense.” Everyone who followed them went down with them.

These things were written aforetime for our learning, and Acts 5 shows the same lesson. The apostles were brought before the council, and Gamaliel stood up and warned them: “Ye men of Israel, take heed to yourselves what ye intend to do as touching these men.” Then he gave examples.

“For before these days rose up Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody; to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves”. Four hundred men joined themselves to a man who came across as a leader, and he “was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to nought.” Then “rose up Judas of Galilee in the days of the taxing, and drew away much people after him: he also perished; and all, even as many as obeyed him, were dispersed.”

That is the pattern with false leaders: the leader perishes, and the ones that obeyed him perish and are scattered with him, just like the men that appertained unto Korah. “For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.” The leaders of the black community today, the Christian pastors, have our people living in hell, with drugs, gang violence, shootings on the block and adultery, and those that follow them are destroyed with them.

precepts.label: Tobit 4:12
precepts.why:
Numbers 36 is the law for the brother who had no sons. The chief fathers of Gilead, of the tribe of Manasseh, came before Moses because the inheritance of Zelophehad was given to his daughters, and “if they be married to any of the sons of the other tribes of the children of Israel, then shall their inheritance be taken from the inheritance of our fathers”. The inheritance goes to her husband. Not even the jubile would bring it back: “so shall their inheritance be taken away from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers.” You are Manasseh, you marry into Judah, and Judah owns that land forever.

So the Lord commanded, “only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry”, “that the children of Israel may enjoy every man the inheritance of his fathers.” That is the law right there: if you have all daughters and you have land and property, they marry within the tribe so another tribe of Israel does not take possession of it forever.

That is what Tobit was making reference to. Brothers often ask, because Judah married outside the tribe of Judah and Ephraim married outside the tribe of Ephraim. But there was a special clause when it came to property and land, and the woman was not allowed to do that.

Tobit tells his son, “chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe”. See that: not of thy father’s tribe. “for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob”, and “our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.” Shall inherit the land: that is the point. Marrying your own kindred is how the inheritance of the fathers stays with their seed.

Tobit keeps going, and it is for anybody here looking at a Chinese lady: “love thy brethren, and despise not in thy heart thy brethren, the sons and daughters of thy people, in not taking a wife of them: for in pride is destruction and much trouble”. “and in lewdness is decay and great want: for lewdness is the mother of famine.” You will lose everything, and you see it all in the news. Janet Jackson married an Arab and ran out of there with the baby, under an agreement not to speak on what she saw. Shannon Sharpe lost millions and millions of dollars over a twenty-year-old white girl from the gym.

That is lewdness being the mother of famine, decay and great want. The Bible is a true book. The law of Numbers 36 kept the inheritance in the tribe of the fathers, and Tobit shows the curse on those who despise their own people and take a strange woman.

precepts.label: Genesis 15:18
precepts.why:
Before Genesis, Deuteronomy 11 was read from verse 21, the word the Lord gave Israel in advance of entering the land: “That your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children, in the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.” For us, heaven has always been upon the earth. If Israel would diligently keep the commandments, “Then will the Lord drive out all these nations from before you, and ye shall possess greater nations and mightier than yourselves.” To possess means to own. Then: “Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours”. Every place your feet touch is your land; that is heaven on earth.

With a map on the screen, verse 24 lays out the borders. “From the wilderness” is the wilderness of Egypt, on the other side of the Nile. “And Lebanon” sits at the top of the map, and Lebanon was ours. “from the river, the river Euphrates” runs through Syria, just above Lebanon. “even unto the uttermost sea” is the Mediterranean on the left. So the land ran from the wilderness of Egypt all the way up to the Euphrates, taking in Syria and everything down from it.

Genesis 15:18 goes with Deuteronomy 11:21-24. “In the same day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, Unto thy seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Euphrates”. The river of Egypt is the Nile. The same land God promised Abraham is the land Israel took. We were fighting from the time of Joshua to get all of it, and we fully had it under David and Solomon.

This matters for Jubilee. Jubilee did not start until Israel got into the land: count seven times seven years, forty-nine, and the fiftieth year is the jubilee, when the land rests and every piece of land goes back to the original owner of that heritage, that tribe. So the land has borders, and they are in the Middle East. The doctrines going around that the Congo, or Kenya, is the real Israel cannot stand. What are y'all talking about? It gives you the land layout right here. The hell is this?

From there Isaiah 14 shows the land coming back: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land”. He is not having mercy on everybody, only Jacob. We may be at the bottom of society, but he will yet choose Israel, and it is God who sets us in the land, not the League of Nations or the United Nations. “And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place”: every nation goes back to the land God first gave it, and “the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids”. The laws of Leviticus 25 cannot be in effect now while we are the slaves in a foreign land, but when we return to the land they go back into full effect.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 31:10
precepts.why:
“At the end of every seven years, in the solemnity of the year of release, in the feast of tabernacles”. Moses ties the year of release to a set time: every seventh year, in the feast of tabernacles. In that solemnity the land was released, the servants were released, and the debt was released.

It comes right after the Sabbath of the land in Leviticus 25. When the people ask, “What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase”, God answers, “Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years.” Think about that with the seventh day Sabbath. Deuteronomy 28:68 says “the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships, by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again”. Moses is being very specific, and Exodus 14:13 explains it. At the Red Sea he told the people: “Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.”

The scripture already said we would never see those Egyptians again, for ever. So when Moses says we will go into Egypt a second time, the Egypt he is speaking of cannot be ancient Egypt. The people would have said, Egypt again? We are going back to Egypt a second time? And he explains: I am not talking about the Egypt you just came out of. The way whereof I speak unto thee, thou shalt see it no more again. It is a different Egypt.

And this time we go into it with ships. Moses saw the end. The Lord showed him the Israelites thrown on cargo slave ships and brought here to America: the transatlantic slave trade. Egypt, from the Hebrew Mizraim, means shut in, restraint, misery, tribulation, distress. So going into Egypt again means going into captivity, misery and tribulation again, carried there on ships, sold to our enemies for bondmen and bondwomen. That is why Revelation 11:8 calls the great city, Mystery Babylon, America, spiritually Egypt.

precepts.label: Psalms 137:3
precepts.why:
“For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion.” “How shall we sing the Lord’s song in a strange land?” We read it right there in the history of the slave ships.

Deuteronomy 28:68 says “the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”. What does Egypt represent? “I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.” Egypt is bondage. The Lord would bring us into bondage again, this time by way of ships; literal Egypt we would see no more again as a nation, and there we would be sold to our enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, slave men and slave women.

The Middle Passage, the Maafa, a massive disaster: for fifty days or more our people were packed in spaces as tight as coffins, a second platform barely twenty inches above the heads of those below, chained to the floor, lying in their own waste, amid rats that gnawed through wood and flesh, on floors covered with blood and excrement, where pregnant women gave birth and the living awoke chained to the dead. Tight packers crammed in as many as possible, reckoning the sales would offset the dead. The meal was horse beans pounded to a pulp with slabber sauce, once or twice a day, and a pint of water. Dumb negroes say it never happened and ask where the ships are: cargo ships carried spices and corn before us, carried us as cargo, and after slavery carried cargo again. Why get rid of them?

Then came the dancing of the slaves: the crew played the bagpipe or forced our ancestors to beat out a rhythm while they jumped about, ankles rubbed raw by the leg irons, to keep the human cargo in salable condition. That is Psalms 137:3: those who carried us away captive required of us mirth. At night the cries rose; an enslaved woman explained the howling came from having dreamt they were in their own country and waking in the hold of a slave ship. A strange land indeed.

Millions were carried from Africa to the West Indies, North and South America and Europe, from Luanda, from the Congo, from Loango, where the old maps mark the Jews; the buyers and sellers both knew they were selling outsiders, not the same people. Deuteronomy 28:68 and Psalms 137:3 were fulfilled on those ships.

precepts.label: Isaiah 66:22-24
precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 29:22 speaks of “the generation to come of your children that shall rise up after you”. Who is that? Isaiah 66 shows it: “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the Lord, so shall your seed and your name remain.” The seed and the name that remain in the new heaven and new earth are the righteous of our people that make it, those of us that get the kingdom.

“And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord.” After they come up to worship, “they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me”. Go forth where? To look on this place, America. That is the same moment Deuteronomy 29 describes, when the generation to come and the stranger from a far land see the plagues of that land, “brimstone, and salt, and burning”, and ask, “Wherefore hath the Lord done thus unto this land?”

After somebody dies, their carcase is supposed to just disappear. So this is letting you know it is something spiritual. “for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.” They are in damnation, cast in hell, being tormented. That is why Deuteronomy 29 says the Lord will separate the man that did not repent unto evil.

There is a place of torment, and it will be set up when Christ returns. After this place is destroyed physically, a spiritual prison and damnation will be set up here, the place of torment for the devils that said, have you come to torment us before our time. Christ has the power over hell and death: he can give you life and immortality, or wake you up and torment you.

precepts.label: Daniel 12:2
precepts.why:
Christ has the power over life and death, which is why Daniel 12 says some shall awake. “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

Many of them are going to awake. Some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. When you die, you go to sleep, yes. But Christ has the power to wake your behind up and torment you.

That is what stands behind the carcases of Isaiah 66:24, whose worm does not die and whose fire is not quenched, and behind the land of Deuteronomy 29 that is all brimstone, salt and burning. Those who forsook the covenant of the Lord God of their fathers and served other gods do not simply die and disappear: they are awakened to shame and everlasting contempt. As 2 Esdras 9 says, read in the same moment, those who despised his law while the place of repentance was open “must know it after death by pain.” And the righteous awake to everlasting life, the seed and the name that remain.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 4:26-27
precepts.why:
In Deuteronomy 31 Moses says, “For I know that after my death ye will utterly corrupt yourselves”, and “evil will befall you in the latter days”. How is Moses able to say I know? Deuteronomy 4 shows what he saw.

“I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land whereunto ye go over Jordan to possess it; ye shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall utterly be destroyed.” When we went into the land of Israel, our days were not going to be prolonged in it; we were going to be destroyed from off that land. “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.” Moses saw the Israelites being scattered throughout the four corners of the earth.

He could see it because God showed it to him. In 2 Esdras 14, read right after, the Lord says, “In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt”, and he held him on the mount a long season, the forty days and forty nights, and “shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”. Moses saw the secrets of the beginning, which is how he wrote Genesis, and he saw the end.

So Moses saw what would happen to us in the time of the Babylonians, the Greeks and the Romans, and he saw us here in America, in the transatlantic slave trade, and America being destroyed. That is why he could say with certainty that evil would befall us in the latter days: he had already seen it.

precepts.why:
“Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people”. There is Judah in Africa too, but this is speaking of Judah on this side of the earth, in the Western Hemisphere, specifically in the United States of America. Judah in North America is under Esau, who controls the world right now, and with an American passport you can go anywhere in the world. “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first”. God is going to raise up the tribe of Judah first, Judah in America. Then, when it says bring him unto his people, it means Judah will know where God's people are and will go find them. Wherever our people are in Africa, in Japan, in Iran, in India, scattered throughout the four corners of the earth, Judah will be able to identify them, find them, and teach them what God commanded of them.

That is why Genesis 49 speaks mainly of Israel on this side of the world: Judah needed to know who they were first. And it is already happening. precepts.label: Judges 21:25
precepts.why:
Naomi told Ruth, “Behold, thy sister in law is gone back unto her people, and unto her gods”. Orpah went back to Moab, to her people and her gods. These were not Israelite women; this was a heathen woman of another nation. That is important, because there are doctrines out there teaching that Ruth was an Israelite. No, she was not. She was a heathen. Was it right for Boaz to deal with a heathen? No, but it happened.

Just in case there is any confusion, the last verse of Judges, right above Ruth, shows why it happened: “In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.” During the judges, we did what we wanted to do.

And Ruth opens in that very time: “Now it came to pass in the days when the judges ruled”. There was no king. It was the time when Israel did what they wanted, and that included taking heathen women.

So Ruth's story does not make her an Israelite, and it does not make it right to take a heathen wife. It shows what Israel was doing when every man did what was right in his own eyes. The scripture keeps calling her what she is: “Ruth the Moabitess”. That is clear.

precepts.label: Zechariah 8:23
precepts.why:
Ruth said, “thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God”. She is a heathen saying, if I go with you, I will be as if I am an Israelite, and I will serve your God too. She is cleaving to an Israelite woman, that's all; there were no promises made to her. “Where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried”: I'm not leaving you.

The nations are going to be the same way in the kingdom. Zechariah shows it: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.”

We will go with you, just like Ruth said. For we have heard that God is with you: your God is a real God, and ours is garbage. They are going to cleave to Israel the way Ruth cleaved to Naomi, and they will cleave as servants.

So Ruth is the picture of the nations in the kingdom: not Israelites, but holding on to Israel because the God of Israel is the true God.

precepts.label: John 4:3-5
precepts.why:
Ruth 4 is a trial at the gate before ten elders over land. Elimelech had land; he died, and his two sons, Mahlon and Chilion, died too, leaving no man to take it. So the land had to be taken up by the next of kin. Boaz told the nearer kinsman that Naomi “selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s.” A parcel of land: that phrase opens the whole chapter.

John 4 uses the same wording. Christ “must needs go through Samaria. Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.” Jacob gave Joseph that parcel of ground; he bought his son that land.

A parcel of land, a parcel of ground, a parcel of a field: they are all the same thing, and a parcel of land and an inheritance are one and the same. So when Boaz bought the parcel that was Elimelech's, he was not making an ordinary purchase. He was taking up an inheritance in Israel, one that had to stay in the family of the dead.

precepts.label: Genesis 33:18-20
precepts.why:
Genesis 33 gives the history behind the “parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph” in John 4. “Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan–aram; and pitched his tent before the city. And he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for an hundred pieces of money.”

Jacob bought that land from the Hamites for a hundred pieces of money, and “he erected there an altar, and called it El–elohe–Israel.” A parcel of a field is again the same thing as a parcel of land: an inheritance.

Later, as he was dying, Israel told Joseph, “Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.” His sons did take the land by the sword; Simeon and Levi went crazy and killed the men of that city. But the field was bought first, before his sons ever took it. So the inheritance at Shechem stood on a lawful purchase, the same way Boaz bought Elimelech's parcel before the elders at the gate.

precepts.label: Joshua 24:32
precepts.why:
“And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver: and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.” The parcel of ground, the parcel of land, the parcel of a field is the land of inheritance, and this one was given to Ephraim.

That is what Boaz was protecting in Ruth 4. The nearer kinsman would not redeem it, “lest I mar mine own inheritance”, and plucked off his shoe; here the shoe is passed without shame, because he is yielding the right to someone else, not refusing his brother. Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and took Ruth, the wife of Mahlon, “to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren.” The son he raised up would inherit that land, because it belonged to Mahlon. Boaz is still the father; Boaz begat Obed, and the line goes through Boaz. There are no two fathers. The land falls under the dead man's line; the lineage goes back to Boaz. That is love your neighbor as yourself.

So Elimelech did not lose his land. We kept our land in house. Land is very important: if you have it, keep it and give it to your children; don't sell it off. Our people once had millions of acres in America, and Esau made laws, eminent domain among them, and found a distant kin to pay off with a little money, and so stole millions of acres, beaches included, from Judah.

The allotment still stands. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land, and Judges says “the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” Those families are here today. The Lord says he “will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” Whoever is left after the destruction, those who repent, will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 12:15
precepts.why:
“And Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed”. Boaz raised up seed in the name of Mahlon, but the record says Boaz begat Obed, not Mahlon, because Mahlon was dead. The genealogy goes under Boaz; the land falls under the dead man's line. Obed takes on the land of Elimelech even though that is not his father's line. That is the inheritance: the parcel of land, the parcel of field, the parcel of ground. You don't inherit a tribe; you inherit the land. And they were both of the same tribe anyway.

That is why the scripture says this in Jeremiah: “And it shall come to pass, after that I have plucked them out I will return, and have compassion on them, and will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” It literally means what it says. In the beginning God allotted every family land.

The line of David had an inheritance given to it; the families of Judah each had land appointed to them. Guess what? Those families are here today. When the Lord returns, those that make it, that repented, are going back to that land, every man to his heritage.

That is why Boaz raised up seed for Elimelech's family: so the land would stay within that family's inheritance. That is loving your neighbor as yourself. We kept our land in house. So land is very important: if you have it, keep it and give it to your kids; don't just sell it off. A lot of Judah had millions of acres here in America, and Esau stole them, creating laws like eminent domain and finding some distant kin to pay a little money and take the land. There are beaches that belong to us. But the Lord will bring every man again to his heritage and to his land.

precepts.label: Judges 2:6
precepts.why:
Judges shows how the land was first given: “And when Joshua had let the people go, the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” We all had land and an inheritance. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land. Whoever of those same families is left after the destruction takes place will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

Notice it says every man unto his inheritance. Sisters, you're divorcing us and taking half our stuff, but it says every man. Our wives benefit from our inheritance; it belongs to the men, but it is theirs too because they are married to us. According to God, the inheritance belongs to the men, just as the earth belonged to Adam, and Eve benefitted from it because she was helping him.

And the land we inherit is not an acre or something. 1 Chronicles 2 shows Jair “who had three and twenty cities in the land of Gilead”, “even threescore cities”. We owned cities. Somebody literally owned the Bronx, Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens. We had castles on those cities, winter houses and summer houses.

That is why the land in Ruth had to stay with Elimelech's family. Boaz begat Obed, and the genealogy goes through Boaz down to Jesse and David, but the inheritance, every man's portion from the time of Joshua, stayed with the dead man's line through the seed raised up to him.

precepts.label: Baruch 2:30
precepts.why:
Solomon prays, “Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives”. Bethink is not a common word we use today. Baruch clears it up easily: “For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.”

“For I knew that they would not hear me”: that is why he put us in captivity, because we are a stiffnecked people. He delivered us to the enemy, by ships, “unto the land of the enemy, far or near”. This land is the land of our enemy: our enemy conquered us and made this land his land. Far is here, far from Jerusalem; near is Africa or Madagascar, colonised just the same.

“but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.” In our captivity, in the land of our enemy, we shall remember ourselves. That is what bethink means: remember, call to mind. Solomon saw in the spirit our people put on the ships and scattered all over the world, yokes put upon our necks, and destroyed so much that we would turn our own eyes against our own people and attack them. He saw that we would lose ourselves and our identity, and try to seek others or recreate ourselves, instead of in the image of God.

So first we must remember ourselves. We can only say “We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness” if we know who we are. And once you learn who you are, you learn who the enemy is by default. As long as you don’t know who you are, you will make your own people from the continent or the Caribbean your enemy, while the white man gets a pass.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 1:17
precepts.why:
“And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel”. What happened? Solomon got old. He had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and he built houses of worship for their individual gods. They did not all serve the same god: Chemosh, Remphan, Ashtoreth of the Zidonians, Molech. Some of those gods required child sacrifice; some involved sexual orgies. And Israel had to pay taxes for those gods.

Solomon said it himself: “And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.” Madness and folly means all kind of sin. However your mind can go, Solomon went there. When Solomon got old, he did a lot of evil. And yes, he did repent, when you read Ecclesiastes 12.

So the Lord said, “I will surely rend the kingdom from thee”, but “Notwithstanding in thy days I will not do it for David thy father’s sake: but I will rend it out of the hand of thy son.” That is why Ahijah tore Jeroboam’s new garment into twelve pieces and told him to take ten: the northern kingdom, while one tribe was kept for David’s sake. That is the tabernacle of David that fell.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 30:4-6
precepts.why:
Rehoboam took his father’s throne. “Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead: for he hath left one behind him that is like himself.” When you die, your son should be in your image. “While he lived, he saw and rejoiced in him: and when he died, he was not sorrowful.”

“He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindness to his friends.” Your son is supposed to look after his father’s friends.

The old men who stood before Solomon were his father’s friends, and they counselled him: “If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.” “But he forsook the counsel of the old men”. And he was like his father in the worst way: Solomon in his old age forced the people to pay tribute to the houses of his wives’ gods, and Rehoboam said, “my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” I am going to be worse than my father.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 3:6
precepts.why:
Rehoboam “forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him”. Those are his peers. Notice the difference: to the old men he asked, “How do ye advise that I may answer this people?” To the young men, “What counsel give ye that we may answer this people”? We, all together: y’all are my peers, we are running this thing.

Paul warns about that kind of counsel: “Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.” A novice is a beginner, a newbie, a neophyte. Lifted up with pride: I know all the precepts. His head gets big because he thinks he knows it all. That is young men, and that type of spirit will destroy itself.

So that is who Rehoboam looked to, and the young men told him to say, “My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins.” Some of you in here make that same mistake.

precepts.label: 2 Kings 25:27-28
precepts.why:
Zedekiah rebelled like his brother and his nephew did. He tried to run away and got caught in the plains of Jericho, and they killed his kids in front of him first, then took his eyes out, bound him and locked him up in Babylon. At this point there are no more kings of Judah; Zedekiah was the last one. His sons are gone, his heirs are gone. So who's left?

Read on: “in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah”, “Evil–merodach king of Babylon in the year that he began to reign did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison; And he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon”. Jehoiachin had been locked up between 36 and 37 years. Then he “changed his prison garments: and he did eat bread continually before him all the days of his life.” His allowance was a continual allowance, a daily rate for every day: Babylon gave him a job and status.

Jehoiachin is Jeconiah, and he is the Jechonias of Matthew 1:11. He got some mercy in captivity, but was he a king anymore at this point? No. He was a king, but now he was a captive in Babylon, receiving wages and some status.

And in Babylon he had children: “the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son”. Salathiel is Shealtiel, the father of Zerubbabel, whose name means born in Babylon. That is where the line of the kings of Judah went on after Zedekiah's sons were slain: through a captive king in Babylon.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 4:31
precepts.why:
Judah had five sons: Er, Onan and Shelah by the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess, and the twins Pharez and Zerah by Tamar. “The sons of Pharez; Hezron, and Hamul. And the sons of Zerah; Zimri, and Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol, and Dara: five of them in all.” Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara became very famous. They were very wise.

How wise? Solomon’s wisdom is measured against them: “For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about.”

Those same sons of Judah were so wise that many men were named after them, and Solomon surpassed even them. He was wiser than the wise men of his own tribe.

That is the house this genealogy runs through. Hezron, the oldest son of Pharez, begat Ram, and from Ram comes Amminadab, Nahshon, Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: a tribe of wise men, princes and kings.

precepts.label: Numbers 2:3
precepts.why:
“And Ram begat Amminadab; and Amminadab begat Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah”. Nahshon was of the elite princes of Judah, a prince family, a royal family. The census confirms the same man: “Of Judah; Nahshon the son of Amminadab.”

And in the camp: “And on the east side toward the rising of the sun shall they of the standard of the camp of Judah pitch throughout their armies: and Nahshon the son of Amminadab shall be captain of the children of Judah.”

So Nahshon was a captain. These men had serious status: princes and captains, leaders. They were warriors; they were not regular men.

“And Nahshon begat Salma, and Salma begat Boaz, And Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse”. Boaz came from that line, the line of Pharez, the twin that breached, not the one whose hand came out first with the scarlet thread. And Jesse had eight sons, and one of those sons is David.

precepts.label: Exodus 6:23
precepts.why:
Now a tie-in regarding family ties: “And Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.”

Aaron is Moses’ brother, of Levi. He took Elisheba, Amminadab’s daughter and Nahshon’s sister, to wife. Aaron’s wife was of the tribe of Judah. Those families intermarried, priests and kings marrying together. It is no coincidence; that is why John the Baptist and Christ are cousins.

Nadab and Abihu were the two who offered strange fire and were killed; Eleazar and Ithamar were spared. Eleazar became the high priest in the days of Joshua, the mediator before the Lord. So Eleazar’s mama was Judah. That is why some Levites don’t have the big heads; their mama is Judah. And don’t forget the big nose, too.

So Amminadab begat Nahshon and a daughter Elisheba. Aaron married Elisheba and had the four sons, the high priests, which makes Nahshon Aaron’s brother-in-law. And from Nahshon came Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: the priesthood and the royal line of Judah bound together in one family.

precepts.label: Genesis 15:3-4
precepts.why:
Abram, childless, was going to leave his house to Eliezer of Damascus, the eldest servant born in his house: “Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: and, lo, one born in my house is mine heir.” The Lord said no: “This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir.” Not a heathen servant, but his own seed. An heir and an inheritance are the same word, like a family heirloom passed down the line.

That is the key to 1 Chronicles 2: “Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. And Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Jarha. And Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant to wife.” This was while Israel was in Egypt, when we had no land of inheritance allotted to us. People read it and say the Egyptian married into the tribe and became Judah. No.

The record follows that line for generation after generation so that it is known. When Israel came out of Egypt and inherited the land, that line could not receive land, because the land passes by the paternal bloodline and that line goes back to an Egyptian servant. They were among us in the land, but they did not inherit. It is written there to exclude, not to include. Sheshan's brothers had sons and received land; his line did not. It does not mean the Egyptian became a Jew. When we came back under the Persians and the Medes, a man who could not show from his father's house who he came from was given no inheritance, and a Levite could not serve in his office. Zerubbabel could show he came from King David's line.

The daughters of Zelophehad show the law when a man has only daughters. They asked, “Why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he hath no son?” The Lord said, “If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter”, then to his brother, then his father's brethren, then the next kinsman: the law Boaz was fulfilling. But those daughters had to marry “only to the family of the tribe of their father”, “So shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe.” The inheritance of Israel is paternal. There is no sin in marrying a woman of another tribe; Aaron did it. The command there was only to keep the land in the tribe. We have no land in captivity now, so marry within your nation and stay with your people.

precepts.label: 1 Chronicles 28:19
precepts.why:
David, chosen out of Judah and out of his father’s house, hands the building of the house to the son the Lord chose to sit on the throne: “Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.” “Moreover I will establish his kingdom for ever”. Solomon’s kingdom, not Solomon and his brethren’s. Then David charges him: “Take heed now; for the Lord hath chosen thee to build an house for the sanctuary: be strong, and do it.”

“Then David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch”. The blueprints to the temple: guess who gave them to Solomon? David. Solomon did not come up with the design; David came up with it, and Solomon fulfilled his father’s wishes. That porch is why the feast of dedication is kept at Solomon’s porch. It took Solomon seven years to build the temple and thirteen years to build his own house, so the temple was done before his house was finished.

David gave him the pattern “of the houses thereof, and of the treasuries thereof, and of the upper chambers thereof”, the floors and levels, “and of the inner parlours thereof, and of the place of the mercy seat”, the holy of holies. “And the pattern of all that he had by the spirit”: the spirit moved David to design the temple. The courses of the priests, which priest for burning incense and which for each service, David was behind all of that too. Gold by weight for the things of gold, “refined gold by weight” for the altar of incense, everything gold, “and gold for the pattern of the chariot of the cherubims, that spread out their wings, and covered the ark of the covenant of the Lord.”

“All this, said David, the Lord made me understand in writing by his hand upon me, even all the works of this pattern.” David did not write it off the top of his head. The Lord moved his hand on what to write, and David drew out the temple through his hands. So the house Solomon built on the throne of the kingdom of the Lord was the Lord’s own pattern, given through David to the son chosen to sit on David’s throne.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:1
precepts.why:
During the Persian captivity we got liberty. Cyrus proclaimed, “The Lord God of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms of the earth”, and he said that because he knew it was a prophecy. Isaiah had written it: “Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut”.

Why is that important? Write this down: it was written 150 years before the birth of Cyrus. So when he came of age, he was shown his name in the scriptures, and he knew that the God of Israel, based on that prophecy, was dealing with him to release his people. It goes into more detail in the writings of Flavius Josephus, how the prophets showed Cyrus what he must do. And he obeyed.

So he made his proclamation to all twelve tribes: “Who is there among you of all his people?” Not just Judah. And whoever chose to stay where they had been living for decades, “let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts”. Some of the northern kingdom went back with Judah; some of the southern kingdom stayed out. Everybody did not go back.

precepts.why:
We read the judgment: the sword coming for Esau and for the nations, for the Lord “will give them that are wicked to the sword”. “But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.” Israel is the poor, and you escape that judgment by keeping the commandments with faith in the Lord and Saviour Jesus the Christ. “So the poor hath hope”: hope that something better is coming than what we are in right now.

“He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.” David shows what that looks like: “A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee.” That fire is not coming near you.

All that is read here is judgment: famine, war, the sword. “In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword.” He is going to deliver you and redeem you from the power of that sword, even while thousands fall around you.

But it comes with correction: “happy is the man whom God correcteth”. Brothers get soft and mealy and yellow about correction, and sisters get bitter at those who correct them. precepts.label: Job 5:12-13
precepts.why:
“The steps of his strength shall be straitened, and his own counsel shall cast him down. For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he walketh upon a snare.” His own counsel casts him down.

Job 5 says the same: “He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise. He taketh the wise in their own craftiness: and the counsel of the froward is carried headlong.”

Remember it: crafty counsel. All of the things they did against us are crafty counsel. The way your neighborhood is set up, redlining, benign neglect, all of it; slavery, exploitation, colonization: all of it is crafty counsel. And God takes the wise in their own craftiness. The net Esau laid is the net his own feet are caught in, and his counsel is carried headlong.

That is how “the light of the wicked shall be put out”. And when Esau's light is put out, the black Christian's head comes right out of the white man's behind. That is the only way the Lord can separate you from the white man, because you are too far gone.

precepts.label: Acts 26:23
precepts.why:
“Terrors shall make him afraid on every side”: the missiles, the ICBMs. “His strength shall be hungerbitten, and destruction shall be ready at his side. It shall devour the strength of his skin: even the firstborn of death shall devour his strength.”

Who is the firstborn of death? Paul tells it: “That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead”. That is the firstborn of death right there: Christ. He was the first raised up.

So it is Christ who will devour Esau's strength. “His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors.” Your slave master, the one who taught you how to fear God, will be brought to the king of terrors. “brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation. His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his branch be cut off.” His branch is his children. The one who rose first from the dead is the one who cuts him off.

precepts.label: Psalms 109:15
precepts.why:
“His remembrance shall perish from the earth, and he shall have no name in the street.” Your slave master, the one who taught you about this Bible, shall perish from the earth. David says it too: “Let them be before the Lord continually, that he may cut off the memory of them from the earth.” God said their memory will be cut off.

“He shall be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.” There is going to come a time when knowing about Esau will be like a bad dream: man, I had a dream I was in slavery to the basest people on planet earth.

“He shall neither have son nor nephew among his people, nor any remaining in his dwellings.” Cut off totally; a time is coming when they will not be around any more. “Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked, and this is the place of him that knoweth not God.” This ain't talking about our people; it is talking about Esau, the wicked on the earth. Destruction is coming to him, and even his memory will be cut off.

precepts.label: Isaiah 30:26
precepts.why:
“God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” See that little g: that is us. Asaph, with the Holy Spirit on him, records what we did wrong as the gods of the earth: “How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked?” So we walk on in gross darkness, and “all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” Everything is wrong. What is out of course because of our sins? Go to Genesis: “And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night.”

Now Isaiah shows the kingdom: “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days.” Does the sun have phases of transition? No. So in the kingdom the moon, which is a sign of the world, will not go back into darkness again. It is going to stay right. And the sun we say is so bright is not bright at all next to what it will be: sevenfold.

It is “in the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” Binding up the breach means gathering the twelve tribes of Israel back again. Acts 15 quotes the prophets: “After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down.” And Amos says, “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof.” Right now it is still fallen; we are trying to gather ourselves together. He will build us as in the days of old, that we may possess, own, the remnant of Edom and all the heathen.

The moon's phases started when Adam fell: the quarters, then the black moon, then it comes back. Before the fall it did not phase. That is why Israel is told, “Blow up the trumpet in the new moon, in the time appointed, on our solemn feast day”: when that brightness returns, we celebrate the Most High, because this is how it was in the beginning. When the Lord binds up the breach, the lights will be set back in course, and the moon will shine as the sun.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:14
precepts.why:
“Moab is my washpot; over Edom will I cast out my shoe; over Philistia will I triumph.” God says Moab is going to wash our clothes; they will be our laundromat forever. And he casts his shoe over Edom. That is why we are not supposed to be married to them. God says come out from among them and be ye separate. Some of us come of mixed parentage, and that is fine, but find yourself an Israelite woman, an Israelite man, and don't do this no more.

Isaiah shows the same triumph: “But they shall fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines toward the west; they shall spoil them of the east together.” We shall fly upon the shoulders of the Palestinians toward the west, and we shall spoil them of the east together.

“they shall lay their hand upon Edom and Moab; and the children of Ammon shall obey them.” We shall lay our hands upon Edom and Moab, and the children of Ammon, the Japanese, shall obey us.

So the nations that rule over Israel now, Edom, Moab and Ammon, will be under Israel's hand. That is what God means when he calls Moab his washpot and casts his shoe over Edom: they will serve.

precepts.label: Zephaniah 2:8-9
precepts.why:
God calls Moab his washpot, and Zephaniah shows why Moab and Ammon come to that end: “I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people, and magnified themselves against their border.”

God says, I heard what them damn Chinese said about my people, and the hatred of the Japanese. You think they love us? God says they reproach us; they hate us. They magnified themselves against the Israelites.

“Therefore as I live, saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation.” Destruction upon the earth: that is nuclear fire, and it has not happened yet.

“the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them.” The remnant of God's people shall spoil them, put them into captivity, and possess them; they are going to serve us. Nobody escapes, brothers and sisters. Nobody gets away with what they did to God's chosen people. And with that we say: twelve tribes.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:12-17
precepts.why:
David says, “Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together: Whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel.” Other nations aren't there; they are not mentioned here. Why does it say the city is compact together? Revelation shows the city.

It “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” This is our book. The kingdom is ours. The names on the gates are the tribes that go up.

“And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.” So it is 1,500 miles, the length, the breadth and the height all equal, like a square, like a box. That is a city compact together.

“And he measured the wall thereof, an hundred and forty and four cubits, according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel.” A hundred and forty-four cubits is approximately 216 feet by a man's measure, but it is the measure of the angel, so it is actually larger. That is the Jerusalem the tribes of the Lord go up to.

precepts.label: Revelation 20:4
precepts.why:
David says of Jerusalem, “For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” John saw those thrones: “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them.”

Thrones set, people sitting on them, and judgment given to them. And who are they? The souls “beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.”

The thrones of judgment in the psalm are real thrones in the kingdom, where the faithful reign with Christ. That is the Jerusalem the tribes go up to, and that is why we pray for its peace: it is a people before it is a place, and those thrones belong to us.

precepts.label: Luke 22:29-30
precepts.why:
The psalm says that in Jerusalem “there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Christ tells his apostles who sits on them and whom they judge: “And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me; That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

Sit on thrones doing what? Judging the twelve tribes of Israel. The thrones of judgment are for Israel, just as the tribes that go up to Jerusalem are “the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel.”

So don't read all this and try to throw the Chinese and the Japanese and everybody in there. Stop it. The kingdom, the table, the thrones and the judgment all belong to the twelve tribes.

precepts.label: Isaiah 62:7
precepts.why:
David says, “Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: they shall prosper that love thee.” Some of y'all are busy praying for Haiti, praying for Puerto Rico, praying for Mexico, praying for America. But the Bible said pray for Jerusalem.

Isaiah says how to pray for it: “And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.” Give the Lord no rest until he establishes Jerusalem and makes it a praise in the earth.

Remember, Jerusalem is a people before it is a place. We are Jerusalem; pray for us. We are not supposed to be praying, stop the war over there. No: they have to be moved out of our land so that we can go back home. That is the peace of Jerusalem, and that is the prayer that gives God no rest until it is done.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 33:2
precepts.why:
The Israelite way of life is structured so that if you lose your nationality, you are also cut off from your heritage. When they strip you of your identity, your laws, statutes and commandments follow it out the door; you stop performing the laws. Ezra prayed for “seed unto our heart, and culture to our understanding”: culture is heritage.

So “If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget her cunning.” The right hand is your strength; you usually work with your right hand. Jerusalem is our homeland, the place where you keep the laws and keep the feasts. Forget Jerusalem, and it is like forgetting your ability to work, the thing you know how to do.

Deuteronomy 33:2 shows what is in that right hand: “The Lord came from Sinai, and rose up from Seir unto them; he shined forth from mount Paran, and he came with ten thousands of saints: from his right hand went a fiery law for them.” The law came from God's right hand.

So if you forget your identity, guess what else goes with it? Your way of life, the fiery law. Forgetting Jerusalem and losing the cunning of the right hand is losing the law along with the nationality.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 3:26
precepts.why:
“If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth.” If we do not remember the Lord and his laws, statutes and commandments, the tongue sticks and you cannot talk; you cannot teach his laws to your people. The pastors in the churches have their tongues cleaving to the roof of their mouths, because they are not teaching the laws of God.

Ezekiel 3:26 says God does it: “And I will make thy tongue cleave to the roof of thy mouth, that thou shalt be dumb.” That thou shalt be a Christian. You are not Israel anymore, you are not keeping the commandments, you do not have faith in Christ; you have faith in white Jesus and in the white man. God made you into a Christian dummy.

Try to talk with your tongue cleaving to the roof of your mouth and hear how you sound. Everybody looks at you like, what's wrong with this dude? That is how Christians sound to those who know the Bible: level five retards, dumb ass Christians making up dumb doctrines, who think they are in the spirit of the Lord. To other Christians they sound totally fine and normal.

“and shalt not be to them a reprover”: you will be unable to reprove your people with this Bible. You are going to be like Michael Todd and Pastor Pam and all these foolish idiots, ordained ministers from the white man's theology schools and seminary classes.

And “if I prefer not Jerusalem above my chief joy”: we cannot prefer Jerusalem as our chief joy if we do not even know we are the Israelites.

precepts.label: Joshua 1:8
precepts.why:
What is supposed to be in your mouth? “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night.” The book of the law, the Bible, God's laws: that is what belongs in your mouth, the word of God and the laws of God.

But because we have been so wicked, God made our tongue to cleave to the roof of our mouth, and we sound like idiots trying to break this Bible down. When you are a Christian you do not know it, so you say strange things and strange doctrines, like the burning mountain is a meteorite. That is the stupidness that comes out when the law is not in the mouth.

Look at the black pastor today, preaching a sermon while getting a haircut: soft, sweet, moist, squishy, and a leader in the black church. That is the result when the law departs out of the mouth of those who are supposed to teach it.

So Psalms 137:6 is the curse on the tongue for forgetting Jerusalem, and Joshua 1:8 is what the tongue was made for: the law, spoken and meditated on day and night, so that we may observe to do all that is written therein.

precepts.label: Mark 7:21
precepts.why:
The psalm says the Lord “gathereth together the outcasts of Israel. He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.” Who are the broken in heart? We are the ones broken in mind and spirit, because the heart is the mind. Christ shows it: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts”. Thoughts come out of the heart, so the heart is the mind.

The broken in heart are the broken in mind: the twelve tribes, the outcasts of Israel. And it is the Lord who “bindeth up their wounds”. Everything we went through in captivity, it is the Lord that will minister the ointment to fix and heal his nation. These other nations cannot fix you with their philosophies and doctrines; they don't care about us and do not want to restore us, because restoring us means giving back everything they spoiled from the children of Israel.

Many of our brothers and sisters feel the only way we will come together is by the hands of these other nations. But it is Christ who is coming to restore this glorious nation, build up Jerusalem, gather the outcasts, and heal the broken in mind.

precepts.label: Tobit 8:7
precepts.why:
Marriage was designed to happen when you are young: you meet a young woman, and this is the person you grow old with. “rejoice with the wife of thy youth.” Tobias prayed the same thing on his wedding night: “And now, O Lord, I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.”

Hands went up around the room for five, ten, fifteen, twenty and twenty-five years of marriage and more, and the Bishop has been married 36 years. These are the examples we have right here. Those married a long time are supposed to still be able to look at their wife or husband and see when they were young. That is why they can be content: both of you change, both of you get old, but you remember.

“let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love.” When you marry her young her breasts are at three o'clock; as you grow old together they will be at six. But they are yours, brother, no matter what time it is. You walk in the room and she is the only thing you see. That bond can't be broken if you are in the Lord.

So we pray we are able to see our older years together. Some of us make it there and some don't; let it be because of passing, not because you weren't applying the scriptures or listening in class. The prophecy classes are dope, but you have to have the same zeal for the classes on marriage and repentance and apply them in your everyday life. Otherwise your marriage falls apart, your kids go who knows where, and then you look at us like it was our fault.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 24:12
precepts.why:
“She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.” That is the kind of wife you want, brothers. There was no kindness or wisdom in the email that attacked leadership over the one instance of a leader put out for adultery, while ignoring the three bishops and the seven or eight deacons who were in the midst of no such thing. For every solution we try to give, that spirit has two problems. That is not wife material; they are idolatrous women, some of them idolatrous evil black women, and they will try to destroy your life. Be mindful who you marry.

Now see what language God uses when Israel is in the midst of sin; he uses it in the female context: “She hath wearied herself with lies, and her great scum went not forth out of her”. There is one word that is often wanted but is hurtful to say, so God says it. Your scum is still in your mouth, sisters.

Scum is a layer of foul or unwanted matter that forms on top of a liquid, such as pond scum or soap scum. Informally it means a despised, immoral or worthless person or group, the scum of the earth. The slang meaning goes further: the epitome of a worthless, good-for-nothing human, at the bottom of the hierarchy of humans, possibly the worst word you can have your name associated with. It describes someone so disgraceful they are seen as the lowest form of life: worthlessness, a waste of skin, dirt, nothing. Because it is perfectly acceptable English and not a swear, it is even more demeaning; it is used only when it is the only word for the job, and it makes the victim feel like the lowest of the low.

That is the word God chose for his own people when she wore herself out with lies and the wickedness would not come out of her. Some of these evil sisters are the scum of the earth; that is what God is saying. So examine yourself, and open your mouth with wisdom and the law of kindness instead.

thread.text: The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 6:10
precepts.why:
“The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be”. What is the thing? Solomon tells you in chapter 6: “That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.” The thing is man on earth.

So “that which is done is that which shall be done”: whether man keeps the commandments or does not keep the commandments. “and there is no new thing under the sun.” From the time of Genesis, as it has been is going to be so in these last days. There are no new incidents on this earth; the things done by man are the things that were done in the past. And “There is no remembrance of former things”, because the spirits from the past return to the future.

Paul says the same in different words: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Written for our learning today, because the things done in the past reoccur. In a Christian mind everything is new; but nothing is new. To deal with these reoccurring events, we must read the history and testimonies of our ancestors.

Ezra shows it too: “I will liken my judgment unto a ring”. A ring is a circle, “like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first.” It is a continual event that reoccurs over and over. And the Lord “used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets”, comparing one thing to another.

That is why what we read in Daniel 3, Nebuchadnezzar setting up his golden image, is coming to pass again with the Trump administration and the golden statue the pastors prayed over. The man that hath been is the man that shall be.

thread.text: All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.
