precepts.label: Zechariah 1:15
precepts.why:
“there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.” That is Esau. The way Esau treated us is going to be to his own detriment.

The Lord says it in Zechariah: “And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction.” Yes, we sinned against our God. Yes, the Lord allowed us to go into the hands of our enemies. But they took it too far.

God was but a little displeased with Israel, and the heathen helped forward the affliction. You think Christ ain't see that? That is why Esau's rule over Jacob is to his own hurt: he went past what God allowed, and the Lord is sore displeased with him for it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 63:9
precepts.why:
“In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them”. In all of our affliction, through all of our slavery, the Lord saw all of it.

In all our affliction he was afflicted. So when he comes back, he is going to feel all of that pain and all of that suffering they did to the children of Israel, and he is going to wreak havoc on these nations.

“the angel of his presence saved them”. Salvation is not for the oppressors. Salvation is for those who have been afflicted. The man that ruled over another did it to his own hurt, because the one he afflicted is the one the Lord saves.

precepts.label: Psalms 119:85
precepts.why:
“The proud have digged pits for me, which are not after thy law.” The proud have digged pits for God's people.

They are not after God's laws. Look at it: how come you can abort in America? How come gay marriage is legalized? They don't keep God's laws and they don't uphold God's laws, but a lot of you coons out there follow behind this white man. They are not after God's commandments.

And who are the proud? Obadiah answers: it is Edom. The man that rules over another in Ecclesiastes 8 is the same proud one digging pits for Jacob, and his own pit is where he is headed.

precepts.label: Obadiah 1:1-3
precepts.why:
Who are the proud that digged the pits? “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?”

And who is he speaking to? Verse 1: “The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”. Concerning Edom: Esau, your friendly neighborhood white man, your Europeans, and the Americans.

Edom's pride has deceived him into thinking none shall bring him down. That is the one man who rules over another, and Solomon says he does it “to his own hurt.”

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 27:26-29
precepts.why:
“Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that setteth a trap shall be taken therein.” The proud digged pits for us, and they will fall in them. They thought evil against us, but the Lord saw it for good. Jacob is going to win in the end.

“He that worketh mischief, it shall fall upon him, and he shall not know whence it cometh.” That is what they do: they work mischief and call it law. And he is not going to know where it came from, because his pride has deceived him.

“Mockery and reproach are from the proud”. That is all they do: they accuse us, falsely accuse us, and mock us. “but vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for them.” That lion is the one in Jeremiah 4:7.

“They that rejoice at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare; and anguish shall consume them before they die.” Remember when they said raze it, raze it to the ground? The Lord has not forgotten. They will be taken in the snare. It does not pay to be wicked, and it does not pay to follow after your oppressor, because in the end they are going to be destroyed.

precepts.label: Psalms 94:20
precepts.why:
He that worketh mischief: that is what they do. “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” They work mischief and then call it law.

Two men getting married, two women getting married: all of these laws. Think about what Trump has done since he came into office: all of the firing and all the DEI hires, all of this is against us. They frame mischief and call it law.

A throne of iniquity cannot have fellowship with God. The ruler that frames mischief by a law over another man is ruling to his own hurt, and the mischief he works shall fall upon him.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 4:7
precepts.why:
Sirach said vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for the proud. Jeremiah shows the lion: “The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way; he is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate; and thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant.”

The destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way, to make the land desolate, without an inhabitant.

And that is twofold. It is talking about Nebuchadnezzar, and it is talking about Christ. The lion that came up against the land in the days of Jeremiah is a picture of the Lion that is coming for the nations that ruled over Israel to their own hurt.

precepts.label: Isaiah 26:10-14
precepts.why:
“Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness”. If favour was shown to Esau, he still wouldn't change his wicked ways. It does not pay to be wicked.

“in the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly, and will not behold the majesty of the Lord.” Where is the land of uprightness? The land of Israel. And what did he do there? He stole it. He will not behold the majesty of the Lord: he changes his image to a white man with stringy blonde hair and blue eyes.

“Lord, when thy hand is lifted up, they will not see: but they shall see, and be ashamed for their envy at the people”. The people are God's chosen people, the ones the heathen envy in 2 Esdras 2:28. “yea, the fire of thine enemies shall devour them. Lord, thou wilt ordain peace for us”, like we read earlier in Ephesians 2: he is going to ordain peace for us and destruction for our enemies.

“O Lord our God, other lords beside thee have had dominion over us”: like the so-called white man, like the Babylonians, like the Assyrians. “but by thee only will we make mention of thy name. They are dead, they shall not live; they are deceased, they shall not rise: therefore hast thou visited and destroyed them, and made all their memory to perish.” All of our enemies, all of these other lords that had rule over us, are dead. That is the hurt of the man that ruled over another.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:28
precepts.why:
Isaiah said the wicked shall see and be ashamed for their envy at the people. Who are those people? God's chosen people. Ezra says it: “The heathen shall envy thee, but they shall be able to do nothing against thee, saith the Lord.”

The heathen shall envy the Israelites. But they shall be able to do nothing. They can't stop it, because they ain't going to be in rulership any more. They are not going to have ownership any more.

That is the end of the man who ruleth over another to his own hurt: the time of his rule runs out, and all his envy cannot stop what the Lord has spoken for Israel.

precepts.why:

Sometimes he is trying to correct you, trying to show you what he wants so that you can be who he wants you to be. It ain't always him.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 7:26

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:18
precepts.why:
Isaiah had just told Ahaz, “the Lord himself shall give you a sign”. Then in chapter 8 the Lord has Isaiah write the name Maher-shalal-hash-baz, quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil, and Isaiah goes unto the prophetess, his wife, and “she conceived, and bare a son.” The child was named before he was conceived, the same way Gabriel named John and named Christ before they were conceived.

Then Isaiah says who the sign is: “Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from the Lord of hosts, which dwelleth in mount Zion.” Behold who? I, Isaiah, and the children. Not his wife. He never counts the woman.

So the sign of Isaiah 7:14 was not the virgin; it was the child. The virgin birth was garbage. The birth of Isaiah's son was the sign that Ephraim and Syria banding together against Judah would fail. Before the child could cry “My father, and my mother,” the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria were taken away before the king of Assyria. Assyria would pass through Judah and “reach even to the neck”, coming close to conquering but failing, because of Immanuel: “Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand: for God is with us.” Once Isaiah's son was born, the two kings could not succeed against Judah.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 12:6
precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezekiel to bear his stuff on his shoulders in their sight and carry it forth in the twilight, covering his face “that thou see not the ground: for I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel.” God made Ezekiel himself a sign unto the house of Israel.

Read on to verse 11 and Ezekiel is told to say it to Israel plainly: “Say, I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them: they shall remove and go into captivity.” What the prophet did, Israel would go through.

This lines up with Isaiah 8. When the Lord gives a sign, it is the man and the child he gives, not the woman. Isaiah and his children were signs and wonders in Israel, and Ezekiel was set for a sign to the house of Israel, which is why the sign of Isaiah 7:14 is the child born to Isaiah and the prophetess.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 24:24
precepts.why:
“Thus Ezekiel is unto you a sign.” What is he? A sign. Not his wife: Ezekiel. “according to all that he hath done shall ye do: and when this cometh, ye shall know that I am the Lord God.”

The Lord told Ezekiel to eat dung, and what did we end up doing? Eating dung. He was a sign, and what he did came upon Israel.

Read on to verse 27: “thou shalt be a sign unto them; and they shall know that I am the Lord.” Again and again the man is the sign. So when Isaiah says “I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs”, it fits the pattern of the prophets: the sign given to Ahaz was the child Isaiah's wife bare, Maher-shalal-hash-baz, not a virgin.

precepts.label: Luke 11:29-30
precepts.why:
When the people were gathered thick together, Christ said, “This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet.” Then: “For as Jonas was a sign unto the Ninevites, so shall also the Son of man be to this generation.”

Jonas was a sign. The Son of man was a sign. Men were always the signs. There is no scripture where the women were signs. Hosea was also a sign, and his marriage was a sign, but the woman by herself was never a sign.

That settles Isaiah 7 and 8. The Lord said he would give Ahaz a sign, and Isaiah tells us who it was: himself and the children the Lord gave him. The son born to Isaiah and the prophetess was the sign that God was with Judah, Immanuel, and that the two kings coming against Judah would come to nought.

precepts.label: Hosea 8:3-4
precepts.why:
“For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.” Who are the leaders in the Black community today? Your Black leaders have you fighting for Palestinians and fighting all kinds of stupid battles. And you Black Christians that are led of them are destroyed. Our people are so destroyed they don't even know it: destroyed with a warm fuzzy feeling every Sunday. The pastors are the new taskmasters. They get sent out by Esau, they learned the doctrines from Esau, and they bring it into your community, pulling up in the Benz while you walk to church in the cold and give him your last.

Hosea shows how it came to this. “Israel hath cast off the thing that is good: the enemy shall pursue him.” What is good? The laws of God, this Bible. Israel cast them off, and because of that the enemy pursues him.

“They have set up kings, but not by me: they have made princes, and I knew it not.” You set up leaders, brothers and sisters, but it isn't of the Lord. “Of their silver and their gold have they made them idols, that they may be cut off.” You make these men, these so-called leaders, your idols. You follow them wholeheartedly. Pastor says he needs an extra thousand dollars and you say, Pastor, I'mma work it out, I'mma get you your money. That's cold pimping.

And look at the fruit: a grandmother in Jamal Bryant's church sowing her twelve hundred dollars and being embarrassed because it was not enough; Eddie Long on the throne while the white man holds the mic and tells him he is no longer a commoner. These are your leaders that cause you to err.

“That they may be cut off.” And now we are cut off. That is what comes of casting off the law of God and setting up kings the Lord never chose.

precepts.label: Proverbs 3:31
precepts.why:
“Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” Put the oppressors on the screen: Pope Nicholas V and Pope Alexander VI. In 1452 Pope Nicholas V issued Dum Diversas, authorizing King Alfonso V of Portugal to fight, subjugate and conquer the Saracens and pagans in African territory. Those were good Christians.

Think about it. Without those two devils, those two Christians, there would be no such thing as an African-American, a Jamaican, a Haitian, a Puerto Rican. We are named after whatever landmass we were scattered to, and we are the result of those men. Christians did this to us. And now we revel in it, reverence them, and follow their laws and their ways of life.

The scripture says choose none of his ways. But tomorrow at 11 o'clock Sunday morning, where will all our people be? Not listening to the truth. They will be in church getting a good dose of the doctrine of the man that enslaved them, that turned them into African-Americans and Jamaicans and Haitians. They can't wait to go learn about a good Jesus.

That is the leaders of Isaiah 9:16 causing our people to err. Look at the results of being taught Christianity: a man on television saying he is a Christian first and that black is a construct, when the white man put us in chains and did not do that to his own people; a girl who let a boy call her the N-word and call him master; our people turning up on each other and showing teeth to everybody else. That is what comes of envying the oppressor and choosing his ways.

precepts.label: Mark 8:36-37
precepts.why:
Terence Crawford said there was not a number that could get him back in that ring, and then said for 100 million dollars you can have my soul. That nigger was dead serious; look at his eyes. That is a dangerous man: a man who would sell out his mama and his children and do anything for money. That is the result of 400 years with Esau, and he just said out loud what the majority of Black celebrities, rappers and singers think.

“For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?” Esau gives you whatever you want: all the riches, all the connections, all the power, wealth you can't run from. But in order to get it, you lose your own soul.

“Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?” What do these celebrities give in exchange for their souls? Their booty. They give it up, and Amalek takes it. Your Jay-Zs and 50 Cents, your Mariah Careys and Whitneys: they have to give in order to receive.

What are you going to stand for if everything is about money? You have no dignity and no morals. These are the results of the leaders of this people causing them to err, and of Black Christians led by them being destroyed. There are no laws with them, because they were taught the laws are done away with.

No one is entering New Jerusalem with hatred in their heart.

thread.label: Isaiah 14:1
thread.text: For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.

precepts.label: Zephaniah 2:1
precepts.why:
“For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land.” Before he sets us in our land, he tells the twelve tribes what to do: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired.” We are the nation not desired, and God is instructing the twelve tribes to gather themselves together, to wake up.

“Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you.” That decree is the destruction that is prophesied to come. Get yourselves together before destruction comes. Things are moving at a quicker pace, and that is why the Bishop says he loves President Trump: he is forcing prophecies to come to pass and forcing the Israelites to do what the Bible says.

Who gathers? “Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.” The meek are humble to God’s word, men and women who do his commandments without making excuses. We cannot gather with camps that say we are not keeping any Sabbath, or that throw you out for wearing fringes with a border of blue.

Then the judgment on the land: “For Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation.” “I will even destroy thee, that there shall be no inhabitant.” The Palestinians are not just pushed out; according to the Bible they are destroyed. “And the coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah”, “for the Lord their God shall visit them, and turn away their captivity.” That is Israel set in their own land.

precepts.label: Amos 3:3
precepts.why:
“Gather yourselves together” does not mean gather with everybody. “Can two walk together, except they be agreed?”

You get some morons that say, Let’s join ourselves with the camp that believes John the Baptist was a wicked nigger. You cannot join with that. Let’s join with the camp that believes men do not have to work: get seven women, eight women, and let them work for you. No, we cannot join with that.

Some people are simple, and they ask, Why aren’t y’all all together? This is why. Two cannot walk together unless they are agreed, and the ones who gather are those who “have wrought his judgment”, the meek who do God’s laws, seek righteousness and seek meekness.

So when the Lord will yet choose Israel and set them in their own land, the gathering before the decree is not one of mixed doctrines. It is a gathering of those agreed on God’s commandments.

precepts.label: Amos 9:11
precepts.why:
The Lord “will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land.” Judah shall live on the sea coast, and it gets better: “For God will save Zion, and will build the cities of Judah: that they may dwell there, and have it in possession.” And Amos: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.” The tabernacle of David is the twelve tribes, built again as in the days of old.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name.” There are people calling themselves Jewish today, and Jew comes from Judah, praise of Yahawah; they are not the praise of Yahawah. And people calling themselves Christians, the anointed ones; they are not the anointed ones.

“And I will bring again the captivity of my people of Israel, and they shall build the waste cities, and inhabit them.” There are waste cities all over there, and after Armageddon there will be more. And we will have servants: that is the strangers joined to the house of Jacob, the heathen round about us as bondmen and bondmaids, when that law goes back in full effect.

“And I will plant them upon their land, and they shall no more be pulled up out of their land which I have given them, saith the Lord thy God.” That is Isaiah 14:1 fulfilled: set in their own land, never pulled out again.

thread.text: The burden of Moab. Because in the night Ar of Moab is laid waste, and brought to silence; because in the night Kir of Moab is laid waste, and brought to silence;

precepts.label: Revelation 11:8
precepts.why:
“The burden of Moab. Because in the night Ar of Moab is laid waste, and brought to silence; because in the night Kir of Moab is laid waste.” Ar and Kir are cities of Moab. This took place under Nebuchadnezzar, when Babylon came in smiting Moab. But there is more to it, and we go to Revelation to see it.

“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city.” The dead bodies are the spiritually dead bodies of the Israelites. And the great city is Babylon the great. That is the point to hold: Revelation speaks of a great city, a Babylon, in the last days, where our people lie spiritually dead in the street.

So Babylon is not only the kingdom of Nebuchadnezzar. There is a Babylon of the last days as well, and Revelation 14:8 names it: “Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city.” When Isaiah shows Babylon laying Moab waste in the night, bringing its cities to silence, and Moab howling over Nebo and Medeba with baldness on every head and every beard cut off, it carries a dual meaning. Moab, which today is China, the Vietnamese and the Mongolians, will be laid waste again, and the great city where our people lie spiritually dead is the Babylon of today.

precepts.label: Revelation 14:8
precepts.why:
Revelation 11:8 speaks of “the great city.” Revelation 14 proves which city that is: “And there followed another angel, saying, Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city, because she made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication.”

The great city is Babylon, the one that made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication. This place, America, is a spiritual Babylon. It is not the actual Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar, but this place God calls Babylon the great.

That is why we went there from Isaiah 15. Isaiah’s burden of Moab took place when Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar smote Moab: Ar of Moab and Kir of Moab, cities of Moab, “laid waste, and brought to silence” in the night. Moab went up to the high places to weep and howled over Nebo and Medeba, and “on all their heads shall be baldness, and every beard cut off”, because Moab shaves off its hair in great sorrow and mourning, a custom that remains in their religions to this day, in the head shaving of the monks and nuns of Chinese religion.

So when Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar smote Moab, know that there is dual significance behind it. There is a Babylon the great today, and Moab today is China, who with the Vietnamese and the Mongolians will be laid waste once again.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 40:11
precepts.why:
Isaiah tells Moab, “hide the outcasts; bewray not him that wandereth”, and “Let mine outcasts dwell with thee, Moab; be thou a covert to them from the face of the spoiler.” The outcast is us, the Israelites; that is why verse 1 speaks of “the mount of the daughter of Zion.” During the time of Nebuchadnezzar many Israelites fled and hid amongst Moab, and the spoiler they hid from was Nebuchadnezzar.

Jeremiah is the proof of where our people fled: “Likewise when all the Jews that were in Moab, and among the Ammonites, and in Edom, and that were in all the countries, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah, and that he had set over them Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan.”

Where were they? In Moab, among the Ammonites, and in Edom. When the king of Babylon came through, Judah scattered into those lands and hid there, just as Isaiah told Moab to hide them. And “Sela” in verse 1 is Petra, which is Edom; they call Edom Petra today.

There is a dual meaning behind these scriptures. What happened with our people and Moab in the time of Nebuchadnezzar speaks again to the last days, when Moab is China and our people are outcasts among the nations, until “the extortioner is at an end, the spoiler ceaseth, the oppressors are consumed out of the land” and the throne of Christ is established.

precepts.label: Isaiah 9:6-7
precepts.why:
“And in mercy shall the throne be established: and he shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David.” The throne that is going to be established is the throne of Christ, and Isaiah 9 shows it: “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder.” The government shall be upon the shoulders of Christ.

“and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” A lot of people don’t understand why he is called the everlasting Father. It is because the one you think is the heavenly Father in the Old Testament was actually Christ. That is why there is a lot of confusion in the Israelite community.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Don’t just read by that word increase; the mustard seed of Matthew 13 shows it. We are at the mustard seed stage now, and this is the beginning of God’s government.

“upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever.” To order it and establish it with judgment and justice: that is law and order. That is why we establish law, order and rank, and teach brothers and sisters the laws, commandments and statutes of the Holy Bible.

Some don’t like law because they like adultery better; they don’t like order because they like disorder, chaos, a toxic marriage and a chaotic life, married today and divorced tomorrow. That is genetic encoding from slavery, and it is in all of us. But the Bible can break that spirit, only if you let it. Only God can cleanse that from you, and his throne, established in mercy, is judging and “hasting righteousness.”

precepts.label: Matthew 13:31-32
precepts.why:
Isaiah 9:7 says, “Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Why does it say the increase of his government? Christ answers in a parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds.”

A mustard seed is one of the smallest of all seeds, and that is how the kingdom of heaven is on the earth now. “but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof.” When it is grown is the increase. All nations are going to submit to it and follow what it says.

We are at that mustard seed stage now. A lot of people say that Israelite thing ain’t nothing. Oh no, it is something: it is the beginning of God’s government. And it is only going to increase. When you check the history from the time of Nat Turner, you might think it ended there. It did not. Look at the history of the Israelite schools; we here are part of that great history, part of that mustard seed that, when it is grown, is the greatest of all. You are not tricking us back into worshipping white Jesus.

So the throne of Isaiah 16:5, established in mercy in the tabernacle of David, starts small and grows until every nation lodges under it.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:8
precepts.why:
“The burden of Egypt.” Egypt was before Isaiah’s time, so what Egypt is this speaking about? Revelation answers it: “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.”

It says spiritually. Sodom is not around anymore; it is destroyed, those cities of Sodom and Gomorrah near Ein Bokek are nothing. But spiritual Sodom is here. It goes on even in the landmass of Israel among the Israelis, but prominently and predominately here in America, with all types of switcheroos: men acting like women and women acting like men, committing things contrary to the laws of God. And it is spiritual Egypt, the house of bondage. So replace Egypt with America: the burden of America.

“where also our Lord was crucified.” They crucify Christ in his image, in his message, and in denying that you men are the greatest thing on the face of this earth. They say, hell no, all people, God loves everybody.

“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city.” America is that great city, and our people are spiritually dead here. They are fearful of freedom; there is no spirit in them to rebel with the laws of God.

So when Isaiah says the Lord rides upon a swift cloud and comes into Egypt, it is the Lord coming with his chariots and angels to bring wrath and destruction upon America. Its idols shall be moved at his presence, and its heart, the mindset, doctrines and mentality of the oppressive kingdom, shall melt in the midst of it. He will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: militia against militia, civil war, brother against brother, city against city. This place is divided; the stars are falling and the stripes are broken. That is Esau rising against himself, and it is not our fight.

precepts.label: Joel 2:15-20
precepts.why:
Isaiah says “they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors.” What will the oppressors be doing? The same thing 2 Esdras 16, Revelation 12:17, Matthew 10 and Matthew 24 say: Jacob's trouble. Joel shows the crying.

“Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly: Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children, and those that suck the breasts.” This is going to be a major fast, because there will be so much devastation to our people. “Let the bridegroom go forth of his chamber, and the bride out of her closet”: when this fast goes out, we are not doing weddings or planning weddings. Weddings are finished. We have to pray to the Lord because our people are dying.

“Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Lord.” That is the cry of Isaiah 19, crying bitterly because there is going to be death. “And give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?”

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people.” He answers, “I will send you corn, and wine, and oil” and “I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen: But I will remove far off from you the northern army.” That is the great multitude after us in 2 Esdras 16. He will “drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea.” The east sea is the Dead Sea and the utmost sea is the Mediterranean: the land of Israel between them, what they call the Middle East. The Lord is going to cause things to pop off there.

“And his stink shall come up, and his ill savour shall come up, because he hath done great things.” The Lord is going to destroy them over there: tribulation, World War III, Armageddon. It is all laid out for us. Yes, you are dying, but you are not dead; the Lord takes the northern army down, and then he sends us “a saviour, and a great one”, Christ, to deliver us.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 49:20-22
precepts.why:
Joel says the Lord will remove the northern army far off and drive it into the land between the Dead Sea and the Mediterranean. Jeremiah shows what happens there.

“Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Edom; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the inhabitants of Teman.” Teman is still Edom. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: the least of the flock is these Israelis, the fake Israelis. That whole area on the map is where it is all going to go down. “Surely he shall make their habitations desolate with them.”

“The earth is moved at the noise of their fall, at the cry the noise thereof was heard in the Red sea.” The ships in the Red Sea are going to hear about this fall.

“Behold, he shall come up and fly as the eagle, and spread his wings over Bozrah.” Bozrah is Jordan, that area on the map. America is going to come to Israel's rescue, so they think. “And at that day shall the heart of the mighty men of Edom be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.” They are going to be afraid, because they don't realize it's a trap: NATO turns against them, and everybody is against America and Israel.

That is how the Lord takes the northern army down over there, while he tells us, don't worry, you are dying but you are not dead. Jacob's trouble is great, “but he shall be saved out of it.”

precepts.label: Jude 1:20-21
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the Lord keeps him in perfect peace “because he trusteth in thee.” That is the key part. You trust in the Lord, you trust in his words, and you build yourself up. Jude says it: “But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost”.

It is the leaders' job to build the man, but once you have the foundation, it is on you to take the notes from the classes, apply them to yourself and add to them. Do a serious checkup from the neck up. Take an erasable dry marker to your mirror and write your issues with the scriptures next to them, what you need to fix, and at the top write: execute. Those are your orders for the day. If you don't see it, you're never going to fix it. Too many brothers and sisters don't write anything down: notes done, Bible closed the rest of the week, and then they're stressing, when the fix to what they were dealing with last week and what they will face this week came out in the class. We don't examine ourselves.

Don't ask the captain what he sees in you. What do you see in you? Leadership has the blessing of discernment, but that only goes so far; we can't see through you or know all the deep recesses of what you're dealing with. You have to go before the Lord, explain it, confess it, and ask him in sincerity to remove those things from you.

Don't play with what you know you are dealing with. The spirits on brothers and sisters who could care less can rub off even on leadership; a lot of brothers and sisters are spiritual vampires, and it takes a toll on leaders who love our people. God has this hospital set up for you to get the help, and the medicine is the laws. You have a headache, you don't throw the Tylenol in the trash, you take it. So why throw away the medicine when it concerns your soul and your salvation? Why be fearful of freedom?

“Keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life.” Keep yourselves in the love of God, not in the crosshairs of his anger, his rage, his wrath. It is our job to keep ourselves there. I can't save you, and you can't save me. It ain't going to be easy; you have to go through this fiery trial to get the kingdom. So do your part. You have the keys to freedom, and that is the trust that keeps the mind stayed on the Lord in perfect peace.

precepts.label: Joshua 1:8
precepts.why:
What actually brings us peace? Not enlisting in this war, and not hoping America goes back to the old ways. “Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee”. The mind that is stayed on the Lord is the mindset of Joshua 1:8: the book of the law does not depart out of your mouth, and you meditate on it day and night.

That is your four chapters a day. That is you not separating yourself, and having that godly conversation consistently, as in Malachi, where they thought upon the Lord's name and a book of remembrance was written. That is making sure the sick among us in the congregations are well taken care of. That is you men doing the blitz, traveling, doing your due diligence by all manner to get out of that black shirt and get out here and teach your people, to become men of valor and soldiers of the Lord, and put in your brick.

You establish yourself on the laws of God. That is your meditation, your chief joy. You're not worried about what is played on the radio, and you could give a damn about what's on the internet unless it is funneled through the Bible so you can keep up with the times.

Then the news, the destruction and the chaos won't worry you. You'll have a Coke bottle smile from one ear to the next, because you know the mysteries. You're not fearful of freedom. The mind that meditates on the law day and night is the mind the Lord keeps in perfect peace.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 1:11-13
precepts.why:
“We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement.” We made a covenant with America. We are going to get America to give us money; we are going to live good and eat good, eat the garlic, the melons and the leeks; we are going to get reparations. Maccabees shows the same device in Israel before: “In those days went there out of Israel wicked men, who persuaded many, saying, Let us go and make a covenant with the heathen that are round about us.”

“for since we departed from them we have had much sorrow.” That is the thinking: we must always have massa around. We are foundational, so all we have to do is stay here, be patient and quiet, and massa will give us money because he knows we deserve it.

“So this device pleased them well. Then certain of the people were so forward herein, that they went to the king.” They went to the king themselves. But ask the questions: how much? Where is the plan? How much does each Negro get, a hundred thousand, two hundred thousand? They have no idea. They have no plan. It is just talk.

And they think the scourge will pass them by: when America is getting destroyed, “it shall not come unto us”; no problems are coming our way. “for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves.” The falsehood is a false identity, false titles, lying about how we got here and where we come from, and they will hide under it until death comes. But the gathering is unto Christ, the gathering of all twelve tribes, not the dividing of foundational Americans; and if you don’t repent and keep the commandments, you will burn with America.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 30:16
precepts.why:
Isaiah calls Israel “a people robbed and spoiled.” We are robbed of our nationality, robbed of the understanding that we are the twelve tribes of the children of Israel. Jeremiah shows how we are spoiled, and what the Lord will do about it.

“Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured”: that is going to take place upon the oppressors of our people. “and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity”: the adversaries are all the nations outside of the children of Israel, and every one of the nations that oppress us shall go into captivity.

How do they spoil us? Over a multitude of captivities the children of Israel have gone into, every single nation has had its hand in the oppression of the twelve tribes. That includes the Arabs, that a lot of brothers and sisters want to cry over when they see what is going on in Palestine. Those people had our people oppressed too; they were spoiling the hell out of us. What we are seeing overseas right now is the righteous judgment of the Lord, prophecy fulfilling right now.

Yet brothers and sisters are so damn fearful to escape this captivity and get themselves together, even as the prophecies come to pass. Many are called, but few are chosen, so self-examine. With bombs dropping and rumors of war, men are still catting around, committing fornication, letting their wives rule over them and hide their folly, paying for prostitutes, hooked on marijuana and controlled by the porn system. Our people are sick; they are afraid of freedom, because sin controls them.

“and they that spoil thee shall be a spoil, and all that prey upon thee will I give for a prey.” The nations that spoiled us shall in turn be a spoil for us, because the tables are turned. We serve a just God. So Isaiah’s people “for a prey” and “for a spoil” will not stay that way: those that prey upon Israel are given for a prey themselves.

thread.label: Isaiah 43:1
thread.text: But now thus saith the Lord that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.

classes.title: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 6:58
precepts.why:
“Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.” And to redeem us, “I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee. Since thou wast precious in my sight.” We are precious in his sight because we are the apple of his eye.

Ezra shows what we are to him: “But we thy people, whom thou hast called thy firstborn, thy only begotten, and thy fervent lover, are given into their hands.” We are his fervent lover. We are his bride. We are his wife.

That is why God gave Egypt, Ethiopia and Seba, which is Somalia, for our ransom: to deliver us out of captivity he had to destroy the Egyptian army, and Ethiopia that was a help to them. “therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” In order for us to be delivered from slavery and captivity, God said, I have to destroy nations for them to release you.

So when Isaiah says “thou art mine”, it is the voice of a husband over his wife. The firstborn, the only begotten, the fervent lover given into the hands of the nations is the one God redeems.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 18:8
precepts.why:
“I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.” Do you think the nations are just going to give his people back? No. Christ comes with armies: “And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.” Wherever the Israelites are, the armies of God will go there and deliver us and destroy those nations.

The Christian mentality wants a white Jesus to come back throwing flowers, and John Hagee says Christ will set his government up to get the Democrats and Republicans in order. Wisdom of Solomon shows what salvation really is: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” We all want the salvation of the righteous, and we have to accept the destruction of the enemy too. That is what we just read in Isaiah 43.

“For wherewith thou didst punish our adversaries, by the same thou didst glorify us, whom thou hadst called.” The same way he punishes our adversaries, he glorifies us. That is the bride of Christ: Christ is coming to get his woman. That is what the whole thing is about.

So the redeeming of Isaiah 43:1, “I have called thee by thy name”, is the calling of Wisdom 18: “us, whom thou hadst called”, glorified by the very judgment that punishes the nations holding us.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 16:14
precepts.why:
“I have redeemed thee.” Jeremiah shows that this redemption will be greater than the first: “Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.” When he delivered us out of Egypt, he destroyed Egypt, he destroyed Ethiopia and he destroyed Seba, Somalia.

“But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north, and from all the lands whither he had driven them.” The land of the north is North America. All the lands whither he had driven them are the Caribbean, Africa, and all the different lands we are scattered in.

“and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.” That is Isaiah 43: “I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west.” We are here in the west, the western hemisphere.

So the redemption promised to Jacob is not the one out of ancient Egypt. It is the deliverance out of the land of the north and every land of our captivity, and it will be so great that the Exodus will no longer be what men speak of.

precepts.label: Romans 8:21
precepts.why:
“Fear not: for I have redeemed thee.” Paul shows what that redemption brings: “Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.”

The creature itself is you and me. We shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. That is talking about us being delivered, not just from this body, but from captivity.

It is the same promise as Jeremiah 16: the Lord that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands whither he had driven them, bringing them again into the land he gave their fathers. Isaiah 43 says he will say to the north, Give up, and bring his sons and daughters from the ends of the earth.

So “I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine” ends in liberty: the children of God set free from bondage, the captives delivered in the year of jubilee.

thread.label: Isaiah 43:3-7
thread.text: For I am the Lord thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour: I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee.

classes.title: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 18:7
precepts.why:
Isaiah says, “I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee”, and “therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” When it says give men for thee, it means kill men for thee. We don’t have to do anything; God says, let me do it. Wisdom of Solomon shows why it must be that way: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.”

The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies go together. There can be no salvation without the destruction of your enemies. There can be no salvation of the oppressed without the destruction of the oppressor. That is so plain, but for Christians it is so difficult to understand.

That is what happened in Egypt, and it is what Isaiah promises again. Egypt, Ethiopia and Seba were given for Israel’s ransom because Israel was “precious in my sight”, “honourable”, and loved of God. The nations fall in Israel’s place.

And with the destruction comes the gathering: “Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.” The same judgment that destroys the oppressor sets the righteous free and brings every one that is called by his name home.

thread.text: The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:23
precepts.why:
“The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory.” That does not mean there will be no sun and no moon. They will always be there. But we are not going to need that light, because we are going to be on another level: a spiritual level, a god level.

Revelation shows the same thing: “And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof.” That is what we just read in Isaiah 60:19.

The city is “the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” That is what Christ meant when he said, Thy kingdom come. It “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.”

“Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the Lord shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended.” Everything goes back to the way it was. Israel in the kingdom lives in the light of the Lamb, and the days of our mourning are ended.

precepts.label: Revelation 21:24
precepts.why:
“And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it.” People use this to say all the nations will be saved. But saved does not mean salvation here; it is in the context of rulership. Saved from what?

The precept is Zechariah: “And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” Saved means left: they were left from being destroyed. Christ did not destroy them, and they are going to obey. Walking in the light of it means they serve the King and keep the feast of tabernacles.

“and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it”, as Isaiah says: “Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.”

“And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.” Those nations do not walk in. They bring it to us at the front gate, and then they go back. Those written in the Lamb’s book of life are the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:3
precepts.why:
“Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.” God is saying to us, Arise, wake up. Shine means teach. Thy light is come: Christ is come. The glory of the Lord risen upon thee is the Holy Spirit.

“For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people.” We are in the worst darkness. “but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee”: wisdom and knowledge shall be seen upon us.

“And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising.” The other nations shall come to our light. What is our light? The laws in Christ. And what does it look like for them to come to it? Zechariah 14: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” Keeping the high holy days: that is them coming to our light.

That is why the Lord is our everlasting light in Isaiah 60:19. The nations do not bring the light; they come to Israel’s light and bring their kings and their wealth to it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 66:23
precepts.why:
“And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord.” This was brought up for the nations coming to Israel’s light in the kingdom.

The book, chapter and verse the Bishop was looking for is Zechariah 14, where it is spelled out: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” The nations that are left come up to worship at the appointed times, keeping the high holy days. That is them coming to our light.

So all flesh coming to worship is not all flesh entering the city. They are the nations left from destruction, serving and worshipping the King at his feasts, while only those written in the Lamb’s book of life, the twelve tribes of Israel, enter the city whose everlasting light is the Lord.

thread.label: Isaiah 61:1
thread.text: The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the pri

classes.title: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.label: Luke 4:18
precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 is fulfilled in Christ, who read it himself: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor.” The good tidings of Isaiah are the gospel. And the poor are not everybody: “the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.” The poor are the poor of Zion. You do not even have to go to Isaiah 14; Isaiah 61 itself says it is them that mourn in Zion.

“he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives.” We are the captives. How can you read captive and think everybody? Rome was dominating Israel at that time. “and recovering of sight to the blind”: we are the blind people. “to set at liberty them that are bruised”: bruised in sin.

“To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.” The acceptable year of the Lord is our day of jubilee, and we had better accept that.

Imagine the Israelites and the Romans sitting in church together, the captives and the captors side by side, told we are all the same. It makes no sense. Jake looks over at Esau to see if he is upset, and if master is upset at this reading, he disregards it: black Christians hate anything that upsets white folks, and that is why they do not believe. But Christ read it plainly: he came to proclaim liberty to the captives of Israel, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound, bound in these prisons we call America, the Caribbean and whatever lands we are in.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:32
precepts.why:
“the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek.” Christ read it in Luke 4 as “to preach the gospel to the poor.” When it says the poor, who is that? Isaiah answers: “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

That is telling you who the poor are: the poor of Zion, the poor of his people. Zion is another name for the Israelites.

And Isaiah 61 itself agrees: he came “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes”. Why are we mourning? Because we are captive.

So the good tidings, the brokenhearted, the captives and them that are bound are not all nations. They are the poor of the Lord’s people, the Israelites in captivity, who shall trust in the Zion the Lord has founded.

precepts.label: Zephaniah 3:19
precepts.why:
When the captives are set free, “ye shall be named the Priests of the Lord”, “For your shame ye shall have double”, and “their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed.” No matter where we go on this planet they are going to know our children by name. Today you want to talk to your boss and he turns his back to you; on that day they are going to beg for your attention.

Zephaniah is the precept to that: “Behold, at that time I will undo all that afflict thee.” He is going to undo all the nations that afflict us. “and I will save her that halteth”: we are the ones that halt, because we are captive. “and gather her that was driven out.”

“and I will get them praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame.” We get that fame and that glory, and our children are going to get it too. Everybody is going to acknowledge who we are. “At that time will I bring you again, even in the time that I gather you: for I will make you a name and a praise among all people of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before your eyes, saith the Lord.”

That is the liberty proclaimed to the captives in Isaiah 61: not only freed, but honoured in the very lands that shamed us.

precepts.label: Isaiah 63:4
precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 proclaims “the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God.” There is a particular day in a particular year when God will come to deliver his people. Isaiah 63 shows that day: “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength?” This is Christ, the Son of God, and his garment is glorious, not a sheet or a robe.

“Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat?” Isaiah is asking Christ, Why are you red? It looks like you were stomping grapes. “I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me.” Christ trod down the nations and killed them alone. He did not need the help of the twelve tribes of Israel; he did it himself.

“for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments.” The wine represents their blood.

“For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.” We are the redeemed. The year of my redeemed is the acceptable year of the Lord in Isaiah 61, our jubilee, and it comes with the day of vengeance on the nations.

thread.text: And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not: for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn

precepts.label: Jeremiah 9:2-3
precepts.why:
“And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee”. Even Jeremiah, who was not a wicked man, still went into captivity and had to deal with the same things as all the wicked Israelites. And look at how Jeremiah felt about his people, knowing how wicked we are.

“Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them!” Far away in the wilderness, just to get away from these people. They look just like him and he grew up with them, but he wants to get away from them. Why? “for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.”

“And they bend their tongues like their bow for lies”. Do black people do a lot of lying? Yes, we do. “but they are not valiant for the truth upon the earth; for they proceed from evil to evil, and they know not me, saith the Lord.” They move from evil to evil and they do not know God.

That is the black Christian. Do not let them fool you. They can quote the popular scriptures all day, John 3:16, neither Jew nor Greek, no weapon formed against me shall prosper, and say God got me. No, Satan got you. You and Satan are like my buddy and me. That is why the Lord says Israel shall discontinue from its heritage and serve its enemies in a land it knew not: a people who know him not.

precepts.label: Sirach 17:11
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says Israel “shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not”. We have lost our heritage and we serve our enemies, one of the curses. Who are our enemies? All the other nations, the enemies of God. Christians do not want to hear that, but here we are unapologetically biblical. Take it up with God.

What is the heritage we lost? “Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.” The law of life is the heritage we lost in Jeremiah 17. To take it, they had to break our bands asunder and separate us.

Rudolph R. Windsor, in From Babylon to Timbuktu, made mention that the Israelite culture is structured so that if you lose your nationality, you also discontinue from your heritage. We have a certain way of life as a certain people. When they strip you of your identity, what follows is your laws, statutes and commandments: you are not going to be performing the laws. Lose the identity and the heritage, the law of life, goes with it.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 8:6
precepts.why:
Ezra prayed, “O Lord, if thou suffer not thy servant, that we may pray before thee, and thou give us seed unto our heart, and culture to our understanding, that there may come fruit of it”. Another word for culture is heritage: the same heritage Israel discontinued from in Jeremiah 17, the law of life.

The Psalmist shows it: “If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget her cunning.” The right hand is your strength, what you work with. And Moses says, “from his right hand went a fiery law for them.” If you forget your identity, your way of life goes with it.

“If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth; if I prefer not Jerusalem above my chief joy.” Forget the law and you cannot speak it; your tongue is stuck. Try to talk with your tongue cleaving to the roof of your mouth and you sound crazy. That is how Christians sound to those who know the Bible, with their doctrines; to other Christians they sound fine. We cannot prefer Jerusalem as our chief joy if we do not know we are the Israelites, so we become ordained ministers from the white man's theology schools and seminaries, and we sound like idiots.

So culture to our understanding is what we need back: the identity and the laws that go with it, so that fruit may come of it.

thread.text: Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the Lord.

precepts.label: Matthew 28:19-20
precepts.why:
“Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the Lord.” “Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them”. The pastors keep the confusion and the sin in the black community going. They keep Ephraim separated from Judah; our bands are cast asunder, and they are not bringing it back. They are furthering the scattering of the children of Israel, not bringing us together.

So look what Christ had to come and say: “Go ye therefore, and teach all nations”. Why all nations? Because we are scattered in all nations, and the pastors are furthering the scattering. Christ sends his disciples out to the scattered sheep in every country, “Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you”: the very commandments the pastors say are done away with.

That is the other half of Jeremiah 23: “I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all countries whither I have driven them, and will bring them again to their folds”, “And I will set up shepherds over them which shall feed them”. Where the pastors scatter and teach that the law is gone, the Lord sends shepherds to go into all nations and teach his people to observe everything he commanded.

precepts.label: Matthew 15:12-14
precepts.why:
The prophets of Jerusalem “strengthen also the hands of evildoers, that none doth return from his wickedness”. When Jamal Bryant was checked over his wife's dress, he did not say the Bible does say a woman should dress modestly, I was in error, I repent. He doubled down: I ain't wrong. So when we see his congregants on the street and say, sis, you can't wear pants, brother, you can't sell drugs, they double down just like him. That is the evil example. None return from their wickedness; they say the Lord did away with that, you twisted the scripture.

Christ cut the Pharisees the same way. His disciples said, “Knowest thou that the Pharisees were offended, after they heard this saying?” He answered, “Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up.” These pastors, these so-called men of the cloth, have to go; they will be rooted up.

“Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch.” The pastor and the congregation both fall. So leave these lying churches alone. If they will not repent, leave them alone. God says of them, “they are all of them unto me as Sodom, and the inhabitants thereof as Gomorrah”, and he “will feed them with wormwood, and make them drink the water of gall”.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 22:25-27
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says “both prophet and priest are profane”. Ezekiel shows what that looks like: “There is a conspiracy of her prophets in the midst thereof, like a roaring lion ravening the prey; they have devoured souls”. These pastors devour your souls. “they have taken the treasure and precious things; they have made her many widows in the midst thereof”, through adultery.

“Her priests have violated my law, and have profaned mine holy things: they have put no difference between the holy and profane, neither have they shewed difference between the unclean and the clean”. They blurred the lines. There is no right or wrong now, just a grey area in the middle: do a little evil, a little good, everything is grey. “and have hid their eyes from my sabbaths, and I am profaned among them.”

“Her princes in the midst thereof are like wolves ravening the prey, to shed blood, and to destroy souls, to get dishonest gain.” The black Christian congregants are the prey. It is money, money, money; covetousness is what they are. Juanita Bynum can charge over a thousand dollars for a prayer class and be that bold because the black community does not know the Bible.

That is the profaneness Jeremiah says has “gone forth into all the land” from the prophets. Teaching prosperity and that the laws of God are done away produces adulterers, gangbangers, murderers and debauchery, and the land is full of adulterers because of it.
