precepts.label: Joel 3:1
precepts.why:
“Write thee all the words that I have spoken unto thee in a book.” That book is called the Bible today. Then pay attention: “For, lo, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah”.

Joel 3:1 confuses some brothers: “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem”. Read that alone and you think it means he is bringing us back into slavery. That is not what it means.

Go back to Jeremiah 30:3. Notice the same words, except Jeremiah explains them: “and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.” When he says he will bring again the captivity, he is speaking of bringing us back from captivity, not into captivity. Jeremiah explains Joel.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 9:2-3
precepts.why:
“We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace.” We are coming up on that moment now. And yet our people cheer the movies on Martin Luther King and Malcolm X. You may not agree with Martin's method, but how many of us would walk down the street knowing we would be beaten, jailed and have dogs sicced on us? Their stand ended Jim Crow, and in sixty years of that liberty, how have we used it? We shoot each other, besmirch one another and hate each other.

Jeremiah said, “Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them!” He wanted to leave black people. Why? “for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men. And they bend their tongues like their bow for lies”. Black people love to use their lips for lies.

“but they are not valiant for the truth upon the earth”. They are valiant in the movie theatre. They cheer on Nat Turner in Birth of a Nation, cheer on Malcolm X and Martin Luther King, cheer the resistance in The Hunger Games and Star Wars, but they do not have that spirit and do not have the balls to do what those men did. They would never have joined Malcolm or Martin, and many will not join us out of fear. Two young boys got shot in the face in Georgia, instigated by a gaggle of other black men who scattered like cockroaches and played innocent when the cops came. So-called revolutionary brothers on podcasts call us a cult while including homosexuality and transgenderism; they have never left the couch.

“for they proceed from evil to evil, and they know not me, saith the Lord.” That is why, in the time of Jacob's trouble, there is a voice of trembling and fear and not of peace.

thread.label: Jeremiah 30:8-11
thread.text: For it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord of hosts, that I will break his yoke from off thy neck, and will burst thy bonds, and strangers shall no more serve themselves of him:

classes.title: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.label: Hosea 3:4-5
precepts.why:
“In that day”, “I will break his yoke from off thy neck, and will burst thy bonds, and strangers shall no more serve themselves of him”: that's Christ's return. “But they shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.” Uh-oh. Did you notice? David is alive.

Hosea says the same: “For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim”. Many days without a king. “Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.”

We are returning now. We are seeking the Lord our God. And it is telling you David is going to be alive in these last days, in the latter days, when Israel returns. That is the day of Jeremiah 30, when the yoke is broken off our neck and the Lord raises David up unto us.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 1:11
precepts.why:
If David is alive in these last days, “David their king, whom I will raise up unto them”, why doesn't anyone know it? Solomon says: “There is no remembrance of former things; neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.”

David will not remember who he is, and neither do you. Our minds are wiped, everybody. We don't know who's who. That is why it says love your neighbour as you love yourself: you don't know who is who.

And that is a good thing. In the old school we used to say, oh, this one's David, and that caused a lot of partiality and a lot of problems. Don't do that. Don't try to guess who anybody is either. Little brother calling himself Samson: you don't know, brother. Just stop it. The Lord will raise up David; it is not ours to name him.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 34:23
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says Israel “shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.” Ezekiel says the same of the last days: “And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.”

One shepherd over the whole nation, and that shepherd is David. After Israel has abided many days without a king, the Lord himself sets David up over them, to feed them.

That is part of the promise that comes at the end of the exile and tribulation: the yoke broken from our neck, the strangers no longer serving themselves of us, Jacob returned to rest and quiet with none to make him afraid, and one shepherd, David, raised up over Israel under the Lord their God.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 9:22
precepts.why:
“though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee”. Why is he going to make an end of all nations? Ezra says it: “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain”.

All these nations were born in vain. In a movie they are the extras; they're not the stars of the movie. We are. And Esau is the villain, the antagonist, the bad guy.

But the stars are not spared from correction: “I will correct thee in measure, and will not leave thee altogether unpunished.” The Lord makes a full end of the nations, but only corrects Israel in measure. So “fear thou not, O my servant Jacob”. What he says will happen would make anyone afraid, and nobody wants to go through tribulation, so we increase our faith by reminding ourselves that this body is just a shell; the real us is within. He will save us from afar, and Jacob shall return and be in rest, and none shall make him afraid.

thread.label: Jeremiah 30:12-17
thread.text: For thus saith the Lord, Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous.

classes.title: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.label: Isaiah 1:4-6
precepts.why:
“Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous. There is none to plead thy cause, that thou mayest be bound up: thou hast no healing medicines.” None stands up on our behalf, and we have no healing medicine. Every Negro that just popped out of his mama's behind has a new idea for how to save black people, and it is always economics or voting. Those medicines don't work. What is the wound? Our sins. Isaiah says the same thing.

“Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.” We are that sinful nation, a people laden with sin; iniquity is sin. He calls us a seed of evildoers.

“Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more”. Our people get punished and revolt more and more against God. Then: “the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint”: the whole head of the Israelites is sick.

“From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.” Neither mollified with ointment means no medicine: there is no healing for us that way. That is Jeremiah's “no healing medicines.”

The only one who can save us is the Saviour, Jesus Christ, our master, our king. Yes, he is our rabbi, and rabbi means master. The wound Jeremiah calls incurable is incurable by any remedy of men; only the Lord can say, “I will restore health unto thee”.

precepts.label: Job 2:7
precepts.why:
What Isaiah and Jeremiah say of the nation is the same thing Job went through. People read Job and think that was only him, but Job's real life symbolizes the nation of Israel. This was the fifth judgment on Job: “So went Satan forth from the presence of the Lord, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.” Didn't we just read that in Isaiah 1? “From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it”.

Job's life is Deuteronomy 28. He lost his businesses, his family, everything. And “There is none to plead thy cause”: Job had friends who would not stand up on his behalf. They were always telling him he was wrong, evil, the devil. There was no cure; God had to intervene and heal Job. That is why the Lord sent Christ to heal the twelve tribes of Israel.

Even Job's wife turned on him in his darkest moment, when he had lost everything. That is how these black women do with us: in this state, the black woman turned on us.

But at the end of Job's life he was blessed. That is what is going to happen to us if we endure to the end: the incurable wound of Jeremiah 30 ends with “I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds”.

precepts.label: Leviticus 26:41
precepts.why:
“I have wounded thee with the wound of an enemy, with the chastisement of a cruel one, for the multitude of thine iniquity; because thy sins were increased.” Our sins are increased: the Houston rodeo, black men and women whoring themselves out, filthy and wicked, so bad a dress code had to be put in place; and in Delta State in Nigeria, a festival where women are openly raped in the streets. That is evil. Then: “because thy sins were increased, I have done these things unto thee”.

Moses said it would be so: “And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies”. God walked contrary to us because we kept breaking his laws, and he brought us into the land of our enemies. Then what we must do: “if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity”.

As we repent, we have to accept that God is right and we are wrong. We have always been wrong. God was just when he punished us. When your child plays in the street or with the light socket, you beat that behind, not because you hate him but so he learns he'll die playing in traffic or with electricity. Some talking doesn't do any good for some kids; you have to rile up on them so they know it's serious. That is what God did with us.

The three holy children did exactly this. In the midst of the fiery furnace, cast in because they would not worship Babylon's god, Azarias prayed: “Blessed art thou, O Lord God of our fathers”, “For thou art righteous in all the things that thou hast done to us: yea, true are all thy works, thy ways are right, and all thy judgments truth.” Then: “for according to truth and judgment didst thou bring all these things upon us because of our sins. For we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from thee”. Everything God has done to our people is justified, because we revolted against him. They said it because of what Moses said in Leviticus, and what happened to them is a reflection of what will happen to us.

Christianity has taught our people the opposite: to mock a God who got angry at his own people for worshipping a golden calf. But accepting the punishment is the way back, because the next verse is: “Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob”.

precepts.label: Luke 9:11
precepts.why:
“For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord”. The Lord is the only one who can restore health; that goes back to verses 12 and 13, “thou hast no healing medicines.” There is no magic voting right and no economic situation to save us.

Luke shows who the healer is: “And the people, when they knew it, followed him: and he received them, and spake unto them of the kingdom of God, and healed them that had need of healing.” Christ spake of the kingdom and healed them that had need of healing. He is the only one who can heal us of all these things. He is the Saviour; he is the physician.

That is how the incurable bruise of Jeremiah 30 is cured. Not by any medicine of man, but by the Lord who received the people, taught them the kingdom of God, and healed them.

precepts.label: Mark 2:17
precepts.why:
Christ is the physician: “When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick”. If you think you're good, that you know everything, you don't need the son of God, you don't need the Saviour.

You have to admit you're sick: that we are in the midst of sin, and that all we have done has been wrong. That is the same thing as accepting the punishment of our iniquity.

“I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” He did not call us righteous. He came for sinners. That is the healing Jeremiah promises Israel, whose “sorrow is incurable for the multitude of thine iniquity”. The sick nation is the one he came to heal.

The churches are the opposite: they say they don't need that Bible, they are already whole. Isaiah 65 shows them saying so, “I am holier than thou.” The ones who think themselves whole will not come to the physician.

precepts.label: Isaiah 65:1-5
precepts.why:
This goes with Christ saying he came not for the righteous but for sinners. “I am sought of them that asked not for me; I am found of them that sought me not”. Like the disciples, we didn't wake up one day as kids searching for the Lord of heaven and earth. The word was introduced to us and woke us up.

“I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name.” We are called African-Americans, Haitians, Jamaicans, Puerto Ricans. That is a nation not called by his name.

“I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts”. We are that rebellious people, walking in Christianity and Islam, our people following their own thoughts in these religions. “A people that provoketh me to anger continually to my face; that sacrificeth in gardens, and burneth incense upon altars of brick”: the churches and mosques. Then: “which eat swine’s flesh, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels”. You know that's the church: there was always a swine fest at the end, pig feet and all of that; possum soup, turtle soup.

“Which say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou.” That is what the churches say to the Israelites on the street preaching: stand by yourself, I don't need no black Jesus, I'm washed in the blood of Jesus, I'm water baptized, I'm holier than thou. “These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burneth all the day.” God can't stand them.

That is the people Jeremiah calls an Outcast, “This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after.” Those who think they are whole push away the physician; the sick who admit it are the ones he heals.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:24
precepts.why:
How does the Lord restore health unto us? “Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes ye were healed.”

Christ bare our sins in his own body on the tree, which is the cross; the cross was made from a tree. We, being dead to sin, should live unto righteousness. We are healed by Christ's punishment, his crucifixion.

That is the prophecy of Jeremiah 30:17: “For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord”. How? When he sent Christ to die on the cross. By his stripes we are healed.

Then: “because they called thee an Outcast, saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after”. Outcast means African-American: made-up names they gave our race. Nobody gives a damn about you, blacks and Latinos; no man seeks after you. But the Lord does. The wound no medicine could close is healed by his stripes, and then “all they that devour thee shall be devoured; and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity”: every one of them, not some.

thread.label: Jeremiah 30:18-24
thread.text: Thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have mercy on his dwellingplaces; and the city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof.

classes.title: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.label: Numbers 1:52
precepts.why:
Just before this, the Lord says, “I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds”, and that healing came when he sent Christ to die on the cross: by his stripes we are healed. “because they called thee an Outcast”: outcast means African-American, made-up names for our race, a Zion “whom no man seeketh after”. Nobody gives a damn about blacks and Latinos. Then: “Behold, I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents”.

What are Jacob’s tents? “And the children of Israel shall pitch their tents, every man by his own camp, and every man by his own standard, throughout their hosts.” Every man by his own camp: Judah is going to be with Judah, Ephraim with Ephraim, Benjamin with Benjamin. That is the restructuring, the restoration of a nation.

And every man by his own standard: Judah had the standard of the lion, Benjamin the wolf, Naphtali the deer, Ephraim the bull. When the Lord brings again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, all of this is being restored again: the tribes set back in order, each under its own standard.

precepts.label: Numbers 24:5
precepts.why:
All of this is being restored again: “How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel!”

The tents of Jacob, pitched every man by his own camp and his own standard, are goodly in the eyes of the Lord. These are the same tents Jeremiah speaks of when the Lord says, “I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have mercy on his dwellingplaces”.

So the promise of Jeremiah 30:18 is that the goodly order Israel had in the wilderness, the tribes camped in their tents, is brought back out of captivity. What was taken captive, the Lord returns, and Jacob’s tents are goodly again.

precepts.label: Psalms 78:55
precepts.why:
“He cast out the heathen also before them, and divided them an inheritance by line, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.” He cast out the heathen before us, divided the land to the tribes by line, and set each tribe in its tents.

That is what it means for the Lord to bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents. The tents of Jacob are the tribes of Israel dwelling in their own inheritance, and to bring them again is to cast out the heathen once more and set the twelve tribes back in their inheritance.

Then Jeremiah goes on: “and the city shall be builded upon her own heap”, because that land is going to be destroyed and built again, and the tribes dwell in it again as the Lord made them to dwell at the first.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:10-13
precepts.why:
“the city shall be builded upon her own heap, and the palace shall remain after the manner thereof.” It says heap because that land is going to be destroyed and built again; the palace means the temple that is going to be built. Isaiah 60 goes with Jeremiah 30:18.

“And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.” The strangers build the walls when Jerusalem is built again on her own heap.

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary”. That is the palace. “and I will make the place of my feet glorious”: the Lord is going to make Jerusalem glorious again.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:21-22
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says, “I will multiply them, and they shall not be few; I will also glorify them, and they shall not be small.” That is why we go to Isaiah 60.

“Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.” Then: “A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the Lord will hasten it in his time.” We shall not be small.

There is more in that verse than what it is saying on the surface. Look at the little bodies we have now. We are not going to have these little bodies. We are not going to be all frail and skinny, and the little fat brothers are not going to be like that either. The Lord multiplies and glorifies Israel, in number and in body.

precepts.label: Isaiah 1:25-26
precepts.why:
“Their children also shall be as aforetime, and their congregation shall be established before me”. The Lord is going to return it all back to the way it was.

Isaiah says the same: “And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin:” “And I will restore thy judges as at the first”. He purges the dross out of Israel and restores the judges as at the first, the way it was in the beginning.

That is what Jeremiah 30:20 is saying: our children as aforetime, our congregation established before the Lord, everything returned to our glorious state. And it answers verse 21 too, “their nobles shall be of themselves”: our own judges, restored as at the first.

precepts.label: Zechariah 12:7-8
precepts.why:
“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” These are the same tents of Jacob that the Lord brings again out of captivity.

“In that day shall the Lord defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David”. The feeble Israelites are going to be like King David. “and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of the Lord before them.” The house of David is the 144,000; they shall be as God.

That is our children being as aforetime and our glorious state being restored: the Lord saving Judah’s tents first, and the weakest of Israel made as strong as David.

precepts.label: Psalms 72:4
precepts.why:
At the bottom of Jeremiah 30:20 the Lord says, “I will punish all that oppress them.” He said all, not some. All that have oppressed us shall be punished.

The precept is Psalms 72: “He shall judge the poor of the people, he shall save the children of the needy, and shall break in pieces the oppressor.” Break in pieces the oppressor.

There is no coming together and joining with the oppressor. The Lord did not say he would reconcile Israel with the ones who oppressed them; he said, I am going to break them. That is the punishment of all that oppress us.

precepts.label: Matthew 2:6
precepts.why:
“And their nobles shall be of themselves, and their governor shall proceed from the midst of them”. Our nobles are going to come from our own people. We are not going to have nobles of another race, like the mayor they have now in New York, Mamdani. That is not our people.

Christ is our governor, and he came from the midst of us: “And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.” That is Christ right there.

So the governor that proceeds from the midst of Israel is Christ, born in Bethlehem of Judah, ruling his people Israel. “I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach unto me”, and then, “ye shall be my people, and I will be your God.”

precepts.label: Hebrews 8:8-10
precepts.why:
Paul quotes this straight from Jeremiah: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah”. Christians avoid that, because when you ask them who the new covenant is for, it tells you crystal clear right there who it was for: the house of Israel and the house of Judah. He separates us like that because there was a split into two kingdoms, and when he says Israel right there, he means all 12 tribes.

“Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt”. That was the old covenant, animal sacrifice. The 12 tribes are the bride and God is the husband. “because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord”: meaning we went into slavery.

“I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people”. This is kingdom, the same promise Jeremiah gave. So this is the answer to replacement theology, the answer to supersessionism. The new covenant was never given to a church that took Israel's place; it was made with the same Israel that broke the first one.

And Jeremiah goes on to seal it: if the ordinances of the sun, the moon and the stars depart, then the seed of Israel ceases from being a nation. They have not departed, so the 12 tribes are still here to this day. Even in Paul's time the 12 tribes were there, yet Christians cannot point them out in the New Testament and say they are lost. It's all a lie. This is where Paul was getting it from.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 4:13
precepts.why:
Paul writes to Timothy: “The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.” The books means the books of Isaiah, the books of Jeremiah, the books of Micah. It is not talking about books about how to braid your hair.

“but especially the parchments”: parchments are writing papers. Paul would read the Old Testament books and base his epistles on those writings. That is why Hebrews 8 carries the new covenant word for word out of Jeremiah 31: Paul was reading Jeremiah and writing from it.

So the New Testament does not replace the Old; it is built on it. When Jeremiah says the new covenant is with the house of Israel and the house of Judah, and that the seed of Israel will not cease from being a nation while the sun, moon and stars stand, Paul was taking that from the prophets he carried with him. The church did not get a new covenant of its own; Paul was teaching Israel's covenant out of Israel's books.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:41
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them; for they shall go into captivity.” That is slavery. It is a different thing from the servant of Leviticus 25, a poor Hebrew brother who sold himself to his brother for six years and went out free and furnished in the year of release. Christianity used the words servants, obey your masters, to make us think the Bible's servant was chattel slavery; it is not. Deuteronomy 28:41 is the captivity that came as the curse.

It is what Jeremiah 34 brought on us. Zedekiah made all the people covenant to let every Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free, “that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Jew his brother.” They obeyed, “But afterward they turned, and caused the servants and the handmaids, whom they had let go free, to return”. This is some negro stuff: the elites among us, those who had money, wanted to keep our own people in continuous servitude. So the Lord proclaimed a liberty for us “to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine”, to be “removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.” That is Deuteronomy 28. Babylon had just left, and God brought them right back. That is the result of hating our brothers and not loving our neighbour as ourselves. Even after Persia set us free, in Nehemiah 5 the nobles did the same thing again.

After the Persian captivity came the Greek. 1 Maccabees 3:41: “the merchants of the country, hearing the fame of them, took silver and gold very much, with servants, and came into the camp to buy the children of Israel for slaves”, and “a power also of Syria and of the land of the Philistines joined themselves unto them.” We look at the slave auction and think it is the first time this ever happened. No, the Greeks did this too, and other nations helped them.

2 Maccabees 5 shows it: Jason, an Israelite, a treasonous negro, “slew his own citizens without mercy”, treating his countrymen like enemies to please the Greeks, and he died cast out, with none to mourn him. “But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done” (Colossians 3:25). Then the king took the city: “fourscore thousand, whereof forty thousand were slain in the conflict; and no fewer sold than slain.” Apollonius was sent “to slay all those that were in their best age, and to sell the women and the younger sort”. The best age, the movers and shakers who make a nation thrive; take them and leave the old and feeble, and you destroy the nation, the same complaint made about the colonialists.

So the sons and daughters we begat went into captivity, sold by the Greeks, and after them by Rome, whose foothold came when Pompey captured Jerusalem in 65 BC, and the slave markets were full of black Jewish slaves. That is where breaking the year of release led.

“And Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Beth–el their confidence.” Chemosh was their god; Moab always had a lot of gods, but Chemosh was the favorite. Notice it says the house of Israel, the northern kingdom, was ashamed of Bethel. What is it talking about?

“Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” Two calves, and our people were worshipping them. “And he set the one in Beth–el, and the other put he in Dan. And this thing became a sin: for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan.”

“And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi.” Then “Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah”. precepts.label: 2 Esdras 15:56-63
precepts.why:
Jeremiah says Moab “shall be destroyed from being a people, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord.” Ezra shows the same judgment and why it comes: “Like as thou hast done unto my chosen, saith the Lord, even so shall God do unto thee, and shall deliver thee into mischief”. “Thy children shall die of hunger, and thou shalt fall through the sword: thy cities shall be broken down, and all thine shall perish with the sword in the field. They that be in the mountains shall die of hunger, and eat their own flesh, and drink their own blood”. That is cannibalism. They that be in the mountains are the ones in those bunkers, little bunkers, big bunkers, all kinds of bunkers. Everybody thinks they have a plan for when Armageddon takes place and all nations fight: we will go into the bunkers, we will survive there, we will live there for a century. No, that is not going to happen.

“And in the passage they shall rush on the idle city, and shall destroy some portion of thy land, and consume part of thy glory, and shall return to Babylon that was destroyed.” The idle city is China. And it shows America is not finished yet. Although the country, Babylon the great, the United States of America, gets wiped out, her military is not finished. That is why America has over 800 military bases worldwide, and it is the only country that has that. Russia doesn't have that, China doesn't have that. Their home base is finished, but they have bases everywhere, and that is how they will successfully get China; then they return and see Babylon destroyed.

“Thy children shall they carry away captive, and, look, what thou hast, they shall spoil it, and mar the beauty of thy face.” Those are prisoners of war. It is the same as Jeremiah, where the mighty men’s hearts in Moab are “as the heart of a woman in her pangs”, very fearful, scared and afraid: “thy sons are taken captives, and thy daughters captives.” Whatever China says in its pride, God says it shall not be so. precepts.why:
Jeremiah ends the judgment of Moab with “Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days, saith the Lord. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.” Although it happened with Nebuchadnezzar, God said it is going to happen again in the latter days. There is no slackness of the last plagues and judgments, and no swiftness of the first. It is a steady flow, a steady flow of judgment upon all nations. thread.label: Jeremiah 49:1-2
thread.text: Concerning the Ammonites, thus saith the Lord; Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir? why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?

precepts.label: Amos 1:13-15
precepts.why:
“Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir? why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?” Historically, when Gad was moved out of the land, Ammon moved their rusty butts into our land and dwelt in our cities. Amos tells what Ammon did to get there: “For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border.”

When they caught our people, they ripped up the women with child. They hung them upside down, just like the white man did to us, cut their stomachs so the baby fell out, and crushed the babies. That is what the Bible says they did, and why: they wanted to enlarge their border and take over our lands. They slaughtered Gad. God says, I'm not forgiving you for that; I'm not letting you slide.

“But I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall devour the palaces thereof, with shouting in the day of battle, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind.” Rabbah is the city of Jeremiah 49:2, where the Lord will cause “an alarm of war” to be heard. A day of battle is coming, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind: that's the Lord.

“And their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together, saith the Lord.” Put the leader of North Korea, Kim Jong-un, on the screen. Whether it is that particular man or not, whoever is the leader in the land of Ammon at that time is going to be a prisoner of war. That is what the prophecy says, so look for it.

precepts.label: Romans 8:17
precepts.why:
“then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the Lord.” What does that mean? Romans 8 jumps right to it: “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.”

We are joint-heirs with Christ. Ammon made itself heir to Gad, inheriting his cities while Israel was carried away. But Israel is the heir of God, and in that day Israel shall be heir unto them that took his inheritance.

The condition is that we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified together. The suffering comes first, the inheritance after, just as Gad lost his cities and the Lord promises to give them back.

precepts.label: Obadiah 1:19
precepts.why:
The prophets show whose the land will be: “And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau”: we're going to own Esau. “and they of the plain the Philistines”: we're going to own them as well. “and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria”: we're going to get our lands back. “and Benjamin shall possess Gilead.”

The tribe of Benjamin, God foretells, will dwell in the land of Gilead. That is the land of Gad and Reuben and half of Manasseh, the same Gilead whose women with child Ammon ripped up to enlarge their border.

So the prophecy says God is going to give that land in the future to Benjamin. That is Israel being “heir unto them that were his heirs”: the land Ammon took is given back to Israel.

precepts.label: Numbers 32:29
precepts.why:
Before Obadiah's prophecy, the history of the land: when we entered the land, Moses already had it mapped out for us. “If the children of Gad and the children of Reuben will pass with you over Jordan, every man armed to battle, before the Lord, and the land shall be subdued before you; then ye shall give them the land of Gilead for a possession.”

So you notice: Gad and Reuben, that was to be their land. Gilead was Gad's by the word of Moses. That is why Jeremiah asks, “why then doth their king inherit Gad”: the land was Israel's possession, given before the Lord, and Ammon had no right to it.

precepts.label: Numbers 32:39
precepts.why:
“And the children of Machir the son of Manasseh went to Gilead, and took it, and dispossessed the Amorite which was in it.” So you had Gad, Reuben and Manasseh in that land. But in the prophecy of Obadiah, God says Benjamin shall possess Gilead.

On the ancient map you can see Manasseh, Gad under them, and Reuben under Gad, and right next to Gad was Ammon. When Gad was moved out of the land by the Assyrian captivity, Ammon moved right in. That is what Jeremiah 49:1 says: “their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities.”

After Nebuchadnezzar began to move them out, then the Persians, then the Greeks, the Arabs got the land of Ammon; the Greeks made a deal with them, as the book of the Maccabees tells. On the modern map it is spelled Amman, and that whole area is what America calls Jordan today. It is all Arab land, but it was Ammon and Moab's land, and before that it was Gilead, Israel's land.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:64
precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

We were scattered everywhere, and that includes, as we are finding out, China and Japan. The paintings from Japan in the 1400s and 1500s show the black faces, and the black faces are slaves, brought over by the Portuguese and Spanish. In ancient China the Kunlun, African slaves, were given as tribute gifts during the Tang dynasty, and slavery peaked under the Tang and Song dynasties. The Portuguese brought enslaved Africans to Macau in large numbers in the 1500s, where they formed the core of its defense and defeated the Dutch in the Battle of Macau in 1622.

You don't learn this in school, and you definitely ain't going to learn it in Sunday school. They keep it secret and hidden. We thought these people were our friends; they had us as slaves too. That is why no nation wants to give us reparations: all nations got to pay.

This is how Israel came to be among all people from one end of the earth to the other, and why the question stands: “Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir?” The Lord answers that Israel shall be heir again.

precepts.label: Lamentations 5:10
precepts.why:
Lamentations 4:7 shows Israel before: “Her Nazarites were purer than snow, they were whiter than milk”. Whiter means holier, more righteous. “more ruddy in body than rubies”: ruddy in body means healthy in body, strong and precious. Then Babylon came, cut off the food supply and starved them out. Verse 7 is the before and verse 8 is the after: “Their visage is blacker than a coal; they are not known in the streets: their skin cleaveth to their bones; it is withered, it is become like a stick.” Their faces could not be recognised from verse 7; they went from ruddy in body to skin hanging off their bones.

Lamentations 5:10 says it plainly: “Our skin was black like an oven because of the terrible famine.” What caused the famine? The Babylonians surrounded us, besieged us, cut off our food and water supply, and starved us for years before conquering us entirely. Through starvation we got darker, blacker than a coal.

Why darker? When black folks go through a famine and are starved, there is a thing called hyperpigmentation: they get darker. When white folks get starved, they get lighter; they don't get darker than a coal, they get more pinker than a pig. A plant has its own melanin, chlorophyll, that gives it the green colour; deprive it of water and sunlight and it turns brown and withers, like the Jews here. They were starved and got darker than they already were.

They say it is only talking about the condition the people were in. Yes, it is a condition. When they call us black people today, they mean our condition too, because the black man is the lowest people on this earth today, and the Chinese and the Arabs are above us. But it also means our skin colour. So is our skin symbolic too? “Our skin was black like an oven”, and ovens are black. Stop playing with us.

We bring scripture, history, records from the 1600s, even science, and still they won't accept it, while all the white man has to say is he's white and they say praise Jesus. That is white makes right. The Bible alone is enough: the Israelites were black, and the famine made them blacker.

precepts.label: Psalms 23:4
precepts.why:
Ezekiel was set down “in the midst of the valley which was full of bones”, and they were “very dry.” A valley full of bones is a graveyard. Very dry means no nourishment, no understanding, no water. David names that same valley: “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.”

That was a rap lyric, huh? Shame on you. That is in the Bible. It is not Coolio and it is not Tupac. The world took the words of the famous Christian prayer and made a song of them, but the valley of the shadow of death is a real place in the scripture.

It is the same darkness Job spoke about in Job 10:21 and 22. It is the same land Baruch spoke of earlier, where our people wax old and are defiled with the dead in a strange land. And it is the same place Isaiah speaks of when the Lord comes to bring out “them that sit in darkness out of the prison house.” The valley of dry bones, the valley of the shadow of death, the land of darkness and the prison house are all one place: the lands of our captivity.

So the valley Ezekiel walked round about is where our people are today, dead and dry in a strange land. Yet even there the one who walks with the Lord fears no evil, because the Lord is with him, and it is the Lord who will bring those bones to life.

precepts.label: Proverbs 21:16
precepts.why:
The bones in the valley were “very dry”: no nourishment, no understanding, no water. Solomon shows how a people come to be counted among the dead: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.”

That is our people. When we got conquered and overthrown and colonised by our oppressors, over the course of time up until now, we wandered out of understanding, and now we are the congregation of the dead. It is the same as waxing old and being defiled with the dead in a strange land.

We are a spiritually dead people. Alive and well on the outside, but inside we are dead: destroyed, divisive, self-defeating, self-hating, self-detrimental. That is why the bones are dry.

So when the Lord asks, “Son of man, can these bones live?”, the answer is the understanding we wandered away from. Ezekiel is told, “O ye dry bones, hear the word of the Lord.” What must be brought to these bones is the word of God, not the word of some hustler, some ex-pimp, some pastor, preacher or rapper. The words of the Bible. The breath is the word of God, and only that understanding can bring the congregation of the dead back to life.

thread.text: And the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron: forasmuch as iron breaketh in pieces and subdueth all things: and as iron that breaketh all these, shall it break in pieces and bruise.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 12:10-11
precepts.why:
The fourth kingdom “shall be strong as iron”. It began with Rome, and America and Europe are the extension of Rome, the iron of the feet. Now Sirach: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” Who is that iron? The fourth kingdom that rules the earth today, Europe and America, the white man.

Who is your enemy? In the 1950s you understood who your enemy was. In the 1800s you understood. Forty or fifty years ago you understood. God says never trust him. As iron rusts, the rust will always appear again, and that is his wickedness. Even though he said, we changed, we gave you civil rights, we are not oppressing you anymore, you see the wickedness coming back now, and they are taking it all back. His kingdom is made of iron, and that wickedness will always return.

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him”. He acts like he loves black people and cares about them. Beware of that iron. “and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass, and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.” If you are righteous and have wisdom, you see all his wickedness as in a looking glass: look at their history. They are a genocidal race of people, and you cannot get justice from them. Look at Palestine, Lebanon and the Congo, hundreds of thousands dead, while the ones running the courts don't stop it. This whole system is unjust.

That is why Daniel says the iron shall “mingle themselves with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave one to another”. After 1945 Britain opened itself to the people of its colonies, and after civil rights everybody started coming to America. The white man said he changed, and brought the same people he colonized and destroyed to live among him. Decades later they say they should never have let any of them in. The white man did not change; he is the same person, his rust has not been wiped away, and white people and everybody else are not going to get along.

precepts.label: Revelation 13:6-8
precepts.why:
The last empire, the dragon with seven heads and ten horns, has attributes like a lion, which was ancient Babylon, and Daniel 3 is Babylon setting up its golden image. You may read that and say it was back then. But evangelical leaders just gathered at Trump National Doral in Miami, and again at Mar-a-Lago, to bless and dedicate a 22 foot gold leaf statue of Trump, Don Colossus, with his fist raised. Pastor Mark Burns led the dedication and said it was not a golden calf, the pastors prayed over the image, and Trump called in to thank them. You see the comparison with Daniel 3.

Revelation 13 shows who is behind that image. “And he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven.” This is the white man as Rome, the Roman Catholic Church, the mother of all Christian denominations, blaspheming the name of the Lord.

“And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them”. The twelve tribes of Israel are the saints. This white man orchestrated war against us under Pope Nicholas V, and he overcame us and enslaved us. Pastor Burns doesn't have a clue: these people made war against us and enslaved us. “and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations”: that is how the white race became the dominant race on the planet.

“And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him”. Everybody on this earth worships the white man as God, as Jesus, as the angels, as the Jews. Show a Muslim or a Buddhist that image and ask whose it is, and they will say Jesus, Christ. Some of your mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers and children worship him.

Even the show The Boys patterns it: the Homelander character, with blonde hair like Trump, becomes president, mixes evangelical Christians into politics, and says his destiny is not serving the Lord but being the Lord, the Messiah, the saviour of the world. The thing that has been is that which shall be. Nebuchadnezzar set up a one world religion with his image, and it is the same thing they are trying to do today. What we read in Daniel 3 we see coming to pass.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 1:41-50
precepts.why:
That was Babylon; now the Greek captivity, to show that this judgment is like a ring. “Moreover king Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom, that all should be one people, And every one should leave his laws: so all the heathen agreed according to the commandment of the king.” It is the same as Nebuchadnezzar calling all people, nations and languages to fall down before one image.

“Yea, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.” Just like we saw with Pastor Mark Burns, praying over a golden statue.

The king sent letters “that they should follow the strange laws of the land”, forbid the offerings in the temple, “profane the sabbaths and festival days”, “Set up altars, and groves, and chapels of idols, and sacrifice swine’s flesh, and unclean beasts”, and leave their children uncircumcised. Why? “To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances.” That was the purpose of setting up these things: that we would forget God's law.

“And whosoever would not do according to the commandment of the king, he said, he should die.” It is the fiery furnace of Babylon again. The same idolatry we read about in Babylon happened in Greece, and it is going to continue. Don't think America is absolved from this; we are seeing elements of it now. Some of you have been swooned to sleep, thinking nothing is ever going to happen here, and now you see a big gold statue set up and say, well, he hasn't made anybody pray to it yet.

So stand like Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego: “But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.” They knew you cannot force the Lord to deliver you, and that the body is temporary but the spirit lives on. These events will occur again, and these are the things we have to learn and put in our hearts, minds and souls.

precepts.label: Revelation 13:2
precepts.why:
John saw “a beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns, and upon his heads the name of blasphemy.” Blasphemy means wicked lies against God, and those lies are written on the heads of this beast. Then he describes it: “And the beast which I saw was like unto a leopard, and his feet were as the feet of a bear, and his mouth as the mouth of a lion”. This is not the old kingdoms themselves; it is a beast rising in the last days that carries the attributes of all three.

The leopard is Greece. Daniel saw “another, like a leopard, which had upon the back of it four wings of a fowl; the beast had also four heads”. The four wings are four armies, the Greek military split four ways, and the four heads are the four generals: Ptolemy, Lysimachus, Cassander and Seleucus.

The bear is the Medo-Persian Empire. It “raised up itself on one side”: Persia rose up over the Medes and became the greater. The “three ribs in the mouth of it” are Egypt, Ethiopia and the Sabeans (that is Somalia), the three nations named in Isaiah 45:14: “The labour of Egypt, and merchandise of Ethiopia and of the Sabeans, men of stature”. The same chapter opens, “Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus”: God raised up Cyrus the Persian to conquer those three nations and take over the world.

The lion is Babylon, the first beast of Daniel 7:4, “like a lion, and had eagle’s wings”. The wings were plucked when Babylon put down Assyria. It was “made stand upon the feet as a man, and a man’s heart was given to it”: great wisdom was given to Babylon.

So the beast of Revelation 13 has elements of Greece, elements of Persia and Media, of Cyrus and those rulers, and the mouth of ancient Babylon. “and the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority”: Satan gave this kingdom its power and great authority.

That is why the lion of Daniel 7:4 matters today. When you read about Babylon, Persia and Media and the Greeks, certain things in that history are being fulfilled in these last days. Everybody doesn't know that. And the head “wounded to death” is Rome, wounded in the year 193 AD.

precepts.label: Genesis 1:14
precepts.why:
Revelation 13:5 says “there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies”, and Daniel 7:25 says the same: “he shall speak great words against the most High, and shall wear out the saints of the most High”. Revelation 13:7 adds that “it was given unto him to make war with the saints”. The great words are things like the image of Cesare Borgia as Christ, a white man dying for the sins of everybody on the planet, getting dumped in the water to be saved, Lent, Christmas, December 25th and the rest. To wear out the saints is slavery.

“and think to change times and laws”. They changed the time with daylight saving time. They moved the beginning of the year from spring to January. Genesis 1:14 was read to show something else they changed: “Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years”.

Leviticus 23 shows what the seasons are for: “These are the feasts of the Lord, even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.” The Sabbath is listed first, and it is all year round. Then come the seasonal holidays: Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, in the spring; the feast of unleavened bread on the fifteenth; Pentecost, counting fifty days; the blowing of trumpets on the first day of the seventh month, the seventh new moon celebration; the day of atonement on the tenth of the seventh month; and the feast of tabernacles on the fifteenth.

Sirach 43:6: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.” The declaration of times is the high holy days. The lights God set in the heaven keep his calendar, and that is the calendar the beast thought to change.

precepts.label: Genesis 1:16
precepts.why:
“And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.” The greater light is the sun and the lesser light is the moon. Notice the wording: great lights. He did not make a quarter moon or half a light. He made two great lights. What they call the full moon today is actually the new moon, and many cultures, like the Maya, hold full moon gatherings. Deuteronomy 33:14 speaks of Joseph's land and “the precious things put forth by the moon”, things that come out when the moon is at its peak, like the coquí frogs that come out under the moonlight in the islands where Ephraim and Manasseh dwell.

Sirach 43 goes on: “From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection. The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing, being an instrument of the armies above, shining in the firmament of heaven”. The word month comes from moon. Every feast starts at the new moon in its brightness, because that is how it was in the kingdom. The armies above are the armies of Revelation 19: “the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses”.

The moon is “a sign of the world”. The full moon stands for when we were in our full power and understanding. As it wanes and goes dark, that is us going into captivity, into full darkness, and when it comes back to fullness, that is us going back into our glory, back into the kingdom. Isaiah 60:2: “the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people”. When you see the dark moon, that is what it represents: we lost our heritage, and darkness covers the world.

Psalm 82 shows why: “How long will ye judge unjustly”, and because of it, “all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” Even the lights are out of course because of our sins. The seasons are out of order, and if the Sabbath comes every seven days, a month should have twenty-eight days. Isaiah 30:26 shows the kingdom: “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” The sun has no phases, so in the kingdom the moon will not go back into darkness. Binding up the breach is gathering the twelve tribes again, as Amos 9:11 says: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”.

precepts.label: Psalms 91:1-12
precepts.why:
Daniel says “there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered”. What makes this tribulation different is World War III and Armageddon, and Psalm 91 shows how Israel is delivered in the midst of it.

“He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.” The secret place of the Most High is the Bible.

“Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day; Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.” The arrow that flieth by day is the missile, the destruction that wasteth at noonday.

“A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee. Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.” And “he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways. They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.”

That is the deliverance of the Israelites in the midst of Armageddon: thy people delivered, every one found written in the book, not all nations. It is the same psalm Satan twisted when he told Christ to jump from the pinnacle of the temple.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 15:37-45
precepts.why:
Daniel's “time of trouble, such as never was” is World War III and Armageddon. Ezra shows it: “And there shall be great fearfulness and trembling upon earth: and they that see the wrath shall be afraid, and trembling shall come upon them.”

“And then shall there come great storms from the south, and from the north, and another part from the west. And strong winds shall arise from the east”: storms from all four winds.

They “shall pour out over every high and eminent place an horrible star, Fire, and hail, and flying swords”. The horrible star is the ICBM, and the flying swords are the missiles. “And they shall break down the cities and walls, mountains and hills, trees of the wood, and grass of the meadows, and their corn.”

“And they shall go stedfastly unto Babylon, and make her afraid.” Babylon is America. And “then shall the dust and smoke go up unto the heaven, and all they that be about her shall bewail her”, just as Revelation 18 says the kings and merchants of the earth will bewail her. That is the time of trouble in which Daniel's people, every one written in the book, shall be delivered.

precepts.label: Luke 4:9-12
precepts.why:
Psalm 91 promises the deliverance of Israel in the time of trouble: “He shall give his angels charge over thee”. Satan used that same psalm on Christ: “And he brought him to Jerusalem, and set him on a pinnacle of the temple, and said unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down from hence”.

“For it is written, He shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee: And in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.” Satan twisted the psalm into a dare, telling Christ to jump.

“And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.” Christ answered that way because the psalm is not a dare to test God. It is about the deliverance of Israel in the midst of Armageddon, when a thousand fall at our side and ten thousand at our right hand, and the angels bear us up.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:11-13
precepts.why:
Daniel says “at that time thy people shall be delivered”. John shows the order of it: “And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.” That standing up is now.

“And they heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them.” Between the standing up and the deliverance, John left out the tribulation, World War III and Armageddon; the precepts supply it. Tribulation has to come, then World War III, then Armageddon, when Christ comes in the midst of World War III.

“And the same hour was there a great earthquake, and the tenth part of the city fell, and in the earthquake were slain of men seven thousand: and the remnant were affrighted, and gave glory to the God of heaven.” A great destruction.

The Israelites who want to invest in airplanes and boats to get out do not believe the angels are coming. Come up hither is the deliverance: the angels bear us up, as Psalm 91 says.

precepts.label: Daniel 12:6-7
precepts.why:
Hosea says the children of Israel “shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod”. Daniel 12 gives the time frame for it. “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?” The wonders are our people being destroyed, enslaved and colonized, being without a king, without a prince, without an ephod.

“it shall be for a time, times, and an half”. A time is a hundred years; times is two hundred, three hundred in all; and an half makes 350 years. “and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.” Within those 350 years we were totally destroyed. All that power was gone from us; we forgot who we are, and we even forgot our nationality.

When we fled Jerusalem in 70 AD, was our power destroyed? Our country was destroyed, but we went to Africa and built cities there, and the ten tribes were set up on this side of the world doing their thing too. We still had governments, we still had kings over us, and we still knew we were the children of Israel. It was within the slave trade and colonization that the power of the holy people was scattered.

That is the many days without a king: without political sovereignty, when Europe colonized Ghana, Nigeria, Angola, Senegal, Papua New Guinea and the Congo, and when the transatlantic slave trade took us. It is without an image: our minds destroyed until the sisters in Africa bleach their skin and put on weaves, because worshipping the God of your oppressor destroys the way you look at yourself. The same curses fell on our people all over Africa, like the Mau Mau in Kenya, tortured in British camps and paid less than 4,000 pounds each. That is why I don't want no damn reparations.

precepts.label: Daniel 12:11
precepts.why:
Daniel 12 gives the time frame for when our people would be without a king, without an image, and without a sacrifice, as Hosea 3:4 says. Verse 11 reads: “And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.”

The daily sacrifice taken away is Hosea's “without a sacrifice”. Without the sacrifice, the image and the ephod, all our religious infrastructure and spiritual guidance was stripped away, and there was no priest to guide us and tell us what God needs us to do. The white man came in, whipped us, taught us white Jesus and his lies, and forced it down our throats in Africa. After he brought the slaves over here, he went to Africa and destroyed them there, until the people in Africa don't even know that we in the Caribbean and America are the same people.

So from the taking away of the sacrifice, the days are counted, and the question Daniel asked, “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?”, is answered with a set time. That goes back to the yoke of iron upon thy neck until thou have been destroyed: it did not just happen to us over here, it happened to our people in Africa, and the scattering of the holy people runs its appointed course.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 21:16
precepts.why:
Joel says the nations “have scattered among the nations, and parted my land”, “cast lots for my people”, and he names who: “O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine”. The Zidonians are Canaanites, Hamites, and the coasts of Palestine are the Arabs. “The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border.” This is nothing new. They did it before, in the days of an evil king named Jehoram.

Jehoram “walked in the way of the kings of Israel”, and in his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah and made themselves a king, “because he had forsaken the Lord God of his fathers.” Because of Jehoram’s disobedience and wickedness, God raised up enemies against him.

“Moreover the Lord stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines, and of the Arabians, that were near the Ethiopians”. The Philistines: that is Tyre and Zidon, the Hamites. And the Arabians, near the other Hamites. “And they came up into Judah, and brake into it, and carried away all the substance that was found in the king’s house, and his sons also, and his wives; so that there was never a son left him, save Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.”

So the Hamites and the Arabs got together and stole his wives and his kids. It is their common nature to do that: they steal people. That is the same pair Joel names, and the records say it plainly: slavery in Africa was due to raids of Arabs and Hamites on Negro communities. The Hamite, the Arab and the white man worked together removing us far from our border, and the land is parted today between the Israelis and the Arabs. That is why God will plead with the nations in the valley of Jehoshaphat for his people.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 8:1
precepts.why:
“Woe to them that are at ease in Zion, and trust in the mountain of Samaria”. At ease in Zion: that is the southern kingdom. Trust in the mountain of Samaria: that is the northern kingdom. How do we know Zion is Judah’s Jerusalem?

“Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the chief of the fathers of the children of Israel, unto king Solomon in Jerusalem, that they might bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which is Zion.” The city of David, which is Zion. So Jerusalem was also called Zion.

So Amos is speaking a woe to both houses at once: Judah at ease in Zion, and the northern kingdom trusting in Samaria. And he tells them both what is coming: “I abhor the excellency of Jacob, and hate his palaces: therefore will I deliver up the city with all that is therein.” All twelve tribes were going off, so the southern kingdom was going to get it, and the northern kingdom too.

precepts.label: John 4:20-24
precepts.why:
Amos set Zion and the mountain of Samaria against each other, and Christ speaks to the same divide with the Samaritan woman. “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”: that was Mount Gerizim. “and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship”: y’all Jews say that.

“Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.” Why? Because 70 AD was coming; Rome was going to destroy all the remaining Israelites.

“Ye worship ye know not what”: you, northern kingdom, don’t understand what you are worshipping, because the northern kingdom went into idolatry. “we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.” Salvation comes from Judah.

What was he letting her know? The temple was going to be destroyed, the Israelites would go into captivity, and you would have to deal with the Lord one on one, with no more priests intervening for you: “the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth”. Neither Samaria’s mountain nor Zion would stand; both houses would go captive, as Amos said.

precepts.label: Psalms 76:1
precepts.why:
“In Judah is God known: his name is great in Israel.” Christ told the Samaritan woman “salvation is of the Jews”, and the psalm agrees: in Judah is God known.

That is why Christ came out of Judah. Salvation comes from Judah. He is not tribe hopping.

So when Amos speaks against those at ease in Zion and those who trust in the mountain of Samaria, the difference between the two is not that one of them was righteous; all twelve went off and both would go captive. But God was known in Judah, and out of Judah the salvation of all Israel would come.

precepts.label: Revelation 11:8
precepts.why:
Amos says, “Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth”. In Amos he calls us, wicked Israel, the sinful kingdom. But if you choose to use the sinful kingdom for America, as brothers do, here is the precept: “And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.”

The great city is Babylon the great. “Spiritually” is the key word to highlight: it is called Sodom and Egypt, a spiritual Sodom and a spiritual Egypt.

“Where also our Lord was crucified.” Christ was crucified in Jerusalem, so what is it saying? America is a spiritual Jerusalem. Just as they hated Christ in the real Jerusalem, they hate the true Christ and his teachings here as well.

Either way the order of Amos stands. The sinful kingdom is destroyed, “saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob”: not all the Israelites are wiped out. We are sifted among all nations, yet the least of us is not lost. The sinners who say the evil shall not overtake them, just like Christianity saying we good in White Jesus name, die by the sword. And then, “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen”, the twelve tribes that were split into two kingdoms, “and I will build it as in the days of old”. He is already letting us know his plan, because we are predestined, foreknown from before the foundation of the earth.

thread.text: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old:

classes.title: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.label: Micah 5:3
precepts.why:
Amos says, “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.” Why does it have to be raised up? Because we fell.

Micah shows the order of it: “Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth.” God gave Israel up until the woman in travail, Israel, brought forth. “then the remnant of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel.” Then the remnant of Christ's brethren returns to the children of Israel.

That is the tabernacle of David being raised. We were given up and we fell, and now he is raising us up as in the days of old. We are coming back to who we are.

precepts.label: Hosea 3:4-5
precepts.why:
Amos says the tabernacle of David is fallen. Hosea tells how long it lies fallen: “For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim.” Teraphim are the little images we made of family members. Many days with none of it: no king, no prince, no priesthood.

“Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.”

So in these latter days, David is going to be here. Who he is, we don't know. But the children of Israel who have gone so long without a king will return and seek the Lord their God and David their king, and that is the tabernacle of David raised up and built as in the days of old.

precepts.label: Psalms 80:1-3
precepts.why:
Amos says, “I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.” Asaph cries out for that raising: “Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; thou that dwellest between the cherubims, shine forth.” The Shepherd of Israel is Christ.

“Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh stir up thy strength, and come and save us.” The tribes cry for him to stir up his strength and save them.

“Turn us again, O God, and cause thy face to shine; and we shall be saved.” Turn us again to your laws; turn us again to our identity, our nationality, and we shall be saved.

That is how the fallen tabernacle of David is rebuilt: the Shepherd of Israel turns the tribes back to his law and back to who they are, and closes up the breaches as in the days of old.

precepts.label: Joshua 15:21
precepts.why:
Before Obadiah, the class read Jeremiah 50:19: “And I will bring Israel again to his habitation, and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and Gilead.” To know whose land Carmel and Bashan were, go back to the first dividing of the land in Joshua. Write it down: Carmel was Judah's.

Joshua 15 gives the cities of Judah: “And the uttermost cities of the tribe of the children of Judah toward the coast of Edom southward were Kabzeel, and Eder, and Jagur,” “And Kinah, and Dimonah”. Then jump to verse 55: “Maon, Carmel, and Ziph”. Those belonged to Judah. Judah's lot ran to the south, right up against the coast of Edom.

Jeremiah 50 goes on to say what God will do when he brings us back: “the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I reserve.” He wipes away our iniquity and brings us again to our own habitation.

Then watch how things get switched around. Obadiah says “they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau.” The mount of Esau is where Edom used to dwell originally, and we are going to take that whole area. “and they of the plain the Philistines”: we are going to take Palestine. We shall possess the fields of Ephraim and the fields of Samaria. The land is ours by inheritance from the first dividing, and when God brings Israel back it will be possessed even further than it was then.

precepts.label: Joshua 13:29
precepts.why:
Jeremiah 50:19 says Israel “shall feed on Carmel and Bashan”. Carmel was Judah's; now Bashan. Joshua 13 shows it: “And Moses gave inheritance unto the half tribe of Manasseh: and this was the possession of the half tribe of the children of Manasseh by their families.” “And their coast was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair”. Bashan belonged to Manasseh.

Read Jeremiah 50:19 again so you get the thought: “And I will bring Israel again to his habitation, and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and Gilead.” God is bringing Israel back to the very lands the tribes were given at the beginning.

Now see how it gets switched around in Obadiah. “And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau; and they of the plain the Philistines: and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria: and Benjamin shall possess Gilead.” Benjamin shall possess Gilead. The tribes come back to the land, but the land is shared out anew.

Verse 20 goes on: “the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites, even unto Zarephath”. The land of the Canaanites is the land of Israel, and Zarephath is Lebanon. “and the captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Sepharad, shall possess the cities of the south.” Sepharad is the Asia Minor region and Spain. Our people scattered there come home and take the cities of the south.

precepts.label: Zechariah 10:10
precepts.why:
Obadiah said “Benjamin shall possess Gilead”, and Zechariah shows God bringing us there: “I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria; and I will bring them into the land of Gilead”. He is going to take us out of captivity and bring us into the land of Gilead. That is Obadiah 19 that was just read.

Then “and Lebanon”. Who belongs in Lebanon? Go back to Obadiah verse 20: “the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites, even unto Zarephath”, and Zarephath is Lebanon. “and the captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Sepharad, shall possess the cities of the south.” Then verse 21: “And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau”, the mount of Edom.

Then “and place shall not be found for them.” There is not going to be enough room for us. Isaiah 49 says the same: “For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction, shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants”. There will be too many of us. “and they that swallowed thee up shall be far away”: the nations that swallowed us up shall be far away.

Then: “The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other, shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell.” This place is too narrow; make room for me. That is why Christ said that in his Father's house are many mansions. Israel will come back in such numbers that the land cannot hold us.

precepts.label: Zechariah 13:8
precepts.why:
Isaiah 49:20 speaks of “The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other”. The ones we lost are the two thirds, here in America. In case somebody asks what that means, Zechariah shows it: “And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.”

Notice it says in all the land. The land it is talking about is Babylon, and that is America. So two out of every three Israelites shall die here in America. The ones we lost are them wicked Israelites.

Then the third: “And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.”

That remnant is who goes back to possess the land in Obadiah. And even after the two thirds are gone, the children that are left shall say, “The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell.” The land will still be too narrow for the ones God brings back.
