precepts.label: Zechariah 4:7
precepts.why:
“for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” Who is that? Christ. And the next chapter says who brings him forth: “Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain.” The great mountain is Babylon, made a plain, destroyed.

“and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.” Who shall bring forth the headstone? Zerubbabel. Chapter 3 said the Lord will bring forth his servant the Branch; here Zerubbabel brings forth the headstone, which is the same as the Branch. And the headstone brings grace unto us.

How will Zerubbabel bring him forth? Through his line. And Zerubbabel comes out of Solomon's line. Matthew 1 shows it: “And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel”, born in Babylon, and from Zorobabel down to “Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” Joseph comes out of the line of kings, the kingdom of Solomon, heir to the throne, but in captivity, with Rome calling the shots and an Edomite, Herod, on the throne, until Christ returns and conquers Edom. There is no scripture that says Jeconiah's line was cursed from being kings; that doctrine was made to justify a virgin birth. The Zerubbabel of Luke 3 is a different one, of Nathan's line: Joseph is written there because he inherited Heli's inheritance as his son-in-law, Heli being Mary's father with no sons.

precepts.label: Psalms 118:22
precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “For behold the stone that I have laid before Joshua; upon one stone shall be seven eyes.” The Branch and the stone are Christ. Then Zerubbabel “shall bring forth the headstone thereof.”

What is the headstone? “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” Who is the Branch, who is the stone? It's the same thing. The headstone Zerubbabel brings forth is the same stone laid before Joshua, and the same servant the Branch the Lord said he would bring forth: Christ, refused by the builders and made the head of the corner.

So when the Lord says “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day”, he is going into Christ. The stone laid before Joshua the high priest and his fellows, men wondered at for a sign, is the Christ who would come through Zerubbabel's loins.

precepts.label: Ephesians 2:20
precepts.why:
Zerubbabel built the second temple, so he brought forth a literal stone with a foundation. That's the first level. But it is twofold: he also brought forth the other stone through his loins, to build up the temple which is us here in the room.

“And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”: the chief corner stone, the headstone. “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”: that's us. “In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.”

So we are that holy temple that Christ builds. Zerubbabel laid the foundation of the second temple, and he brought forth the same stone and the same foundation, which is Christ, on whom we are built. Praise the Lord for that.

precepts.label: Hebrews 13:20
precepts.why:
“As for thee also, by the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water.” What is the blood of the covenant? Hebrews answers it: “Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant.”

That is the new covenant blood of Christ. The God of peace brought Christ, the great shepherd of the sheep, back from the dead through that blood, and by the same blood he sends forth his prisoners out of the pit. We are the prisoners. The pit is the same valley as Ezekiel 37, and that pit is Babylon the Great. It has “no water”: there is no truth in this land.

So Zechariah is speaking of our deliverance by Christ's blood. The great shepherd who was brought again from the dead is the one who brings the flock out, and in the end “the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people.” All twelve tribes.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 7:6
precepts.why:
“Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope.” The strong hold is the Holy Bible, and we are the prisoners of hope, hoping for New Jerusalem. Some of our people are hoping for equality. We ain't hoping for no damn equality. We are hoping for supremacy, and it is written: “For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.”

We are holy. We are special unto God. Above. Does it say equal? It says above all people upon the face of the earth. The hell with your equality; we don't want that. Think about the white man's words: when he says we're all equal, what does that translate to? Him on top, we on the bottom. It's all trickery when he speaks.

That is the hope the prisoners hold, and Zechariah shows where it ends. He will raise up “thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece”, all twelve tribes against Esau, and make us “as the sword of a mighty man”, transformed from these weak, frail bodies. And “they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land”: not a brick, not cement, but rubies and jewels. That is being above, not equal.

precepts.label: Genesis 29:22-23
precepts.why:
Matthew says Mary was espoused to Joseph, and “before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.” What does “came together” mean? Genesis 29 shows the custom. Jacob served seven years for Rachel, then said, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.” “And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast. And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her.”

The feast is the coming together. Coming together was the customary wedding feast, the same custom seen with Tobit. So before Joseph and Mary came together in the wedding feast, they lay together. There was no fornication, because they were already espoused. Espousal is marriage: once the father made the promise, she could not go and marry another, and a man who lies with a betrothed woman commits adultery. That is why the angel called Mary Joseph's wife. She was his wife by espousal, not because he had lain with her; sex alone does not make a marriage.

Then “Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily.” The commentators say that means he meant to divorce her secretly, because the child was not his. But if a just man's espoused wife were pregnant by another man, the law said she must die; a just man would not hide her. Put her away privily means hide her, the way “Elisabeth conceived, and hid herself five months.” A public example means being put to death in public. Had Mary gone back to her father's house showing, they would have said she played the harlot, just as they said of Tamar at three months.

So here is the question: why would a just man hide a pregnant woman he did not impregnate? And if she had committed adultery, why would a just man hide her sin? There is no way around that question. Minded means he was thinking about it: he was going to hide her so nothing would happen to her for what the two of them had done, because the child was his.

precepts.label: 2 Samuel 7:12
precepts.why:
The Lord promised David a king out of his own body: “And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.”

The seed that proceeds out of David's bowels is the promised king. So when the angel came to Joseph in the dream, he called him “Joseph, thou son of David”. The line is Joseph's, David's line.

The angel said, “fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.” That which is conceived in her is of the prophecy of 2 Samuel: the seed promised to David, coming out of his bowels.

That is why the Nativity begins with the bloodline. The child Mary conceived is the fulfilling of the promise made to David, that God would set up his seed after him and establish his kingdom.

precepts.label: Psalms 132:11
precepts.why:
The promise to David was sworn: “The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.”

The Lord swore it in truth, and he will not turn from it. The king on David's throne would be the fruit of David's body. That is the same promise as 2 Samuel 7:12, the seed that shall proceed out of David's bowels.

So when the angel said to Joseph, “Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost”, that which is conceived in her is of the prophecy: the fruit of David's body that the Lord swore to set upon his throne. The line runs through Joseph, the son of David.

“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” The son is the fruit of David's body, sworn in truth, set on David's throne.

precepts.label: Acts 2:30
precepts.why:
Peter said of David: “Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne”.

God swore to David that of the fruit of his loins he would raise up Christ, and notice the words: according to the flesh. Not according to the spirit. Christ sits on David's throne as the fruit of David's loins in the flesh.

That is why the angel spoke to “Joseph, thou son of David”, and why “that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost” means it is of the prophecy: the promise sworn to David in 2 Samuel 7 and Psalm 132 that the king would come out of his bowels, the fruit of his body.

So the child of Matthew 1 is the Christ God swore to raise up of the fruit of David's loins, according to the flesh, to sit on his throne. The bloodline is the birthright.

precepts.label: Romans 1:3
precepts.why:
Paul says it plainly: “Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh”. According to what? The flesh.

According to the flesh, he was made like you and I: made flesh and blood like unto his brethren, like his children. The same thing.

That is how Matthew 1 reads. Joseph was minded to put Mary away privily, “But while he thought on these things”, not did them but only thought about doing them, the angel appeared to him saying, “Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.” That which is conceived in her is of the prophecy: the seed promised to David in 2 Samuel 7 and Psalm 132, of the fruit of his loins according to the flesh.

So Jesus Christ our Lord was made of the seed of David according to the flesh. He came into this world as a son of man, made flesh and blood like his brethren, and that is how he fulfils the promise to David.

precepts.label: Isaiah 9:1-2
precepts.why:
Some Israelites had come back to the land, and watch what they were calling part of the kingdom of Israel: “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” They were calling them Gentiles.

Isaiah wrote it first as prophecy: “when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.” That affliction is the Assyrian captivity: wham. Zebulun and Naphtali were carried away, and their land became Galilee of the nations, of the Gentiles.

Then Isaiah says what would come to them: “The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.” Matthew gives it back as “The people which sat in darkness saw great light.” Isaiah is prophesying and Matthew is revealing what it is really talking about.

“From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” Christ was that great light spoken of, shining on the scattered tribes of Israel that had been made Gentiles.

precepts.label: Isaiah 42:6-7
precepts.why:
“I the Lord have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand, and will keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles.” The one given for a light is Christ, the great light that sprung up in Galilee.

Those Gentiles there are not talking about other nations. It is talking about what we just read in Matthew: “Galilee of the Gentiles”, the land of Zabulon and Nephthalim, the tribes of Israel carried away and called Gentiles.

Why is he sent? “To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house.” Them that sit in darkness are the same “people which sat in darkness” in Matthew 4:16, the people that walked in darkness in Isaiah 9. It all goes back to Matthew 4:15-16 and Isaiah 9:1-2.

So when Christ began to preach “Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand”, he was the covenant of the people and the light of the Gentiles, sent to Israel sitting in darkness to bring them out of the prison house.

precepts.label: Baruch 4:2
precepts.why:
Where does the light of Matthew 5 come from? Baruch says: “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” That is the end if you reject it.

“Turn thee, O Jacob, and take hold of it”: take hold of the book of the commandments. “Walk in the presence of the light thereof”: the light is the commandments in the book. Walk in them, “that thou mayest be illuminated.” Enlightened. You become a light in a dark place, the light that cannot be hid.

That is why “A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.” Come to this truth and start applying the laws of God and the commandments, and you cannot hide. You dress different, act different, walk different, talk different. How was your Christmas? I don't celebrate that. How was your New Year? I took a nap; a regular day. Thanksgiving, birthdays, the same. And they keep prying: where you from? Who learned you? Esau asks it, Ishmael asks it, Moab asks it, because they see something different in you, that spark, that light.

So don't hide it. “Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel”; you came to this truth to bring forth the wisdom and the light, giving light to the house of our people Israel. “Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works”, so our people may see it and maybe take that light themselves and repent.

precepts.label: Zechariah 12:7
precepts.why:
Christ commanded the twelve, “Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” Those Gentiles are the northern kingdom; that's why they are in the same sentence with Samaria. He names the Samaritans because Ephraim was the leading tribe. The lost sheep there means the kingdom of Judah: start with Judah first.

Here's the prophecy of it: “The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” The tents of Judah first.

So when Christ came, he wasn't going, hey, I'm just gathering all Israel at once. He said, no, I got to start with Judah, and then the rest of them come later on. That is why he held the apostles back from the Gentiles and the Samaritans in Matthew 10: the order was set by the prophet, Judah first.

precepts.label: Psalms 83:3
precepts.why:
Christ says, “And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul”. They can't kill the real you, brothers and sisters. You think that body is the real you, but it is just a shell that corrodes in time. So why is our people so afraid to die? David shows it: “They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.”

Slavery, miseducation and religion are all part of that crafty counsel. Their religions make you think this is all there is, like the Sam Cooke song: I don't know what's up there beyond the sky. It puts a spirit of fear on you: if you die, you're going to hell and you're going to burn down there. So everybody is afraid to die.

But when you read the Bible, how come our foremothers and forefathers did not have the spirit we have today? They knew something we don't. The woman with the seven sons said, kill me now, cut my arms off, cut my tongue. We say, what the hell is this? Because the crafty counsel taught us lie after lie about reality: that after this you're done.

The Bible calls death sleep, many times. That's all it is, and you wake up before the Lord. Paul said to be absent from the body is to be present with the Lord. But do we believe that, or what the white man says on his television screens?

Christ goes on, “but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell”: that is the lake of fire, which is not now. When you die now, everybody is at rest, even the wicked. When the Lord returns he takes the keys of hell and death and opens it all up, and that is when the lake of fire comes. So don't fear them that kill the body, because the things we teach will get us killed, and you will not deny Christ if you have not swallowed their crafty counsel.

precepts.label: Acts 26:10-11
precepts.why:
Christ says, “But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.” Under what conditions? Not at work saying, yeah, I believe in God. Read in context, it is tribulation, persecution, Jacob's trouble: I never believed that Israelite stuff, I don't believe in those commandments, my husband forced me, my wife forced me.

Paul testified what denying looks like from the persecutor's side: “Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.”

“And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme”. Compel means he forced them to blaspheme. That is what Christ was talking about: deny me under torture, persecution, tribulation, hard times. That is the trial all of us alive at this time must go through.

Paul was not the only persecutor. What Paul did, they were all doing: the Pharisees, and later the inquisitors under Queen Isabella and King Ferdinand in the time of Spain and Portugal, whose job was to hunt down Israelites keeping the commandments, to Africa, to Mexico, to South and North America.

And “being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.” That is why Christ said, when they persecute you in this city, flee into another.

Everybody in here says they love God, but some of us are liars. Some are not valiant for the truth; you are a professional student, a hireling. The hireling sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep. Think about being compelled to blaspheme, as in the film Unthinkable, where they brought in a man's wife and kids to make him confess. You think that could never happen to you; the devil is a liar. What Paul was doing is what Christ said is going to happen.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 2:2-5
precepts.why:
Matthew names Christ's family: “is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?” Mary his mother and Mary his aunt at the cross, a brother named Simon among Simons everywhere: Israel used the same names over and over, even inside one family. The Maccabees prove it.

“In those days arose Mattathias the son of John, the son of Simeon, a priest.” “And he had five sons, Joannan, called Caddis: Simon; called Thassi: Judas, who was called Maccabeus: Eleazar, called Avaran: and Jonathan, whose surname was Apphus.” Stop at Jonathan. Joannan and Jonathan are the same name: John and John, two sons of one father. Like George Foreman naming his sons George, George, George and George.

So it was a common thing for Israel to name sons the same name. You had Mary and Mary, John and John, John the Baptist too; they loved that name. You had Simon Iscariot, Simon the Canaanite, Simon Peter, and Christ's own brother Simon. That is why two Zerubbabels in the genealogies is no puzzle at all.

precepts.label: John 1:45
precepts.why:
In Matthew his own people asked, “Is not this the carpenter's son?” John shows his own disciples said the same thing: “Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”

The son of who? The son of Joseph. The one Moses and the prophets wrote about is called by his disciple the son of Joseph, the carpenter.

And Matthew says he had brethren, James, Joses, Simon and Judas, and sisters, more than one: a bunch of siblings. James wrote the book of James and Judas wrote Jude. So you Christians who say Mary was a virgin who never had sex read this all the time. Now some hear us teach it and act like they came up with it, saying the Roman Catholic doctrine is wrong, playing catchup. Christ had a father and a mother, brothers and sisters.

precepts.label: Mark 6:3
precepts.why:
Mark gives the same account as Matthew 13. On the sabbath Christ “began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things?” Then: “Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.”

They knew his family. They knew his background, his mother, his brothers by name, and his sisters. Who do he think he is? We grew up with this guy. He ain't nobody special. You're from the hood like us, from Nazareth; what you talking about, Savior? In his own home, where he was from, he got disrespected by his own neighbors and family members.

So the scripture itself shows Christ was born into a real family, the son of Mary with brothers and sisters, and that the people offended at him were the ones who knew exactly where he came from.

precepts.label: Proverbs 16:1
precepts.why:
Christ told the twelve, “Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven”. Someone thinks it's just leadership saying it. No: “The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from the Lord.” The Lord had already ordained you to come up to that leadership table. Even your walking up to the council you want to go against was declared before time, as Isaiah 46:10 says, declaring the end from the beginning. God already agreed.

The preparing of your mind is from the Lord. You may say, I'm going to get up at 9:00 today and make it to the gym. The Lord says no, you are getting up at 10:00, and you'll get out the bed on the left-hand side and stub your damn toe. You set that timer to the T all week, you're a light sleeper, and that joker doesn't ring, because that was the Lord's doing. The Lord seals man's instruction in his sleep.

And the answer of the tongue, is that from the man or the woman? It is from the Lord. The Lord dictates even what you are going to respond back. The Lord may send a spirit down on you to go contrary to the doctrine, contrary to what leadership says in counsel to save your life, and you don't even catch that it is a spirit speaking through you. That is also a learning experience, for you to catch yourself.

But many cannot shake that legion. They ride that wave onto the bitterness boat and find themselves outside the congregation, making three- and four-part emotional videos and complaining on Clubhouse about how they were done unjustly. Then the Lord blinds your mind; you are reprobate, and only if the Lord chooses will he bring you back.

So your issue is not with leadership; you are bitter toward the Lord. Leadership has nothing to gain by telling you the word. All we gave you was the word of God, and we will be judged for it. Take it here and forbear, or go out there and get burnt. Our people hate their freedom; they are fearful of freedom, of responsibility, and of leadership.

precepts.label: John 11:47-50
precepts.why:
Why would the rulers of the synagogues kill and crucify the prophets sent to them? John 11 shows what was in their hearts. “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

That is the problem. It is not that they could not see the truth; it is their place. The same holds for the pastors today: if they speak the truth, the white man is going to take away their place, their riches and their platforms and make them into commoners. They do not want that, so they have to follow Rome. They have to follow America's doctrines. They cannot speak the truth.

“And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” The one man is Christ. Better to kill him than lose their position.

So when we come into the churches with the same Bible they have, and they put hands on us and pull guns on us with the love of Jesus, it is the same spirit: the prophets are scourged in the synagogues to protect the place of the rulers.

precepts.label: John 12:1-11
precepts.why:
This shows how evil they are. Six days before the passover Christ came to Bethany, “where Lazarus was which had been dead, whom he raised from the dead.” At the supper Mary took “a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair”.

Judas Iscariot complained: “Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred pence, and given to the poor? This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag, and bare what was put therein.” Christ answered, “Let her alone: against the day of my burying hath she kept this. For the poor always ye have with you; but me ye have not always.”

“Much people of the Jews therefore knew that he was there: and they came not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead.” In the chapter before, the Pharisees had already said, we have to kill this man because he does many miracles and Rome is going to take away our place.

Now: “But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death; Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.” Christ raised Lazarus out of the grave, and they said it is not just Christ we have to kill; we have to kill the one he raised from the dead too. That is next-level evil.

And that is what they will do to us. Because by reason of the truth many believe on Christ, they will seek to put us to death, the same as “some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues”.

precepts.label: Isaiah 46:10
precepts.why:
“See that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass”. Why must they come to pass? Because it was already ordained to happen this way. That is why this Bible is a great mystery given to the sons of the living God.

“Declaring the end from the beginning”. God declared the end from the creation of the earth. There was already a council with us and our heavenly Father, and all of us agreed to take our roles as the twelve tribes of the children of Israel. “And from ancient times”: there is no time with God; he is beyond time. God declared the end of this white man's captivity from the beginning. He declared our rulership from the beginning. He gave us the playbook before time was even created.

“The things that are not yet done”. We are walking and living through the timeline of prophecy. Things declared from ancient times are unfolding right before our eyes, and still many read it and do not believe it.

“Saying, My counsel shall stand”. God's counsel and his will shall be done. You cannot move it around, thwart it, or throw it off track. Whether you believe it or not, prophecy will be fulfilled; the word of the Lord will not go out void.

“And I will do all my pleasure”. This destruction was declared before time existed, and it is pleasure in the sight of the Lord. But many of our people do not see it as pleasure; they are fearful of the Lord's pleasure, fearful of freedom, while they love sin. Every war and rumour of war since 1917 has been a birthing pain. The ones who are troubled are the ones with secret sin on the back end. Now is not the time to play with your salvation.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 6:7-10
precepts.why:
“And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another”. Many in the body are here for the wrong reasons: opportunists out to make a quick buck, and some sent by the three-letter boys, the FBI and CIA, to spy out our liberties. But to the pure all things are pure. If you are among us to spy, all you are going to learn is to repent. You will not find us making maps or plotting to take over buildings. You will find no guns, no pimping, no drugs; only the word of God, our weapon of mass destruction. They want to know the secret sauce, and it is always God's commandments.

Paul lays it out: “By the word of truth, by the power of God”. That is how we roll: God's laws, statutes and commandments. “By the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left”: wherever we turn, that is our way.

“By honour and dishonour”: some honour the works, the platforms and the doors opening, and some see it as dishonour. “By evil report and good report”: evil report from some, but our intentions are pure. We are about family, raising our children and taking care of our wives. “As deceivers, and yet true”: those who hate God's commandments call us deceivers, but our word is true.

“As unknown, and yet well known”: they label us black Hebrew extremists as if they know nothing about us, but they know exactly that we are the sons of the living God. “As dying, and, behold, we live”: we are afflicted, and they think we have no life because we keep the Sabbath; but Christ is in us, and we keep more feast days than their wicked holidays and enjoy our families. “As chastened, and not killed; As sorrowful, yet alway rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich”.

precepts.label: James 2:5
precepts.why:
Paul said we are “as poor, yet making many rich”. James shows why we are rich. They like to think this life we live is miserable. No: we are fulfilling God's prophecy.

“Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world”. How are we poor? Because they robbed us. We have been robbed of our nationality and robbed of our land. Israel is your land: black man, black woman, Latino man, Latino woman, Native American man, Native American woman. We did not know our nationality or our history. But that stops now; now we know.

“Rich in faith”. We are rich because Christ came for us; that is our faith. We keep the commandments and the faith of Jesus Christ, and we have the hope of deliverance coming our way: “heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him”.

That is why we are not fearful of freedom. Every bomb dropped and every war fought is loosening the links of the shackles of our captivity. The Lord is the director of this thing, and those he chose out of poverty are the heirs of the kingdom.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 5:2
precepts.why:
“And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.” Why is iniquity going to abound? Because of the false prophets: the false Christians and these foolish Abrahamic religions teaching lie after lie. They glorify sin; sin is being glorified. And the love of many waxing cold means we are going to start to hate one another.

Ezra was told the same thing: “But iniquity shall be increased above that which now thou seest, or that thou hast heard long ago.” The angel was telling Ezra that iniquity would go way beyond anything he had known or seen.

And look at it now. Men are cutting their privates off and having a vagina cut in there. That was unheard of. Women are getting penises sewn on. You cannot make this stuff up. Magic Johnson's son says he is only attracted to straight men; if he is attracted to you, he is not straight.

That is iniquity increased above anything heard of long ago, exactly as the angel said. So repent. “But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved”: we have to endure the hardships, the tribulation and the persecution Christ said would come, and not let our love wax cold.

precepts.label: Revelation 7:1-4
precepts.why:
“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.” Earlier Christ said in Matthew 10, “Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.” So we are not going to reach all the Israelites. Then what does “all the world” mean, and when does the end come? Revelation 7 answers.

“I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth”. That is the fighting, the wars. “That the wind should not blow on the earth”: the armies. “Nor on the sea”: the marines and the navies. “Nor on any tree”: what is above the trees is the air force.

“And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God”. The seal of the living God is not the hexagram. It is the law: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” He cried to the four angels “to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea”, hurt it with destruction: “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.”

“And there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” So the end begins when the 144,000 are sealed. The world Christ is talking about in Matthew 24 is the 144,000: when they are sealed, then shall the end come.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 13:5
precepts.why:
Revelation 7 has four angels holding the four winds of the earth. Let the Bible say what the wind is. Write it down: “And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”.

Where did the multitude come from? From the four winds of heaven. And what did they come for? To subdue the man that came out of the sea. So the winds are their armies coming against the Son of God, coming against the master.

That is why the four angels hold the winds so they do not blow on the earth, the sea or any tree: the armies on land, the navies and marines on the sea, and the air force above the trees. The destruction is held back until the servants of God are sealed. When the 144,000 are sealed, the winds are let go, the nations gather for war, and after that tribulation the Son of man comes in the clouds of heaven.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:16
precepts.why:
In Revelation 7 another angel ascends from the east “having the seal of the living God”, and the destruction is held back “till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” What is the seal of the living God?

It is not the hexagram. Many of us thought so years ago when we were young. Isaiah says what it is: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The seal of the living God is the law, bound up and sealed among his disciples. Pay attention, because if you blink you might miss it.

So the servants sealed in their foreheads are the ones with the law of God in their minds: “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” When they are sealed, the four winds are loosed and the end comes. That is why this gospel, the law and the testimony, has to be preached in all the world for a witness: to seal the 144,000 before the end.

precepts.label: Isaiah 66:19-21
precepts.why:
Remember, the 144,000 have to be sealed, and then the end comes. Isaiah shows what they do: “And I will set a sign among them, and I will send those that escape of them unto the nations”. Those that escape are the 144,000. He sends them “to Tarshish”, Spain; “Pul”, Libya; “and Lud, that draw the bow, to Tubal”, Turkey; “and Javan”, the Grecian islands; “to the isles afar off, that have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glory”.

There will be people who have not heard the fame of the Lord and have not seen his glory: Israelites who have not heard or seen anything, and we have to go get them. “And they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles.” That is “this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations”.

You might think that is talking about now. The next verse clears it up: “And they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the Lord out of all nations upon horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and upon mules, and upon swift beasts, to my holy mountain Jerusalem”. Jerusalem is already established as holy. Is Jerusalem holy today? No, there are bombs and missiles going off there. So this is not now; the kingdom is already set up.

“And I will also take of them for priests and for Levites, saith the Lord.” The brothers gathered from among those nations, the Lord will make them priests and Levites. With that, Matthew 24:14 gives a deeper understanding: the gospel preached in all the world is the work of the 144,000, and once they are sealed, the end comes.

thread.label: Matthew 24:29-31
thread.text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:

classes.title: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.label: Isaiah 34:4-5
precepts.why:
“Immediately after the tribulation of those days”: the churches argue about a seven-year dispensation, pre-trib and post-trib, and say the church is not going through tribulation. They do not know the Bible. Those who are alive must and will go through tribulation. Then “the stars shall fall from heaven”: missiles, rockets. “And the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”: that is war. Notice it says heavens, plural; it is not talking about the sky. What powers of the heavens?

Isaiah shows it: “And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll”, the mushroom effect. “And all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree”: missiles and rockets falling.

“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven”. Christ said his sword would be bathed in heaven, so what heaven is he going to bathe his sword in? “Behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.” Idumea is the so-called white man, the leading race on the planet. The powers of the heavens shaken is the war with Idumea, all these Edomite nations.

So Christ comes back for war, not only to save. The order is tribulation, then war between the nations, then the sign of the Son of man. The gap may be five years, as World War II was once America entered, or seven; it does not say.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:4
precepts.why:
“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” Who is the elect? Not everybody.

Isaiah says: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”. We are the elect. Israel is the elect. Not the Baptist church, and not all races on the planet.

And it is from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other, because Isaiah 66 already showed there are Israelites scattered in the isles afar off who have not heard his fame nor seen his glory, and we have to go get them.

Before that gathering, “then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn”. It is going to be a happy day, but we will be crying and fearful too. And it comes only after the tribulation. Christ is not returning this year or next year; bad things have to happen first and we have to be proven. Not being able to pay your light bill is not tribulation. We are too comfortable, still smoking weed, going to the club, defiling the Sabbath, the women dressed like hoes with no clothes; in their affliction they will seek him, and the affliction has not even begun.

precepts.label: Luke 21:25-28
precepts.why:
Luke tells the same coming, and shows where we are in it. “And there shall be signs in the sun”, like a solar eclipse, “and in the moon”, blood moons and lunar eclipses, “and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations”: we are seeing that now. “With perplexity”: perplexity means confusion. “The sea and the waves roaring”: the nations roaring.

“Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.” That is war. “And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.” Right now we are in verse 25 going into the top part of verse 26.

“And when these things begin to come to pass”: the signs in the sun, the moon and the stars, the distress of nations with perplexity. “Then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.” We are supposed to be looking up and lifting up our heads, knowing redemption is soon to come.

But we know the order of what is going to happen: tribulation, war, then Christ. So this is our time to clean ourselves up and get right with the Lord, because the time is drawing close.

precepts.label: Isaiah 66:15-16
precepts.why:
When Christ comes after the tribulation and the war, he does not come only to gather; he comes to judge. Isaiah shows it: “For, behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire.”

“For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh: and the slain of the Lord shall be many.” All flesh. The slain of the Lord shall be many, and that is not just Esau. The wicked Israelites too.

That is why Christ is not coming tomorrow to rapture a comfortable church out of trouble. He comes with fire and sword against the nations of Idumea, and against every wicked one, including our own people who keep smoking, clubbing, and defiling the Sabbath. The powers of the heavens are shaken, his sword is bathed in heaven, and only his elect, Jacob and Israel who repented and endured, are gathered from the four winds.

precepts.label: John 1:29
precepts.why:
At the Passover dinner Christ took the cup and said, “For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.” The blood the Israelites put on the doorposts in ancient Egypt represented Christ's blood. It represented the new covenant: Christ coming and dying for our sins.

John shows who the lamb is: “The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God”. Christ is called the Lamb of God. That male lamb of the first year represents Christ. He is that sacrifice.

So we do not sacrifice anymore, but we do have the dinner, with the understanding that the lamb represents Christ. Do not take blood and put it on your doorpost today; some brothers are crazy. Killing a lamb is not going to protect you from the wrath of God. Believing in Christ and doing what is right is what protects you from the wrath of God.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 5:7
precepts.why:
The bread represents Christ's body, and the cup his blood “shed for many for the remission of sins.” Paul says it plainly: “Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”.

Christ is our passover. The lamb that was killed represents Christ, and that is saying a lot. He was sacrificed for us; he came and died for our sins.

So you do not have to go kill a lamb and put the blood over the doorpost so that you do not die. You believe in Christ and you keep the commandments, and we come together, we break bread and we drink wine, as Christ did with the twelve at the Passover. That is being under the new covenant.

precepts.label: Ruth 4:13
precepts.why:
Gabriel tells Mary, “thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son”. It is the same word used of her cousin: “And after those days his wife Elisabeth conceived”. What does it mean to conceive? To conceive you need seed; the man’s seed has to go in and fertilize the egg. Some might be confused, so Ruth shows how that happens.

“So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son.” When Boaz went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception. That is how it works: a husband goes in unto his wife, and the Lord gives the conception.

And when Luke 1:28 says the angel “came in unto her”, he came in and talked with her. He did not come in and have sex with her; he came in and talked to her, plain and simple. So when Luke 1:31 says Mary shall conceive, it is conception the way Ruth conceived, the Lord giving it when her husband came unto her. It could well have been the first time Joseph touched her that the Lord made her conceive.

precepts.label: Leviticus 12:2
precepts.why:
The law shows what conceiving is: “Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If a woman have conceived seed, and born a man child: then she shall be unclean seven days”. She conceived what? Seed.

A woman conceives seed through intercourse. That is the same seed Onan spilled on the ground in Genesis 38, knowing the inheritance would not be his. It is the same exact thing.

So Luke 1:31, “thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son”, is a woman conceiving seed and bearing a man child. It is said to Mary in the same form of words as to Zacharias about Elisabeth: “thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John,” and “shalt call his name JESUS.” The same thing being done, the same thing being said.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 19:7-8
precepts.why:
Luke 1:35 says “the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee”. What does overshadow mean? Wisdom of Solomon shows it: “For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments that were given unto them, that thy children might be kept without hurt”. The whole creature is Israel, the whole nation that came out of Egypt, made new, serving the peculiar commandments.

“As namely, a cloud shadowing the camp; and where water stood before, dry land appeared; and out of the Red sea a way without impediment; and out of the violent stream a green field: Wherethrough all the people went that were defended with thy hand, seeing thy marvellous strange wonders.”

What did the cloud shadowing the camp do for us at the Red Sea? It led us. It guided us through the Red Sea, and the people went through “defended with thy hand.” That is what overshadow means: to lead, guide and defend.

So when the angel says the power of the Highest shall overshadow Mary, it is not the spirit coming into her and making her pregnant. It is the Lord guiding and defending her, leading her to where she had to go.

precepts.label: Baruch 5:7-9
precepts.why:
Baruch gives another one. Overshadow does not mean that it got her impregnated. It means to guide her to where she had to go. “For God hath appointed that every high hill, and banks of long continuance, should be cast down, and valleys filled up, to make even the ground, that Israel may go safely in the glory of God”.

“Moreover even the woods and every sweetsmelling tree shall overshadow Israel by the commandment of God. For God shall lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory”. The trees shall overshadow Israel, for God shall lead Israel. To overshadow is to lead, guide or defend.

So in Luke 1:35 the Lord would lead Mary to Joseph. When it says overshadow thee, it means he will guide and lead her, like he led Zacharias home to his wife to lay with her. That is what it is talking about, not him overshadowing her into pregnancy.

precepts.label: Proverbs 20:24
precepts.why:
This goes with overshadow: the Lord guided Mary, and she went and came together with her husband. “Man’s goings are of the Lord; how can a man then understand his own way?”

A man’s goings are of the Lord because the Lord guides us and overshadows us in everyday life. Sometimes you are walking in the street, something tells you to pick something up off the ground, and a car goes right by where you would have been. Why? The Lord was there guiding you.

“how can a man then understand his own way?” Remember, Mary did not understand. She said, “How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?” She was espoused to Joseph but had not yet come together with him. The Lord said, don’t worry, you are going to fulfil the scriptures; I am going to guide you. She could not understand her way, but the Most High had plans for her, and he guided her, the same way he guided every one of us here.

precepts.label: John 4:19-22
precepts.why:
Christ told the Samaritan woman by the well the same thing he said in Luke 21. She said, “Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet. Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.” The Samaritans worshipped up on Mount Gerizim, because their fathers used to worship up there back in the days.

“Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. Ye worship ye know not what”. The Samaritans were not going to worship in that mountain, and the Jews, the Israelites, would not be worshipping at Jerusalem either.

What is Christ saying here? What Luke 21 says: we would “fall by the edge of the sword”, and be “led away captive into all nations”, carried away as slaves into all nations. We fell by the sword in 70 AD, and being led into all nations is a process of time; it didn't all happen in 70 AD. Jerusalem would be “trodden down of the Gentiles”, occupied by heathens, until Christ returns and destroys the Gentiles.

In 70 AD most of us fled into Africa, formed communities, built cities and mingled amongst the Hamitic tribes. Esau drew maps pinpointing where the tribes were all over Africa, the Levite cities of Nigeria, Bnei Ephraim on the slave coast, the Jewish kingdoms, because slavery was not coincidence. Slavery was war.

precepts.label: Hosea 4:17
precepts.why:
After Christ dealt with Judah, “he must needs go through Samaria.” There the woman said, “How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” The southern kingdom did not deal with the northern kingdom. Remember the rift from Rehoboam; that was always the problem.

Hosea gives the reason: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” Remember, Jeroboam set up priests in the land, and Ephraim went into idolatry. So we did not deal with them.

But she was still an Israelite: “Art thou greater than our father Jacob”? Right there she's telling you she's an Israelite. People on YouTube say she wasn't, because Shalmaneser put men of Babylon and the Chaldees in the land, but there is more history: Ezra shows Israelites coming back to the land. And if she was lying about her identity, why didn't Christ correct her? He did correct her about something, her five husbands, letting her know she was living a whorish lifestyle, because sex does not constitute marriage. But he never corrected her nationality.

He revealed himself to her, “I that speak unto thee am he”, which he would not do if she were not an Israelite, and his disciples marvelled that he talked with her, because the Jews had no dealings with the Samaritans. Then he abode there two days teaching them, and they knew he was “the Saviour of the world”, the world of Israel. The one Hosea said to let alone, Christ went to gather.

precepts.label: Isaiah 7:9
precepts.why:
Why is a woman of Samaria an Israelite, and why did the Jews have no dealings with her? Isaiah names it: “And the head of Ephraim is Samaria”. Samaria was the capital of Ephraim, the head city of the northern kingdom.

So when John says Christ “must needs go through Samaria” and met “a woman of Samaria”, he is in the land of Ephraim, among the northern kingdom. That is why she could say “our father Jacob, which gave us the well”, and “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain”. Her fathers were the fathers of Israel.

The rift between the kingdoms went back to Rehoboam, and Judah had nothing to do with Ephraim and its capital. But Christ said “the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father”, the hour of 70 AD, when nobody would be worshipping in Jerusalem or Samaria. “Ye worship ye know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.” He stayed two days in Samaria and many believed on him. That is the raising up of the tabernacle of David that fell: both houses gathered back to the Messiah.

precepts.label: Acts 17:11
precepts.why:
“Search the scriptures.” Our job is to search the scriptures. The nations don't; they leave their scripture searching to Matthew through Revelation with their misunderstanding from Christianity. If you start from Genesis, you find out that salvation and rulership of the earth is only for the Israelites through Christ. The Bereans show how it is done: “These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.”

When Paul presented the truth of Christ to them, they did not just take it; they searched the scriptures daily to see whether what Paul was teaching was accurate according to the scriptures. That is what made them more noble, and that is what we have to do.

The scriptures they searched were the same ones Christ said “testify of me.” Searching them daily with a ready mind is how the truth of Christ is proved.

precepts.label: Proverbs 25:2
precepts.why:
“It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.” When God conceals something, it is in parable form, metaphors and allegories, and it is our job to figure out what the Lord means by A, B and C.

That is why we must search. Read Jeremiah 48, “against Moab”, or Jeremiah 49, “Concerning the Ammonites”, and unless you search the scriptures and pray to the Lord, you'll say, I don't know who Moab is, I don't know who the Ammonites are, I don't know who Gad is, I'm confused, so I'll stick to Matthew through Revelation. That's what the churches do. Christians don't know and Muslims don't know, confused and discombobulated, unable to identify these nations today.

The honour of kings is to search it out: to find who Moab, Ammon, Gad and Asia are today. The matter is concealed, but it is there for those who search.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 29:29
precepts.why:
“The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.”

What God has kept secret and then revealed to us is for our children and our children's children forever. So what we bring out in the scriptures is meant for our sons and our daughters. Teach them. Don't let this truth fall by the wayside, with your sons and daughters worshipping Caesar Borgia all over again. That would be a detriment to you and your family.

Searching the scriptures is not only for ourselves. What the Lord reveals by it belongs to us and to our children, so that we and they may do all the words of this law.

precepts.label: Acts 22:12
precepts.why:
Cornelius is called “A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.” How do you become a devout man? People go, yeah, he was another nation, but he was devout. No, no, no.

Look at how the scripture uses the word: “And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there”. You see? A devout man according to the law. The other nations did not have the law.

So how was Cornelius a devout man according to the law? How did he fear God? How did he know how to pray to God? He had to know the law. He even kept the hours of prayer: the angel came to him “about the ninth hour of the day”, and he told Peter, “at the ninth hour I prayed in my house”.

So yes, Cornelius is an Israelite, northern kingdom. His devotion was devotion to the law of God, which was given to Israel and to no other nation.

precepts.label: Acts 21:16
precepts.why:
Cornelius was “a certain man in Cesarea”. Write this down: Caesarea is in the land of Israel. It is in the land of West Manasseh, right beside Samaria. It is not some foreign country; it is the land of the northern kingdom.

And Acts shows believers coming out of that very place: “There went with us also certain of the disciples of Cesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.” You had some disciples that came from Caesarea as well, the same place Cornelius is from.

Peter lived in Joppa, the seaport there, and he sailed up north to visit Cornelius. Christ was raised further up, in Galilee, so he was raised around them in that area. And the place called Scythopolis means city of the Scythians, and the Scythians are northern kingdom also: that is who Paul wrote to in Colossians 3:11.

So Caesarea was a place of disciples in the land of Manasseh, and Cornelius and his kinsmen were northern kingdom Israelites living in their own land, not a Roman people God took in instead of Israel.

precepts.label: Hosea 8:8
precepts.why:
In the dream Peter “saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners”. What is that vessel? Hosea says it: “Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.”

Israel is the vessel. Swallowed up among the nations, a vessel no one has pleasure in: that is what came down to Peter in the sheet.

That is why the dream was never about eating unclean animals. Verse 28 is where Peter breaks the dream down: “God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.” Any man. It is not talking about roaches or ants or eating unclean pig. The dream was about man.

What man? The Israelites being cleansed, the northern kingdom being cleansed. The vessel full of fourfooted beasts and creeping things is Israel scattered among the Gentiles, and God was showing Peter it was time to bring them back in.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 37:21-23
precepts.why:
The voice spake unto Peter the second time: “What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.” So what does God cleanse? Does he cleanse Esau? I never read that one. Ezekiel tells us who God cleanses.

“Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land: And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”.

Then: “but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” God says he is going to cleanse us, the twelve tribes.

So what God hath cleansed is Israel, the northern kingdom brought back to Judah. That is why Peter could go into Cornelius’ house. Christians read verses 34 and 35, “God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him”, and say God accepts everybody, that Cornelius was a white man, an Italian, a Roman. That is supersessionism, replacement theology. The next verse explains it: “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel”.

thread.label: Acts 10:1-4
thread.text: There was a certain man in Cesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band,

classes.title: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.label: Matthew 4:15
precepts.why:
“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”. Zabulon and Nephthalim are tribes of the northern kingdom, and the scripture calls their land Galilee of the Gentiles. That is what they called the northern kingdom: the Gentiles. Christians have not figured that out yet.

So when Cornelius is brought in, he is not a Gentile of the nations. Look at where he was from: “a certain man in Cesarea called Cornelius”. On the map of the Holy Land, Caesarea sits right above Samaria on the left. That is Manasseh’s land. That is where Cornelius was from.

This is more proof that Cornelius was northern kingdom. You can jump up and call him a goy all you want to; we don’t give a damn. Do some research. Do some study.

Cornelius was “A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house”, an Israelite of the northern kingdom, a Gentile in the way the scripture uses the word, and his prayers and alms came up for a memorial before God.

precepts.label: Acts 15:15-17
precepts.why:
When God accepted Cornelius and his kinsmen in Acts 10, the apostles came together in Acts 15, and James said, “to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written, After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down”.

What does that mean? Bring back the twelve tribes of Israel. Bring back the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom. Christians do not realize it; ask them what happened to the northern kingdom and they say, I don’t know.

“And I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up: That the residue of men might seek after the Lord”: they are going to seek him in slavery. “And all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called”: those that call themselves Jewish and those that call themselves Christian.

So the accepting of Cornelius was the beginning of that building again. The tabernacle of David fell when the kingdom split, and bringing Cornelius, a northern kingdom man out of Manasseh’s land, into the fold is God starting to put the two kingdoms back together.

precepts.label: Amos 9:11-12
precepts.why:
James in Acts 15 was quoting the prophet Amos. This is what James and Peter were quoting: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”. He is going to bring back the southern kingdom with the northern kingdom.

“And I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”: as in the days of old, when the twelve tribes were one.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name”. The heathen called by his name are those that call themselves Jewish and those that call themselves Christian. Christian is a Greek word that means anointed ones. They are not the anointed ones. We are.

So Cornelius and his house being accepted was the word of Amos coming to pass: the breach between the kingdoms being closed up, the tabernacle of David raised, and Israel set to possess the remnant of Edom, “saith the Lord that doeth this.”

precepts.label: Revelation 7:4-8
precepts.why:
“And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” All the tribes, the northern kingdom along with the southern, are sealed. The two kingdoms that God said he would bring back together are there together in the end.

Look at the bottom of verse 6: “Of the tribe of Manasses were sealed twelve thousand.” Manasseh is mentioned by name, the same tribe whose land Caesarea sat in, where Cornelius came from.

Then verse 8: “Of the tribe of Joseph were sealed twelve thousand.” Highlight that. Joseph is mentioned, and Ephraim is not. Joseph here is Ephraim.

So the northern kingdom that Christians say disappeared is sealed in Revelation 7, Manasseh by his own name and Ephraim under the name of Joseph. That is the tabernacle of David built again: all twelve tribes counted and sealed.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 37:19
precepts.why:
Revelation 7 names the tribe of Joseph but not Ephraim. How do we know Joseph there is Ephraim? Write the precept down: “Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim”. See that? Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim. That is how you know Joseph stands for Ephraim.

And God does not leave that stick by itself: “and the tribes of Israel his fellows, and will put them with him, even with the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, and they shall be one in mine hand.”

Ephraim and the tribes of Israel his fellows are the northern kingdom; the stick of Judah is the southern kingdom. God puts them together and makes them one stick in his hand.

That is the same work James spoke of in Acts 15 and Amos prophesied, the tabernacle of David built again, and it is why Cornelius, a man of the northern kingdom, was received. Joseph and Judah are made one.

thread.label: Acts 13:21-22
thread.text: And afterward they desired a king: and God gave unto them Saul the son of Cis, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, by the space of forty years.

classes.title: Sovereign Idiocracy

precepts.label: Psalms 40:8
precepts.why:
Why is it that the Lord established David over his people, to establish the sovereign kingdom of Israel? If you want to be sovereign, there is one way to it: a one-way road with one victory at the end of it, the kingdom of heaven.

“And afterward they desired a king: and God gave unto them Saul the son of Cis.” Even though we wanted a king, it was still the Lord that had to establish him. “And when he had removed him”: the Lord removed Saul from being king over Israel. So where does this power and authority come from? Only from God. Only God can make you sovereign and remove your sovereignty; not you, and not your piece of paper with weird words on it. “he raised up unto them David to be their king”: as righteous and powerful and mighty as David was, it was still the Lord that established him as king over Israel, a sovereign government.

“I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will.” That is the caveat to being sovereign, to ruling over God's heritage: a man after God's own heart, exactly how the Lord wanted his servant and king to be. And he fulfils all the Lord's will, not his own personal will or desire.

What is the will of God? David says it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The will of God is the laws of God. What pleased God in David, to the point that he established him as ruler over his people as a sovereign government? He kept God's commandments; he kept the testimonies. The Lord establishes his rulers by who is faithful to him, faithful to the commandments.

thread.label: Acts 13:45-47
thread.text: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy, and spake against those things which were spoken by Paul, contradicting and blaspheming.

classes.title: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.label: John 7:1
precepts.why:
“But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy, and spake against those things which were spoken by Paul, contradicting and blaspheming.” The same thing that happened with Paul happened with Christ: “After these things Jesus walked in Galilee: for he would not walk in Jewry, because the Jews sought to kill him.”

Christ was not walking with the southern kingdom any more. He went to Galilee, and Matthew 4:15 shows you who was in Galilee: Zebulun and Naphtali, “Galilee of the Gentiles”. Those Gentiles are the northern kingdom.

So the same thing Paul and Barnabas met, the Jews rejecting salvation in Jesus Christ, is the same thing Christ had to deal with. And Paul did what Christ did: “seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles.”

The word had to be spoken to Judah “first”, as the Lord “shall save the tents of Judah first”. When Judah put it from them, Christ went into Galilee, and Paul and Barnabas turned to the Gentiles: the northern kingdom. You cannot just assume that because it says Gentiles it means the other nations; there are times it refers to the Israelites in a Gentile state, cut off from being his people in Hosea chapter 1.

precepts.label: Obadiah 18
precepts.why:
Obadiah shows Samaritans, Gentiles and Israel at the same time: “And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble”.

The house of Jacob in verse 18 is Judah alone: the southern kingdom, Judah, Benjamin and Levi. The house of Joseph is Ephraim and the rest, the northern kingdom. That is who the Samaritans and Gentiles are in Matthew 10:5.

So when Christ tells his disciples not to go to the Samaritans or the Gentiles, the house of Joseph, but rather to the lost sheep, the house of Jacob, he is saying the exact same thing Paul says here: “It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you”. First to Judah, the southern kingdom; then “lo, we turn to the Gentiles”, the house of Joseph.

And both houses are brought together against Esau: “they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.” Judah received the gospel first, and then the Lord showed the other tribes, and that order has always been the same.

thread.label: Acts 15:14
thread.text: Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.

classes.title: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.label: Amos 9:11
precepts.why:
Isaiah spoke of “the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” What does it mean to bind up the breach of his people? Acts 15 answers it. “Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name. And to this agree the words of the prophets”: “After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down”. That is bringing back the twelve tribes of Israel.

James was quoting Amos: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”. Closing up the breaches is the binding up of the breach in Isaiah 30: when he gathers the twelve tribes of Israel back again. Right now the tabernacle is still fallen; we are trying to gather ourselves together. “and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name”. Possess means own. We are going to own the remnant of Edom and all the nations. The heathen called by his name are those who call themselves Jews and Christians. Jew comes from Judah, which means praise of God, so Amalek is saying they are the praise of God, and they're not. Christian means anointed ones, calling themselves God's anointed. All of them that call themselves by those names, we are going to possess, “saith the Lord that doeth this”: he is going to make sure that thing is done.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:12
precepts.why:
Simeon's words, “That the residue of men might seek after the Lord”, can be confusing. How are they going to seek after the Lord? Isaiah answers it: “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.”

They will seek after the Lord in captivity. There is no we're equal to you, we're ruling with you. The nations don't get a pass for all the evil they did. They are going to learn God's laws, his statutes and his commandments, and they will learn them in slavery, serving Israel. Whoever does not want to follow it shall be put to death. That is what the Bible says.

People online say the door is open for everyone, that God is going to take everybody in the same way. They don't understand. The residue of men seek the Lord by serving the kingdom of Israel, and the nation or kingdom that will not serve shall perish and be utterly wasted.

precepts.label: Zechariah 14:16
precepts.why:
Here is more on how the residue of men will seek after the Lord: “And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

What do they have to keep? The feast of tabernacles. The nations that are left will worship the King and keep the feast. When is the feast of tabernacles? The seventh month, the fifteenth day. So we are going to have to teach that to the nations: in the seventh month, on the fifteenth day, you go up towards Jerusalem to worship the King and you keep the feast of tabernacles.

That is what it means that the residue of men seek after the Lord. They come up under Israel, learning and keeping God's law, the law they would not keep before. It does not contradict Amos 9:12; it says the same thing. Amos just made it plain, while the way Simeon put it leaves people asking what it means.

precepts.label: Zechariah 14:17
precepts.why:
There may be some rebellious heathen out there: “And it shall be, that whoso will not come up of all the families of the earth unto Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, even upon them shall be no rain.”

That is judgment. No rain means famine, no rain means dearth, no rain means death. Read on: “And if the family of Egypt go not up, and come not, that have no rain; there shall be the plague, wherewith the Lord will smite the heathen that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

So when Acts 15 says “That the residue of men might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called”, it is not an open door where everyone is equal. The residue of men will seek the Lord in servitude, keeping the feast, and those who refuse get no rain and the plague. And the Gentiles upon whom his name is called, those who call themselves Jews and Christians, God's praise and God's anointed: chains for them.
