thread.text: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?

classes.title: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

precepts.label: Jeremiah 14:2
precepts.why:
When Paul was led into the castle, the chief captain asked, “Canst thou speak Greek? Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?” He took Paul for a specific Egyptian. “But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus”. Paul passed for an Egyptian. Moses passed for an Egyptian. Joseph passed for an Egyptian. Christ passed too: his family ran into Africa from white folks. What more do you possibly need at this point?

Jeremiah shows what Judah looked like: “Judah mourneth, and the gates thereof languish; they are black unto the ground; and the cry of Jerusalem is gone up.” Jeremiah is speaking of the same situation he wrote of in Lamentations, when Babylon came, overthrew us and starved us. We became blacker to the ground: dark, swelled bellies, ribs showing, ribs touching. That is how we looked when Babylon besieged us for those years.

Some try to say it is only symbolic. No: it is the same thing, and Jeremiah, who wrote Lamentations, is saying the same thing in both places. Calling it symbolic is simple and unfaithful and weak.

So the chief captain looking at a Jew and seeing an Egyptian makes sense. Judah was black, and a Jew of Tarsus could pass for an Egyptian because our people looked like the people of Africa. Israel sits in Western Asia bordering North Africa, one land mass, and all the native inhabitants of that region were nonwhite.

thread.label: Romans 6:16-17
thread.text: Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?

classes.title: Eleutherophobia the Fear of Freedom

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:20
precepts.why:
“Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” That is the million-dollar question: who do you give your service to? Money? The spirit of fornication? Alcoholism? The big-mouthed black woman that sleeps right next to you? Weakness as a man? Fear? Satan whispering that God can never use you because of your past? When you come into this truth and apply it, you are a new creature; old things are passed away.

“But God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin, but ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you.” What is that form of doctrine? “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.” The law and the testimony, the commandments and the testimony of Christ, is the doctrine delivered to us, and we obeyed it from the heart.

Thank God you understand your mission. You have your crown; it is already there, and it is for you to keep it on your head. You erase yourself out of the book of life; you are already ordained to get it. Will you hold on? “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.”

Your opponent is not the brothers that look like you. First it is the man in the mirror, and sin is the op. Use this Bible to shoot down all sin that opposes you, and put your energy there. Many cannot function without an oppressor, because with freedom comes change and responsibility. Choose this day who your Lord is: sin unto death, or obedience to the law and the testimony unto righteousness.

thread.label: Romans 8:17
thread.text: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.

classes.title: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.label: Revelation 2:26
precepts.why:
In Psalms 2 the Father says to Christ, “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession. Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.” Christ is going to inherit all these nations and rule the planet.

All that Christ was given, we share, because we are “joint-heirs with Christ”. That is what a joint heir is: what Christ gets, he is going to give to us. Here is the proof: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”.

This is what we read in Psalms 2 that Christ is going to get, but because we are joint heirs, we are going to get it too. “As the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father.” The same honor and glory the Father gave to Christ, Christ says, I am going to give you that same power.

All we have to do, brothers, is endure to the end. “If so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together”: he that overcometh and keepeth his works unto the end is the one who receives power over the nations.

precepts.label: Revelation 1:6
precepts.why:
Psalms 2 goes on after the Father gives Christ the heathen for his inheritance: “Be wise now therefore, O ye kings”. Who are these kings? Revelation shows you: Christ “hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father”.

That is a message to us, advice and a command: be wise, O ye kings. “Be instructed, ye judges of the earth.” Christ is calling us judges of the earth. We might look like knuckles right now, but just give us time.

Paul says the same thing: “Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?” And the saints are not everybody who believes on Jesus: “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”. The saints are the Israelites, and the Israelites will judge this planet. Christ said the twelve that followed him “shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

So being heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ means being made kings and priests, the rulers and judges of the earth with him. If that is our future, Paul asks, why can we not judge the smallest matters among ourselves now? Be wise, be instructed, and endure.

thread.label: Romans 8:28
thread.text: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.

thread.label: Romans 8:29-30
thread.text: For whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son, that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.

classes.title: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.label: Amos 3:1-2
precepts.why:
“For whom he did foreknow”. Foreknow means knew from the past. Who did God know from the past? Everybody? The church? No. That has to be stressed, especially on the street, because people are so brainwashed with supersessionism, replacement theology, that they say foreknow means everybody in the church.

Amos settles it: “Hear this word that the Lord hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, You only have I known of all the families of the earth”. The family God knew is the family he brought up out of Egypt, the children of Israel. So it is no church he is talking about: no Presbyterian, no Catholic, all that garbage.

“therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities”. Because he knew us, we were punished.

Paul could have said Judah and Israel plainly, as he does in Hebrews and in Romans 9, but in many of his epistles he uses other words for the 12 tribes. “whom he did foreknow” is one of them: the 12 tribes, the only family on earth he has known.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:25
precepts.why:
“whom he called, them he also justified”. Who is being justified? Isaiah answers: “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” The only ones being justified are all the seed of Israel. It is not talking about the Catholics, not the Jehovah's Witnesses, not any of those false religions.

That is why there is predestination in the Bible. People love to say there is no such thing, but there is, for the 12 tribes of Israel. We were his people in the past, we are going to be his people today and forevermore; we are predestined to be his chosen forever. Whether we as individuals make it or not is up to each individual.

And “whom he justified, them he also glorified”: the seed of Israel that is justified in the Lord “shall glory.” The whole chain of Romans 8:29-30, foreknown, predestinated, called, justified and glorified, runs through the seed of Israel, whom God will transform into the image of his Son, Christ, “that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.”

precepts.label: Isaiah 48:12
precepts.why:
“Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called”. Who did he call? “Hearken unto me, O Jacob and Israel, my called; I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.” Jacob and Israel are his called.

So he is not calling all nations on the planet earth. He is only calling Israel. He is not calling Catholics, Jehovah's Witnesses, Baptists. The teaching that the called are everybody in the church all goes back to replacement theology, which came about through the Catholic church, and then the Protestant church that many of us grew up in, which teaches the same thing.

Put Amos, Isaiah 45 and Isaiah 48 together and Romans 8:29-30 opens up: the ones he foreknew, the ones he called, the ones he justified are the 12 tribes of Israel, predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son.

thread.label: Romans 11:1-6, 26
thread.text: I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

classes.title: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:4
precepts.why:
“I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid.” The answer is no: God has not cast away the 12 tribes of Israel. “For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.” Read that first verse on the street and it tells you what the subject is about.

Paul speaks of “a remnant according to the election of grace.” Who is the elect? Isaiah says: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me.” We are the elect. Israel is the elect, not all nations. This is where Paul is getting that from.

Paul even says “God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew”: there is that word again, the same as Romans 8:29, so we did not even have to go to Amos 3; Paul deals with it here. Elijah thought he was by himself, but God answered, “I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal.” The elect remnant is Israel.

“And so all Israel shall be saved”. And so, meaning as a result of all that has been said: all 12 tribes shall be saved. “For this is my covenant unto them”: unto the 12 tribes of Israel, the elect of Isaiah 45.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 10:33
precepts.why:
“And if by grace, then is it no more of works”. A Christian will try to hem you up with that: see, my brother, it's not about works. Christians assume that when Paul used the word works he meant thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not commit adultery. That is not what Paul is talking about at all.

Nehemiah shows what the works are: “For the shewbread, and for the continual meat offering, and for the continual burnt offering, of the sabbaths, of the new moons, for the set feasts, and for the holy things, and for the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.”

Stress that last part: “all the work of the house of our God.” Those are the works Paul is speaking of: the works of the temple, the works of animal sacrifice, the offerings and things of that nature.

So the remnant chosen by grace is not chosen by the temple works of sacrifice and offering; it does not throw away the commandments. The elect of Israel are kept by grace, and all Israel shall be saved.

thread.label: Romans 11:17-21
thread.text: And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree;

classes.title: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.label: Jeremiah 11:16
precepts.why:
“And if some of the branches be broken off”. The branches broken off are Judah. Jeremiah shows the olive tree and its breaking: “The Lord called thy name, A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit: with the noise of a great tumult he hath kindled fire upon it, and the branches of it are broken.”

God himself named his people a green olive tree, fair and of goodly fruit. That is the tree Paul speaks of. And the fire kindled on it with a great tumult is how the branches came to be broken.

Why were they broken? Paul answers: “because of unbelief they were broken off”. Judah's unbelief caused them to be broken off.

So when the wild olive tree, the northern kingdom, is graffed in among them, it is graffed into God's own green olive tree. “Boast not against the branches”: do not boast against Judah. “thou bearest not the root, but the root thee”. The root is Christ, and Christ is the one that keeps the northern kingdom graffed in with Judah. “Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee.”

precepts.label: Ezekiel 37:16-17
precepts.why:
“and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them”. That is what Ezekiel 37 shows: “Moreover, thou son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions”.

“And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand.” That is the grafting: the stick of Joseph, Ephraim and the house of Israel, joined to the stick of Judah, and the two become one in God's hand.

So the wild olive tree is not the nations; it is the northern kingdom being joined back with Judah. That is why Paul warns, “Boast not against the branches.” Zechariah 12:7 says the same: that they do not magnify themselves against Judah. That magnify is telling you: do not be highminded, do not boast.

“Be not highminded, but fear”. The root that bears the graffed-in branch is Christ, and he is the one that holds the two sticks together as one.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 5:42
precepts.why:
Solomon said, “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.” Paul says the same thing in different words: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning”. Our learning today. There are no new incidents on this earth; everything that was done in the past is reoccurring.

Ezra shows it with a ring: “And he said unto me, I will liken my judgment unto a ring”. A ring is like a circle. “like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first”. Slackness means slow: there is no slowness of the last judgments and no swiftness of the first. His judgments on the earth are a continual event that reoccurs over and over; it is the same thing.

That is why Paul said to comfort ourselves through what is written in the testimonies of the past: what we are living is a reoccurring event. To deal with these reoccurring events we must read the history and testimonies of our ancestors, “that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

We see it now. Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image and gathered the rulers to its dedication, setting up a one world religion; today pastors gather to pray over and dedicate a towering gold statue of Donald Trump. What we read in Daniel 3 is coming to pass again, because the judgments go around like a ring.

precepts.label: Hosea 12:10
precepts.why:
The things written aforetime were written for our learning, and Hosea shows how they were written: “I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.”

All the prophets spoke: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, even Hosea. God multiplied visions, and he used similitudes, or parables, by the ministry of the prophets, comparing one thing to another.

That is how the scriptures teach us today. The past is a similitude of what is happening now, and by comparing one thing to another we can see our own time in what was written. The last beast of Revelation 13 is described with the leopard, the bear and the lion of Daniel 7: it carries the attributes of Greece, Persia and Media, and Babylon. The golden image of Daniel 3 stands again in our day.

So we read the prophets as similitudes, and through patience and comfort of the scriptures we have hope, because the Most High already showed in the past what he will do in the future.

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 1:3-4
precepts.why:
“That we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Where does that comfort come from? Paul says, “Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort”. The God of all comfort, and we find that comfort in this Bible.

“Who comforteth us in all our tribulation”. Christ comforts us in all our tribulations. The things written aforetime show the Israelites going into captivity after captivity and committing sin after sin, but they also show the redemption: when the Israelites came out of captivity, they had to keep the commandments. That is our comfort, and our hope is that a saviour is coming to redeem the children of Israel.

And he comforts us for a reason: “that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.” Are our people in trouble today? Absolutely. So what are we supposed to comfort our people with? This Bible.

We have to let our people know there is a better way. Go this way, not that way. Do not go to the left and do not go to the right. Go to this Bible, the straight and narrow path. The comfort the scriptures gave us is the comfort we carry to our people.

Imagine us being perfectly joined together as one man. Imagine how much we could get done if we thought as one man, with the same mind, the same spirit and the same judgment. That is called unity.

It is the same unity Paul calls for in Ephesians 4: “Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace”, “Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man”. That perfect man is the one man. Brothers are going to offend brothers and sisters are going to offend sisters; get over it. There are bigger things to worry about than your feelings. Keep the unity no matter what, for the perfecting of the saints.

precepts.label: Acts 5:30
precepts.why:
Peter and the other apostles told our wicked elders, “We ought to obey God rather than men.” And then: “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.” Christ was lynched.

Why does Peter call it a tree? What is the cross made of? Wood. Hanging on the cross is hanging on a tree. He says it again in Acts 10:39: “whom they slew and hanged on a tree”. Some say he was hanged from an actual tree, but Thomas said, “Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.” What would they need nails for on a tree? His hands and feet were nailed to a cross, and he hung there for hours, lynched slowly. And they mocked him: “If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.” A man hanging by the neck from a tree could not be answering questions; he would be choking to death. So Peter called the crucifixion hanging on a tree, and the two men beside him were lynched too.

It is ironic: the same way the white man lynched us in slavery and into the 60s is the same way our King was killed. That is why Galatians 3:13 matters: “Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. Christ was hanged on a tree under the same curse as his people.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 21:23
precepts.why:
Hanging was our punishment too, in the law, for the wicked: “And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree:” “His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled”.

That is what Paul quotes in Galatians 3:13: “Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. The curse of the law means its condemnation; being made a curse means being put to death for us, a sacrifice.

So what happened to our people? We were hanged on trees, because we went under the curses. Christ went under the curses of Deuteronomy 28 along with us, and we are under the curses too. He that is hanged is accursed of God: Christ was hanged on a tree, and so were we. The King and his children were hanged.

And the pattern keeps turning, like a ring. In Egypt, when Moses said, let my people go to serve God, Pharaoh called us idle and took away the straw but kept the tale of bricks, with a quota of 2,000 bricks; the records name Yupa son of Uriah, a Hebrew, 370 short. Here it was a quota of 200 or 500 pounds of cotton. The officers set over us, the black elites, pastors and politicians in the white man's pocket, turned on Moses and Aaron for making Pharaoh hate them. It is the same curse, the same judgment, until Christ, who bore the curse, redeems us from it.

precepts.why:
Pastor Philip Anthony Mitchell preached that black people use their ethnicity as an idol, that black people don't like white people for something they cannot control, and that Ephesians 2 is about joining blacks and whites together through Christ into one family. Did he forget about slavery? He leans on Ephesians 2:14: “For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us.” So we have to deal with the us. Who is Paul talking about?

Paul uses two specific words, our and us. To know who they are, go back to the top of the letter and see who it was written to: “Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints which are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus.”

The letter was written to the saints which are at Ephesus. So the question becomes, who are the saints according to the holy scriptures? Answer that, and you know who the our and the us are in chapter 2. It is not blacks and whites coming together.

precepts.label: Psalms 148:14

When the brothers were dealing with Fred Price and brought out the scripture about the saints, he asked, are you saying all the saints in the New Testament have to be the children of Israel? Yes. He said he didn't necessarily see that. But you know what Christianity has never been able to do? Show another definition of saints in the scripture. They are not going to be able to. The only saints in the scriptures are the twelve tribes of Israel.

So the saints which are at Ephesus are Israelites, and the us of Ephesians 2 is the nation of Israel. This isn't talking about blacks and whites coming together, like Pastor Mitchell was saying.

precepts.label: Acts 13:17
precepts.why:
Ephesians 2:12 says that at that time they were “without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world.” Christians will say, well, you have to deal with those strangers. So let's see who the strangers are.

“The God of this people of Israel chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they dwelt as strangers in the land of Egypt.” The book of Acts is saying that the God of Israel chose our fathers, so the people Paul was speaking to in Antioch were Israelites. And who dwelt as strangers in the land of Egypt? The nation of Israel.

So those strangers are the Israelites. The scripture calls Israel strangers, and that is who Ephesians is speaking to when it says strangers from the covenants of promise.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 1:1
precepts.why:
“Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.” Peter writes to the strangers, and the strangers are Israel, scattered abroad.

Put the map up and focus on Asia, which is Asia Minor. There you see Ephesus, and right next to it Colosse. That is what we are dealing with: the letter to the Colossians, and since Pastor Mitchell brought up Ephesus, which is right there in Asia next to Colosse, the letter to the Ephesians too.

So the saints at Ephesus and the strangers Peter wrote to are the same people: Israelites scattered through Asia. When Paul says they were “strangers from the covenants of promise”, he is writing to scattered Israel, not to the nations.

precepts.label: Romans 9:4-5
precepts.why:
Christians never address the covenants of promise. The only time the Lord made a covenant with all nations was in Genesis 9, when he said he would not destroy the world by water any more. In regards to the covenants, the Lord made covenant with Abraham, and through his seed, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. He never made any other covenants with other nations.

Paul says it plainly: “Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises; Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came.” The Bible is letting you know that Christ came for the Israelites, and he made the covenants of promise for the Israelites. No other nation.

The question was even put to ChatGPT live in class: did God ever enter into a covenant with all nations or only Israel, answered with KJV scriptures. Its answer: God made a universal covenant with all humanity through Noah after the flood; the covenant of the law at Sinai was only with Israel, not with all nations; and the new covenant as prophesied is with the house of Israel and the house of Judah. They know that, but they try to force this all nations could be saved doctrine. It is not in the Bible.

So “strangers from the covenants of promise” can only be read one way: the covenant of promise is only with Israel.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 46:27
precepts.why:
Ephesians 2:13: “But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” Who was afar off? We deal with precepts. These Christians like to say, let's go to the Greek, let's go to this book, let's go to that. We stick to the scriptures and stay within our book.

“But fear not thou, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel: for, behold, I will save thee from afar off.” It is Israel who is afar off.

It's really that simple. The ones who were far off and are made nigh by the blood of Christ are Israel. Then verse 14: “For he is our peace.” Our peace, not everybody's peace. Reading from verse 12 down to verse 14, the our becomes plain: these Ephesians in Ephesus are Israelites scattered in Ephesus.

precepts.label: Isaiah 9:6-8
precepts.why:
Ephesians says “he is our peace”, so go to the prophecy of the Prince of Peace. “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”: unto us, possessive again. “and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.”

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever.” When it's time for Christ to return and the Israelites to reign, there is not going to be any end to it. “The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.”

Then: “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel.” So our peace is Israel's peace. Christ is the peace that brings both nations, the southern and the northern kingdom, back together. That is the both he made one.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 37:21-22

When Christ came on the scene, he abolished animal sacrifice. And it was never prophesied that Israel would be joined back together through animal sacrifice, but only through Jesus the Christ.

“Thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land.” He gathers the children of Israel from among the heathen, so you would have Israelites living in places like Galatia, Ephesus and Colosse.

So he is our peace: the Israelites' peace. These Christians in America do not know what they are talking about. Turning Ephesians 2 into blacks and whites coming together is a racist lie. Christianity is nothing but white supremacy, because it is not backed up with the Bible whatsoever.

“As the sun when it ariseth in the high heaven; so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house.” The way she sets it up and the way she does things: that is her beauty.

Ephesians 5 says “as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” Submitting “as unto the Lord” means listening to your husband as you would to Christ, and assisting him in what he wants. It is the house of the husband, the house of Abiel, not the house of Abiel and his wife. When you understand whose house it is, you understand whose desires set what the house is supposed to be. If he wants a sound home, give him a sound home; if he wants a clean house, give him a clean house. The confusion comes when a sister thinks her aspirations supersede his. We are on the same team, but somebody is the CEO of the team making the decisions for the franchise.

Be honest, sisters: in the ordering of the house, most husbands let you do pretty much what you want. I don’t give a damn about them pots. The drapes, the knives and forks, the couch set: most men are not tripping over that. As long as he comes home to good food and a clean house, however she got there is fine. So stop acting like submission is straight slavery; most of that is exaggeration. If she wants to lift the carpet and vacuum the cushion every morning, that is her ordering, and that is her beauty.

For the brothers whose wives do not want to clean except when company comes over, cleaning for presentation: you have to order your house. Tell her this is not the desire of your home, this is what needs to be done, and demand it. For the brothers with neat freaks, that is a blessing; sometimes you have to calm them down.

This is also what Titus 2 means by “keepers at home”: a good wife in the ordering of her house, not idle, not a busybody in everybody else’s house, taking care of home.

thread.label: Ephesians 6:5
thread.text: Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as unto Christ;

classes.title: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.label: Colossians 3:22
precepts.why:
“Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh”. These are the same scriptures Esau uses to justify slavery, and that dumb black people use to reject the Bible. But it is not talking about chattel slavery. It is what was read in Leviticus 25 and Exodus: Israel, in a time of stability, still following the laws on selling yourself to work if you were poor or owed debts.

Leviticus says it: “And if thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant: But as an hired servant, and as a sojourner, he shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile”. Then he departs, he and his children, back to his own family, because “Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour”. Rigour is chattel slavery, and God forbade it over a brother.

Colossians says the same: “Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God”. The servants were Israelites, Hebrew servants, hired servants.

Exodus 21 shows the master: “If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.” If his master gave him a wife and she bore children, he could say, “I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free”. Why would he say, I love my master? Because the brother treated him real good. That is what “Servants, obey in all things your masters” is talking about.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:18
precepts.why:
“Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward.” This is in the slave Bible; Esau used it. But the good and gentle masters and the froward ones were Israelite masters. The law said not to deal with Israel with rigour, meaning hard, yet some of them were like that. The froward ones are the ones who did not really like you.

“For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully. For what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God.”

Why would a master not like his servant? Exodus 22: a thief found breaking in, “If the sun be risen upon him, there shall be blood shed for him; for he should make full restitution; if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.” That is different from a poor brother saying, I lack food, clothing and shelter, will you help me? If I broke into your house, stole all your stuff and got caught, now I have to work for you, and you are not going to like me too much. You have to see him every morning.

So Peter tells servants to be subject even to the froward master, and to take it patiently. It is Israelite servitude under the law, not chattel slavery.

precepts.label: Titus 2:9
precepts.why:
“Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again”: not talking back. Esau perverted this. But read on: “Not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.” To purloin is to steal something: sticky fingers, a kleptomaniac. That is what was read in Exodus 22. Paul is dealing with brothers who were stealing, got caught, and were sold to make restitution.

Philemon shows it plainly. Paul met Onesimus while under arrest. He had been a servant to Philemon, and he ran away: “For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receive him for ever; Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved”. Deal with him like a brother beloved.

Was he a servant because he was poor, or because he did something bad? “If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account”. He owed something because he stole or broke something, and Paul said, put it on my account.

So Paul was dealing with servants who were Hebrews, Israelites in servitude to other Israelites. Chattel slavery came later, when Israel fell by the edge of the sword and was led away captive into all nations, under Rome, Spain and Portugal, France, Britain and the United States.

precepts.label: Galatians 1:6
precepts.why:
How did “Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters” become a scripture used to justify chattel slavery? This is what they did: “I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: Which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.”

That is what Esau did. They took this Bible and perverted it. The servants of Ephesians, Colossians, Peter and Titus were Israelites serving Israelites under the law, hired servants and sojourners who went free in the seventh year and at the jubilee, and whom God said not to rule with rigour. Esau took those scriptures and made them into the slave Bible, to justify ruling over us with rigour in chattel slavery.

And dumb black people, seeing how Esau used them, reject the Bible altogether, not knowing it was perverted.

But God says, “Fear not: for I have redeemed thee”. He gave Egypt for our ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for us, because we are precious in his sight, and he will give men for us. He will bring our seed from the east and gather us from the west, say to the north, give up, and deliver us into the glorious liberty of the children of God. That is the true jubilee.

precepts.label: Colossians 2:1
precepts.why:
Paul writes “To the saints and faithful brethren in Christ which are at Colosse,” just as Ephesians is written to the saints at Ephesus. Same concept: these are Israelites in Asia. Then he says, “Since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus.” What is Paul saying? He never went to Colosse. The spirit was so heavy in Ephesus that it spread all throughout Asia, and Paul heard there was another congregation over in Colosse that was fervent in spirit too, so he wrote to them.

Chapter 2 proves it: “For I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh.” Why had they not seen Paul’s face? Because he never went to Laodicea, and he never went to Colosse. For anyone who wondered why there is no precept in Acts of Paul going to Colosse, that is the precept.

On the map, Ephesus is in the middle, Colosse to the right of it, Laodicea above it (the Laodicea you read about in Revelation), and Hierapolis, known as one of the wealthy cities of that region. The gospel spread through all those cities, “as it is in all the world.” Acts 19 says Paul turned away much people “not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia” from the goddess Diana, the woman all Asia worshipped, just as America worships the Virgin Mary. The spirit was so heavy on the apostle that places he never physically went to were getting touched.

thread.label: Colossians 1:7-8
thread.text: As ye also learned of Epaphras our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ;

classes.title: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.label: Acts 18:1-8
precepts.why:
The Colossians learned the truth “of Epaphras our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ.” That is how they woke up: one brother heard it and said, I am going to teach all of you. Acts 18 shows the same concept at Corinth: “After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth.”

“And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house.” If you were in the synagogue, you were practicing the law of sacrifice. Crispus was the chief ruler of it, and he believed on Christ, just like a lot of us were practicing Christianity and then believed. “And many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.” It started with him and then the others took hold of it.

Paul was actually at Corinth, though. With Epaphras it was different: he was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He said, that is true, I believe it, I am going to go teach it. That is just like today when somebody sees IUIC on YouTube, prints out flyers and starts hitting the city, and then this school pops up and that school pops up. We are the continuation of the acts of the apostles, and when we read these scriptures we have to put ourselves in them, because we are doing the exact same thing.

precepts.label: Colossians 4:12-13
precepts.why:
Epaphras, the “faithful minister of Christ” the Colossians learned from, comes up again at the end of the letter: “Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, saluteth you, always labouring fervently for you in prayers, that ye may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God.”

“For I bear him record, that he hath a great zeal for you, and them that are in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis.” On the map you see Colosse, then Laodicea and Hierapolis, all in that same region. Epaphras was one of them, and he carried the work through all three cities.

Epaphras was putting in serious work. He heard the truth, believed it, taught it, and kept labouring fervently in prayer for the congregations he raised up, with great zeal for them. He is the example of the brother who takes the truth and gets the ground running in his own region.

precepts.label: Philemon 1:23-25
precepts.why:
In the epistle to Philemon, Epaphras shows up again: “There salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus.” Paul calls Epaphras his fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus. But why is he mentioned in the letter to Philemon? Because Philemon was also of Colosse.

“Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellowlabourers.” Remember Demas: when you read Timothy, Demas forsook this truth. “The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.”

The letters Paul wrote from Rome to that region, Ephesians, Colossians and Philemon, overlap and name the same people because he wrote them at the same time and to the same place. Following Epaphras through them shows how the work in Colosse spread from one faithful brother to a whole company of labourers.

precepts.label: Philemon 1:1-2
precepts.why:
“Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer, And to our beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house.”

Philemon was of Colosse, the same place Epaphras taught. So it started with Epaphras, and then others came: Philemon, a dearly beloved fellow labourer, Apphia, Archippus the fellow soldier, and a church meeting in Philemon’s house.

That is how the truth spreads. One brother, a faithful minister of Christ, wakes up and teaches, and then fellow labourers rise up around him and congregations meet in houses, the same way schools pop up one after another today.

precepts.label: Philemon 1:10
precepts.why:
“I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds.” Why would Paul write to Philemon on behalf of Onesimus? Because they had to be in the same place: Colosse.

Colossians 4:9 calls Onesimus “a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you,” one of the Colossians. And he is the same Onesimus Paul begot in his bonds and sent back to Philemon.

So the letters tie together. Epaphras, Philemon and Onesimus all belong to Colosse, and the epistles to the Colossians and to Philemon were carried to the same city, to the same congregation of Israelites that had learned the truth of Epaphras.

precepts.label: Colossians 4:18
precepts.why:
“The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.” Then the subscript many Bibles carry: “Written from Rome to the Colossians by Tychicus and Onesimus.” Some people’s Bibles may not have that line, so it was put up on the screen for everyone to see.

This epistle was written from Rome, while Paul was under house arrest, which parallels Acts 28, and sent to the church at Colosse by Tychicus and Onesimus. Ephesians, Colossians, Philemon, Philippians, 1 Timothy, Titus and 2 Timothy were written in that same time, which is why they overlap and speak of similar topics and the same people.

Paul never went to Colosse. He wrote to a congregation raised up by Epaphras, and sent the letter by brothers who were themselves of that city.

precepts.label: Colossians 4:7-10
precepts.why:
“All my state shall Tychicus declare unto you, who is a beloved brother, and a faithful minister and fellowservant in the Lord.” Tychicus carried the letter. “With Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They shall make known unto you all things which are done here.” Onesimus was one of the Colossians.

“Aristarchus my fellowprisoner saluteth you, and Marcus, sister’s son to Barnabas.” If Marcus is Barnabas’ sister’s son, that makes Marcus his nephew: John Mark.

That is the same John Mark that Paul and Barnabas had their dispute over at the end of Acts 15. Barnabas was sticking up for him because he was his nephew. So these closing names are not filler; they tie the letter to the history of the apostles and the men who carried the work.

precepts.label: Acts 15:37-41
precepts.why:
“And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark. But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work.” That is the Marcus of Colossians 4:10, Barnabas’ sister’s son.

“And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus; And Paul chose Silas, and departed, being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God. And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches.”

It shows you not just anybody can travel. Paul gave him a chance, and when it came to the work he was nowhere to be found; he came up missing. Paul said straight, I do not care if that is your nephew, he is not traveling with me any more. Barnabas said, that is my sister’s son, I am taking him with me. You can understand that dynamic. The faithful ministers like Epaphras are the ones who stay with the work.

thread.label: Colossians 1:26-27
thread.text: Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints:

classes.title: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.label: Matthew 4:15
precepts.why:
Colossians speaks of “the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints,” once again using that term saints, and then of “the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles.” There is a Christian out there watching who will say, see, Gentiles means the other nations. Matthew shows who the Gentiles are.

“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” Zebulun and Naphtali are Israelite tribes of the northern kingdom, and their land is called Galilee of the Gentiles.

So the mystery among the Gentiles is that the northern kingdom can come back into the fold: “which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.” We had no hope unless Christ came and died for us. There was no repentance and no reconciliation, except through Christ.

precepts.label: Ephesians 3:3-6
precepts.why:
Ephesians, Colossians and Philemon were written in the same period, around AD 60 to 67 while Paul was under house arrest in Rome, to the same region. That is why they overlap and speak of the same things, like this mystery.

“How that by revelation he made known unto me the mystery; (as I wrote afore in few words, Whereby, when ye read, ye may understand my knowledge in the mystery of Christ) Which in other ages was not made known unto the sons of men, as it is now revealed unto his holy apostles and prophets by the Spirit; That the Gentiles should be fellowheirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel.”

That is the mystery: the animal sacrifice is done away with, no longer in play, and the northern and southern kingdom now have a chance to come back into the fold with Christ. Partakers of his promise, the covenant: the promises were not made through animal sacrifice but through Christ. That is the same “mystery among the Gentiles” of Colossians 1:27, Christ in you, the hope of glory.

thread.label: Colossians 3:1
thread.text: If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God.

classes.title: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.label: Galatians 3:16-22
precepts.why:
“If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above.” If you decide to repent and follow Christ, this is what you do. If you do not want to accept Christ, it is not for you; all Israel is not Israel, as Romans 9:6 says. Galatians shows who it is for.

“Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made.” Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and from that came the twelve tribes of Israel. “He saith not, And to seeds, as of many”: not to every nation, just that chosen lineage. “But as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.” Through that lineage came Jesus the Christ.

“Wherefore then serveth the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made.” The promise was made to the twelve tribes of Israel. As soon as Christ came on the scene, animal sacrifice was done away with. “Now a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one.”

“Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid.” If a law could have given life, righteousness would have been by the law. “But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe.” That is not talking about everybody. From verse 16 it is the Israelites that believe on Christ who get the promises. There should be no confusion: those are the ones risen with Christ.

precepts.label: Romans 3:29-30
precepts.why:
Galatians says “a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one.” Romans explains it: “Is he the God of the Jews only?” Is he only for the southern kingdom? “Is he not also of the Gentiles?” Is he not also the God of the northern kingdom? “Yes, of the Gentiles also.”

“Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.” The circumcision is Judah, the southern kingdom; the uncircumcision is the northern kingdom. One God justifies both, by faith.

That is who Colossians 3:1 is speaking to: “If ye then be risen with Christ.” Both houses of Israel, Jew and Gentile, who believe on Christ are risen with him, and the promise by faith of Jesus Christ is given to them that believe.

thread.label: Colossians 3:10-11
thread.text: And have put on the new man, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him:

classes.title: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.label: James 1:1
precepts.why:
“Where there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian, bond nor free.” A Christian will say, to hell with all the facts you just showed, because Greeks, Barbarians and Scythians are the other nations. Really, after reading all of that in context? No.

A history of the Jewish diaspora shows that the Jews in the western diaspora basically knew only Greek; their Torah reading and prayer were conducted in Greek, and the scripture was translated into Greek for those communities. So some of our people were called Greeks and some were called Jews, a language difference, but the same people. Barbarian comes from the Greek barbaros, what the early Greeks called all foreigners, including the Romans.

James writes “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.” Would it be a surprise for us to be called Greeks and barbarians? We were scattered abroad throughout the four corners of the earth, and Esau with his demonic self has tried to insert himself in our place.

Israel Redivivus by Frederick Charles Danvers says each tribe was divided into families and subtribes, and later many tribes bearing different names were known collectively to the Greeks as Scythians, the nomadic people of that area. We were scattered everywhere, so we are the Barbarians, we are the Scythians, we are the Greeks. Get mad; this is our book.

precepts.label: Acts 2:10
precepts.why:
Barbarian was the word the Greeks used for all foreigners, including the Romans. And we were the Romans too; that is what mainstream Christianity does not understand today. Acts 2 lists the people gathered at Pentecost: “Phrygia, and Pamphylia, in Egypt, and in the parts of Libya about Cyrene, and strangers of Rome, Jews and proselytes.”

Strangers of Rome. And verse 5 already said who they all were: “And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” Jews, devout men, out of every nation.

So we were called Romans, we were called Greeks, we were called barbarians. When Colossians 3:11 says “neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian,” those are the names Israel carried in the places it was scattered, not the other nations.

precepts.label: Acts 10:34-36
precepts.why:
Colossians 3:11 ends, “but Christ is all, and in all.” Now they will say, see, Christ is in all. Then they go to Acts 10: “Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.”

Read the whole thing: “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ: (he is Lord of all:)” Lord of all what? Lord of all Israel, scattered in every nation.

And Paul clears it up himself in the very next verse of Colossians: “Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved.” Isaiah 45:4 says “Israel mine elect”; Leviticus 20:26 says the Lord has “severed you from other people”; Baruch calls Israel “his beloved.” He is speaking in a language we can understand, not for the heathen. They know good and well this Bible does not belong to them, but in slavery they played on our ignorance. Now the God of Israel has poured His spirit on His people in these last days, and we know what the Bible is talking about.

thread.label: Colossians 3:12-13
thread.text: Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering;

classes.title: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:4
precepts.why:
In verse 11 Paul references us as the Greeks, the Barbarians and the Scythians. Then in verse 12 he says it one more time, plainly: “Put on therefore, as the elect of God”. He is speaking in a language we can understand, not for the heathens to understand. Isaiah tells us who the elect of God is: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”.

Israel is his elect. So the elect of God that Paul is instructing in Colossians 3:12 are Israelites.

They know good and well this Bible don’t belong to them. But in slavery they played on our ignorance. We couldn’t read or write; they taught it to us by oral tradition, wouldn’t let us read the Bible, and gave us the slave Bible where the majority of the Bible wasn’t even there. They wanted to keep us docile, ignorant and misinformed. But there is a God, the God of Israel, who has poured his spirit upon his people in these last days, and now we know what the Bible is talking about: Israel mine elect.

precepts.label: Leviticus 20:26
precepts.why:
Colossians 3:12 calls the elect of God “holy and beloved”. Leviticus tells us how to be holy, and who it is for: “And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.”

Holy means severed, separated from all other nations on the face of the earth. He has severed us from other people, “that ye should be mine”: that ye, you Israelites, should be his people.

So right there in Colossians 3:12 the Lord is saying it ain’t all nations. Just in case anyone was confused by what Paul was saying in verse 11, he clears it up in verse 12. The ones told to put on mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness and longsuffering are the holy people, the ones severed from the other nations to be his.

precepts.label: Baruch 3:36
precepts.why:
Holy, and beloved. Baruch shows who the beloved is: “He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” Israel is his beloved, and it is to Israel he gave all the way of knowledge.

So the “holy and beloved” of Colossians 3:12 are the children of Israel: holy because he severed them from other people, beloved because he calls Israel his beloved.

That is why the Lord, through the apostle Paul, instructs the Colossians on how to deal with one another: “bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another”. Why? Because we are the same people. We are the sons and daughters of the living God, and there is a way we have to govern ourselves and treat each other.

thread.label: Colossians 3:22
thread.text: Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God:

classes.title: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.label: Ezekiel 25:8
precepts.why:
“Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh”. Going precept upon precept and in context, these servants would have to be Israelites, and these masters would have to be Israelites. It is a scripture they cherry-picked to fit their evil narrative. In The Religious Instruction of the Negroes in the United States they wrote of us, the 697,697 slaves of the 1790 census, as the original stock, in a state of absolute heathenism. They inserted themselves as the people and made us the heathens.

But the Lord did say this would happen: “Thus saith the Lord God; Because that Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen”. Moab and Seir look at the house of Judah and call us heathen.

How did we become like the heathen? By following after the heathen: celebrating their pagan rituals, Christmas, Thanksgiving; eating crab, shrimp, pork, lobster; praying to a white man. That is what makes us heathenistic. So the servants of Colossians 3:22 are Israel, and the enemy calling Judah heathen is only what the Lord already said Moab and Seir would say.

precepts.label: Galatians 3:7-8
precepts.why:
Our enemies would like to think God cast us away because we became like the heathen, and that he isn't going to redeem us. Even with us becoming heathens, this is what the Lord says: “Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham. And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.”

The scripture foreseeing: the Lord already knew we were going to become heathens. He saw that this would happen to us, and he would justify us through faith, through Christ. They may be mad all over again; it doesn't matter. We are still God's chosen people.

So the heathen Galatians speaks of justifying is Israel fallen into heathenism, the same servants Colossians 3:22 speaks to. That justification is only for one people, as Isaiah 45:25 shows.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:25
precepts.why:
Galatians says God would “justify the heathen through faith”. Who is that justification for? “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” Shall the seed of what be justified? Israel.

So it is what it is. Yes, we became heathen, following after the heathen in their holidays, their foods and their white image; but we are still going to be justified through Christ, and we shall glory. The justification is for one people, the seed of Israel.

That is why the servants of Colossians 3:22 are Israelites and not the slave master's property to be taught his religion. The masters' books called us heathens in need of their instruction, but the Lord had already written that all the seed of Israel, heathen as we became, would be justified in him.

precepts.label: Acts 5:31
precepts.why:
In 1673 Mr. Baxter published his Christian Directory with directions to masters in foreign plantations who have negroes and other slaves, a rubric to follow. In their evil minds they really believed they were masters. Did the Lord allow this to happen? Absolutely. But that is not what Colossians 3:22 is talking about. The first direction: remember that they have immortal souls and are equally capable of salvation with yourselves. That is where the false sense of equality comes from. It comes from slavery; it comes from Christianity.

Who is salvation for? “Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.” A savior brings salvation, and that salvation is only for the children of Israel.

They believed they could be saved and then us; they are the people, and we come after. That is not how it goes. The same directions said that they and you are equally under the government and laws of God, and that is incorrect: we are not equal with these people. Christ was exalted to give repentance to Israel, so the servants of Colossians and the salvation preached to them belong to Israel.

precepts.label: Daniel 9:24
precepts.why:
The slave masters' directions said that God is their reconciled tender father. God is our reconciled father, but that reconciliation is not for everybody. What does re mean? To do again: repeat, redo. Reconcile means to do it again. So if they wrote that reconciliation was for the slaves, that means they knew who we are.

Reconciliation cannot apply to the other nations, because they were never a people close or near to God. The Israelites are the only ones that have been close or near to God. Daniel shows it: “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.”

That is determined upon Daniel's people and holy city, and the most Holy anointed is Christ. Through Christ we get our reconciliation. So the very masters who twisted Colossians 3:22 wrote down, in their own directions, that their slaves were the people God reconciles: Israel.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:48
precepts.why:
The third direction to the masters: serve your necessities by your slaves so as to prefer God's interest and their spiritual and everlasting happiness; teach them the way to heaven. So in want of all things we wanted food, clothing, housing, shelter, and we also got that old time religion from them too.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. In want of all things: even our religion had to come from the enemy we were serving.

The next page shows what that religion was for. They wrote that we were redeemed with them by Christ from the slavery of Satan and may live with them in the liberty of the saints in glory. They want us to go to heaven with them and live with them. That's called hell. That mind was beaten into us: a brother on the street asked if the Edomite could be saved, and said if he goes to hell, so will I, because he doesn't want to go anywhere without his master. That is the want of all things the curse brought, and why the master's reading of Colossians 3:22 still holds our people.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 5:19
precepts.why:
The masters' own book says of us: they are in the eye of the law property. In the eyes of their laws, we were their property. The Lord told us why: “And it shall come to pass, when ye shall say, Wherefore doeth the Lord our God all these things unto us? then shalt thou answer them, Like as ye have forsaken me, and served strange gods in your land, so shall ye serve strangers in a land that is not yours.”

We are serving strangers in a land that is not ours, a land we are not familiar with. That is the servitude the Lord allowed because we forsook him.

So the slavery here was the curse on Israel for serving strange gods, not the obedience Colossians 3:22 teaches between Israelite servants and Israelite masters. They took the scripture and used it to hold us as property, but the Lord had already told us we would serve strangers.

precepts.label: Lamentations 5:8
precepts.why:
Jeremiah said we would serve strangers in a land that is not ours. The Lamentations goes further: “Servants have ruled over us: there is none that doth deliver us out of their hand.” Servants have ruled over us. This is Bible prophecy.

It happened in the time of Assyria, Babylon, Persia, Greece, Rome, and America in the present day. It keeps happening over and over again. Why? Because we are the people of God. But this is the last time.

So the masters who took Colossians 3:22 and told us “Servants, obey in all things your masters” were themselves the servants ruling over Israel, just as the prophets lamented, with none to deliver us out of their hand.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 5:42
precepts.why:
Servants ruling over us happened with Assyria, Babylon, Persia, Greece, Rome, and America present day. The Lord explains it to Ezra: “And he said unto me, I will liken my judgment unto a ring”.

A ring is a circular motion. You see this curse? It comes right back around, empire after empire, and it keeps happening because we are the people of God. But this is the last time. All praise to the Most High.

So the slavery in America where Colossians 3:22 was used against us is one more turn of that ring of judgment on Israel. It was not the Lord making the white man our rightful master; it was his judgment coming back around on his own people, and it ends with this last time.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 9:37
precepts.why:
We were their property, and they still view us as that. They may have said we were equal in salvation, but while we were here they treated us like beasts: chattel slavery, three-fifths of a man. They never looked at us as their equals.

Nehemiah prayed it: “And it yieldeth much increase unto the kings whom thou hast set over us because of our sins”. This is happening because we sinned against our God. “also they have dominion over our bodies, and over our cattle, at their pleasure, and we are in great distress.” Dominion over our bodies, to look at us as their property, at their pleasure.

Their own book says it plainly: they are in the eye of the law property over which there is an absolute control; and by law or custom we were excluded from education, and by consequence from the reading of the word of God. If we were equal, why were we excluded from education? Because they don't want us to know the truth of the Bible, that servants obey your masters isn't talking about them. They want to keep us docile and uneducated.

precepts.label: Revelation 13:14-15
precepts.why:
Their book says we may, according to the power lodged in our hands, forbid religious meetings, and no independent churches were allowed, so we depended on them alone. It went on during the Inquisition too, when they changed Christianity into the all-inclusive Catholic system and went around killing us, the real Jews, tearing up our safe houses and taking our book. The same thing is going to happen again, because now we know the truth. The only way the lie could hold strong was to destroy anybody who did not get down with it.

Revelation shows it: he “deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles which he had power to do in the sight of the beast; saying to them that dwell on the earth, that they should make an image to the beast”. “And he had power to give life unto the image of the beast”: that is the false image of Christ. “that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed.”

If we did not agree to it, we were killed. Over time our people knew it wasn't true, but they didn't want to be killed, so they went with the lie, generation after generation. But it's a new generation on the earth, and we aren't accepting the lies any more. We know we are the people, and we know what comes with the territory.

precepts.label: Isaiah 32:7
precepts.why:
The masters' book called us the most needy of any people in their country. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too: “The instruments also of the churl are evil: he deviseth wicked devices to destroy the poor with lying words, even when the needy speaketh right.”

The needy in that book is us. The churl devised wicked devices with lying words: cherry-picking “Servants, obey in all things your masters”, writing directions for masters to bring slaves to their religion, forbidding our meetings and our reading.

And even when we speak straight out of the Bible, going precept upon precept, they call it hate speech. That is the needy speaking right and the churl answering with lying words to destroy the poor. So when Colossians 3:22 is read in context, it speaks of Israelite servants and Israelite masters, and the lying words that turned it against us are the churl's devices.

thread.label: Colossians 4:1
thread.text: Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal; knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven.

classes.title: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 19:21
precepts.why:
Colossians 3:22, read in context, says “Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God”. Why? Your master was taking care of your clothes, your raiment, your housing, your food. So why would you disrespect him? Number one, that is your brother. Number two, he is doing this for you: as you do your duties and work, he takes care of you.

Sirach says it: “If a servant say to his master, I will not do as it pleaseth thee; though afterward he do it, he angereth him that nourisheth him.” The master nourishes the servant, and a servant who refuses him angers the one that feeds him.

And you are not just angering the master. You are also angering the Lord that nourisheth us. That is the order Colossians 4:1 completes from the other side: the servant honours the master, and the master gives the servant “that which is just and equal; knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven.”

precepts.label: Ephesians 6:5-6
precepts.why:
“Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal”. They said that they were the masters. Did they do that? No. They were living in the big house; we were living in the outhouse, and when we got emancipated, did they ever give us the forty acres and the mule? No. So they are showing that they are hypocrites. They are impostors. They’re the damn devil that the Bible speaks of.

Remember, Colossians, Ephesians and Philemon were all written generally at the same time, to the same region. Ephesians says the same thing Colossians does: “Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as unto Christ; Not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart”.

The servants are serving “as unto Christ”, as “the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart.” This is instruction to one people serving under Christ, not a charter for the slave masters of America, and the verse ends by reminding the masters they “also have a Master in heaven.”

precepts.label: Jeremiah 34:9
precepts.why:
To go a little deeper into who these servants are, Jeremiah says: “That every man should let his manservant, and every man his maidservant, being an Hebrew or an Hebrewess, go free; that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Jew his brother.”

Being a what? An Hebrew, or an Hebrewess. So these servants are Israelites. And the one they served was “a Jew his brother.”

That is the servant and master of Colossians 3:22 and 4:1: Israelite servants and Israelite masters, brothers. Christianity took a scripture about brethren and cherry-picked it to fit its evil narrative over us.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 6:1-2
precepts.why:
Paul elaborates on the masters: “Let as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed.” The servants are under the yoke, the yoke of bondage. If you had a master who still believed in the law of sacrifice, but you believed on Christ, you still honoured him. He follows sacrifice, but you still treat him with respect.

“And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren”. Now you have Israelite masters who believe on Christ. Don’t despise a master, your brother, that believes on Christ, because they are brethren.

Not one time has the Lord ever said we are brothers with the other nations. So that is showing you those masters are Israelites. When Colossians 4:1 tells masters to give their servants what is just and equal, it is speaking to Israelite masters over Israelite servants, their brethren.

precepts.label: Galatians 3:28
precepts.why:
Now this makes more sense: “There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.”

Neither Jew nor Greek we already understand from Colossians 3:11: the Greek-speaking Jews and the Jews. Neither bond nor free: the Israelite servant and the Israelite master. Neither male nor female: the manservant and the maidservant, the Israelite man and the Israelite woman.

“for ye are all one”: we are all one nation, under Christ. That is all it is talking about. So the servants and masters of Colossians 4:1 are one people in Christ, and that is why the master must give the servant what is just and equal.

precepts.label: Leviticus 25:55
precepts.why:
More on these servants: “For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.”

The children of Israel are servants, and they are his servants, the ones he brought out of Egypt. That is who the servants of Colossians are, and why the masters must remember they “also have a Master in heaven”: the servants belong to the Lord.

They changed the narrative and flipped the script, inserting themselves into the scriptures where they are not. Where they are, Leviticus shows it right after: “Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you”, and “they shall be your bondmen for ever”. They were originally our possession, but we sinned against our God and became their possession. Don’t worry: it is going to go back to the way it is supposed to be.

precepts.label: Romans 14:4
precepts.why:
When we read precept upon precept, in the context of the scriptures, we see how we have been lied to as a people. Paul asks: “Who art thou that judgest another man’s servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth.”

Who are you to judge another man’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. So our real master is Christ. That is the “Master in heaven” of Colossians 4:1, the one both servants and masters answer to.

And the servant is not left alone: “Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.” There it is. For God is able to make him stand.

thread.text: This is a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 36:25
precepts.why:
“Where no hedge is, there the possession is spoiled.” A bishop must be “One that ruleth well his own house”, and a man who will not lead his house has no hedge around it. If you don’t lead your house, you are going to lose control, and your possession, your wife, will be spoiled.

Failure to lead is one of the things husbands do that destroy marriages. Not stepping up, not taking control of your home, being a passive individual while your wife walks all over you. Eventually some other man is going to come along who catches her eye, and she is going to desire and look to him. Coach Dingolane destroyed a house that way, all because a man would not step up and lead his home.

The flock of God’s pasture are men, and leaders are men. If you are not there guiding, not there instructing, not there correcting, the marriage will come to a crashing halt with her standing over you.

That is why Paul asks, “For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?” How can you lead other men and tell them this is the way, if your own house is out of order, if your wife doesn’t listen to you and your kids don’t listen to you? You cannot be over men if you are not able to rule your own house. And the qualities of a bishop are for every man: a bishop is an example of what we are all supposed to be.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 3:7
precepts.why:
“Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel.” Failure to dwell with his wife according to knowledge is another of the things husbands do that destroy marriages, and ruling your own house well depends on it.

A wise husband studies his wife: her fears, her emotions, her struggles, her strengths. That is dwelling with her according to knowledge. When you understand your wife, you are able to guide your house. You push her toward greatness, but you also know her limits, and because you know them you set things up in the home so that things can work. If your wife is emotionally not there to deal with certain things, then you set it up another way. In order to lead, you have to know what they deal with, what they are able to do and what they are not able to do. That goes for your kids as well. You do it now without realizing it: you understand strengths and weaknesses, and you prioritize based on that.

Some men never learn their wives and then wonder why the marriage feels distant.

The other things that destroy a house show the same failure to know her: bitterness and harshness, holding things over her after she has repented and humiliating her, when you are supposed to love your wife as your own self; neglect, when a trip to Walmart is an exciting event for her because you haven’t taken her out, while ordering the house and dealing with the kids all the time is difficult; and withholding love and affection, because if she is not getting it from you, where is she going to get it from? A bishop rules his own house well by dwelling with his wife according to knowledge and giving her honour.

thread.text: And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.
