precepts.label: Titus 1:14
precepts.why:
“And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.” That is why people have left the truth of the word of God to follow fables. Christmas is a fable. All of those are fables, meaning lies, story-told lies, with symbolic meanings in the stories: Santa Claus and his blackened helper, Santa with his horse in the Netherlands and his flying reindeer here, Rudolph and the fairy dust. Our people have celebrated this foolishness for a long time.

Titus gives the warning: “Not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth.” Don’t give heed to them. Christmas and all these things are commandments of men, and they turn you from the truth.

That is why you have people online saying it is not wrong to celebrate Christmas, it is in your heart, it is how you feel, and all that crap. It is turning you from the truth of God. Some try to figure it out: we agree his birthday is not December 25th, so we can make up another day. That is what they do, but it always comes back to December 25th. It is still a fable and a commandment of men, and Paul told Timothy the people would turn away their ears from the truth to follow it.

precepts.label: John 10:22
precepts.why:
There is a winter holiday that Christ kept: “And it was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter.” Read on: “And Jesus walked in the temple in Solomon’s porch.” The feast of dedication is celebrated in the winter, and Christ was there at the feast in the wintertime.

So the holiday of the winter that Christ kept was the feast of dedication, not a December birthday. Christmas, December 25th and the birthday of Christ are fables and commandments of men, and people have turned their ears from the truth to follow them.

The same goes for the new year. The new year is in the spring, not the winter. Abib, or Aviv, means spring: the season when the young, tender barley ears first appear, marking the start of the religious new year around March or April in the Gregorian calendar, the time of the Passover and the firstfruits offering, signifying renewal and freedom from Egypt. They celebrate the new year in the winter. And if you see Israelite groups keeping Passover in February, or July, or June, there is something wrong. The truth is in the scriptures; the winter birthday and the winter new year are the fables they turned to.

precepts.label: Hebrews 7:14
precepts.why:
“Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same.” The children are the disciples, us, and Christ took part of the same flesh and blood. “For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham”, which is flesh and blood. “Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren.” In all things, not some things. How is a man made like his brethren in all things? By having a father and a mother.

Then Hebrews 7: “For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.” He sprang out of Judah based on his father. The tribe comes from the father, as every Israelite’s does.

The fathers show the same. God told David, “I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels.” David knew “that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne.” And Paul says Christ “was made of the seed of David according to the flesh.” According to the flesh: made flesh and blood like his brethren.

That is why Matthew says “When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.” Coming together was the customary wedding feast, as when Laban “made a feast” and Jacob went in unto his wife. Joseph and Mary were already espoused, and betrothal is marriage, so there was no fornication; they lay together before the feast. Child of the Holy Ghost means child of prophecy, the prophecy made to David. Joseph, a just man, was “not willing to make her a publick example”, which means stoned to death, and “was minded to put her away privily”: to hide her, because the child was his. Why would a just man hide a woman for something he did not do? And the angel called him “Joseph, thou son of David.” So our Lord sprang out of Judah through his father, made like his brethren in all things.

thread.label: Hebrews 6:1
thread.text: Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God,

classes.title: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.label: Hebrews 9:10
precepts.why:
Rome taught that in order to be saved you must be water baptized. Hebrews 6 answers it: “Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection”. The principles of the doctrine of Christ are animal sacrifice. The principle goes to the beginning; that is how we got forgiveness of sin at first. And among the things we must leave, Paul names “the doctrine of baptisms”.

Hebrews 9:10 shows what those washings were: “Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation”. Divers washings are carnal ordinances. They were imposed only until the time of reformation, and then they were to end.

So when Hebrews 6:1 says leave the principles, it means leave the meats, the drinks and the divers washings with the animal sacrifices. We did not get perfection in animal sacrifice, and water baptism belongs with those carnal ordinances.

precepts.label: Exodus 30:19
precepts.why:
Where did the washing come from? Exodus 30:19: “For Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet thereat”. The priests washed at the laver. This is where John the Baptist got it from.

Isaiah shows what the washing symbolized: “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil”. The water was a symbol of putting away evil.

John the Baptist did not make up water baptism. It came from the priests, and John was in the lineage of the priesthood; he was a Levite. So the doctrine of baptisms that Hebrews 6 says to leave is the priests' washing, one of the old ordinances Christ, the new high priest, brought to an end.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 2:22
precepts.why:
Jeremiah shows that the water never took away sin: “For though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me, saith the Lord God”. Wash all you want with nitre and much soap; the iniquity is still marked before God.

That is the proof that the washing was always symbolic. It came from the priests, from Aaron and his sons washing at the laver, and it was a sign of cleansing, not the cleansing itself.

So go back to Hebrews 6:1 and stress the word leaving: “Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection”. Leave the animal sacrifice, and leave the doctrine of baptisms with it. Rome's teaching that you must be dumped in the water to be saved is going back to what Paul said to leave.

precepts.label: Matthew 3:11
precepts.why:
The doctrine of baptisms Hebrews 6 says to leave includes John the Baptist. John said it himself: “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire”.

John used water. Christ baptizes with the Holy Ghost and with fire, not using water. Christ never used water, because water baptism was to end. It was always symbolic.

So when Paul says “let us go on unto perfection”, the baptism we go on to is Christ's, with the Holy Ghost and fire. The water was part of the principles we leave behind.

precepts.label: Leviticus 16:21
precepts.why:
Hebrews 6:2 goes on to “laying on of hands”, and Leviticus shows where that came from: “And Aaron shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions in all their sins, putting them upon the head of the goat”. That is what we did. The high priest laid his hands on the goat to put the sins of Israel upon it.

So Paul was saying: all that stuff the priests were doing, we have to leave it. Christ is the new high priest. The laying on of hands belongs with the animal sacrifice and the washings, the principles we leave to go on unto perfection.

precepts.label: 2 Maccabees 12:43
precepts.why:
Hebrews 6:2 also names “resurrection of the dead”, and 2 Maccabees shows how that was handled under the old ordinances: “And when he had made a gathering throughout the company to the sum of two thousand drachms of silver, he sent it to Jerusalem to offer a sin offering, doing therein very well and honestly, in that he was mindful of the resurrection”. A sin offering sent to Jerusalem for the dead. That is how we thought we got the resurrection, through the sacrifice.

So Paul lists them all to leave: “the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment. And this will we do, if God permit”. In Paul's letters they were still doing those things. It finally came to an end, with no ifs, ands or buts, in 70 AD, when Esau destroyed the temple, put the priests in slavery, and many of us fled into Africa. It was finished.

And there is no going back: “For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost”, “If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame”. Some Israelites said we have got to go back to animal sacrifice and water baptism. If you leave Christ and go back to that stuff, you cannot be renewed. They never believed. Brothers and sisters who leave this truth and go back to white Jesus and water baptism, we can't help them.

precepts.label: Exodus 5:14
precepts.why:
Moses “refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God”. Understand that in ancient Egypt everybody was not bad off. Things were not bad for Moses; Moses made things bad for himself by killing the Egyptian, and there was a consequence for killing an Egyptian, so Moses was on the run.

Exodus 5:14 shows that some of our own people were set up over us: “And the officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten, and demanded, Wherefore have ye not fulfilled your task in making brick both yesterday and to day, as heretofore?” The taskmasters set officers of the children of Israel over us. In ancient Egypt they were called officers; in America they are called Uncle Tom Negroes, house Negroes.

To be an officer you were making money. Some of our people in ancient Egypt had money and high standing, a form of good living, and they were okay with the oppression they were going through, until the officers started getting their behinds whooped too.

It is the same thing today: Beyoncé, Usher, the pastor praying for Trump, people with money who are comfortable here in modern day Egypt, spiritual Egypt. When a people live in oppression for centuries, oppression becomes a norm and you take it as a way of life. That is why the scripture talks about us trusting in the shadow of Egypt, trusting in oppression. Moses had that comfort and refused it, choosing to suffer affliction with the people of God.

precepts.label: Proverbs 29:1
precepts.why:
Hebrews warns “lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you”. Where does that root come from? Proverbs answers: “He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck”. He that is often corrected hardens his neck, meaning his mind. You can't tell that brother nothing: I'm a man, you a man, I do what I want. Well, do what you want and burn by yourself.

That is the mindset of a lot of our brothers and sisters. They never took the scripture serious. Leadership corrects them, corrects them, corrects them, to the point where the correction is null and void, because they are not going to apply anything. After a while the Lord says, this spirit is rebellious as hell; he always hardens his mind and doesn't give a damn what you're saying.

You end up hardening your heart from always having correction done to you, until at the end of the day bitterness is formed, and then you're out the door with your wife and your children.

So the question for every brother and sister: are you one of the many that shall be offended when correction comes, when the men are told to get their homes in order and the women to be that pillar of rest and not stress? Or will you get in check with the Lord? The bitterness of Hebrews 12 grows out of a neck hardened against reproof.

precepts.label: Psalms 109:6-9
precepts.why:
Hebrews says “Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau”. Paul is comparing the wicked of our people to Esau, who was wicked and estranged from the womb and went to the Canaanitish women when he wanted to get married. The bitter among us become compared to Edom, and Satan becomes their daddy. Psalms shows it: “Set thou a wicked man over him: and let Satan stand at his right hand.” That wicked man is Satan, the daddy of Esau and of the wicked of our people.

“When he shall be judged, let him be condemned: and let his prayer become sin.” Why does his prayer become sin? Because Christ said if you have an ought with your brother, go to him; leave your gift at the altar. You can't come to the Lord while the matter between you and your brother and your sister is not dealt with right. In 2018 there were extortioners speaking against leadership. You are not supposed to rise up against the hoary head; you are supposed to honor, and not revile the gods, your leaders. There was a lot of disrespect and dishonor.

“Let his days be few; and let another take his office. Let his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow.” That is what happens when Satan becomes your daddy. Repent.

So the profane spirit of Hebrews 12, the bitter brother or sister who turns on leadership, carries this lot. We are trying to encourage our people not to be worldly, not to keep the customs of Edom and the I-do-me, but to come back home to your people.

precepts.label: Baruch 3:36
precepts.why:
“He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” All the way of knowledge is the Bible. The Bible does not belong to all nations on earth; it was given only to the beloved Israelites.

That is who Peter is writing to: “This second epistle, beloved, I now write unto you”, to stir up their pure minds by way of remembrance, “That ye may be mindful of the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets”. The beloved of 2 Peter 3 is Israel his beloved of Baruch, the ones the way of knowledge was given to.

So when Peter warns “that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts”, he is warning the beloved about scoffers among them. Are we not seeing scoffers in these last days, like never before? Every black urban apologist is a scoffer. They don't believe the Bible. They don't believe Christ is black. They think Jesus is Caesar Borgia and the white man is coming to deliver them.

They say “Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.” Nothing has changed. But they “willingly are ignorant”, because we can take them to Deuteronomy and show them how things were prophesied and have come to pass, and it fits us perfect to a T. How are you going to say the Bible isn't a true book, when the knowledge in it was given to you?

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 2:2
precepts.why:
Peter asks, since this whole earth is reserved unto fire, “Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness”. That means we have to act right and speak right. A lot of our conversation is filth and sports. We have to train ourselves to speak the words of this book.

When we came into the school, they used to say about one of the elders: if you weren't talking about the Bible, don't talk to him; that's all he wanted to hear. Paul said the same: “For I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified.” He trained himself. All I want to hear is Bible. I don't want to hear Betty got a big booty. I don't want to hear how many touchdowns somebody ran or how far he hit the jump shot. I don't want to hear that crap.

That is holy conversation, and godliness is our actions, our works: the way we live must match the way we speak. The scoffers walk after their own lusts and their conversation follows their lusts. The beloved, knowing the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, train their minds and spirits to know nothing but Christ and him crucified, so that they may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:21
precepts.why:
Peter says “we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.” Isaiah 60 shows what that promise is. “Violence shall no more be heard in thy land”: the white man will be subdued, because he is the violent man, behind every coup and every war. The land is the land of Israel, with no “wasting nor destruction within thy borders”, and “thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise.”

“The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light”. That doesn't mean the sun and moon are done away with; they will be there, but the Israelites won't need them, because the Lord will be our light. “Thy sun shall no more go down”: our understanding shall no more go down, and our moon, our understanding, won't withdraw itself. And “the days of thy mourning shall be ended.”

“Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever”. That is why the new earth is one wherein dwelleth righteousness: because our people shall be all righteous. Esau isn't going to be there enjoying anything. “A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation”: we're going to have a whole lot of children. “I the Lord will hasten it in his time”: I'm going to speed it up.

The scoffers say all things continue as they were. But one day is with the Lord as a thousand years; he is not slack concerning his promise. So, beloved, seeing we look for such things, be diligent to be found of him in peace, without sin, and blameless.

precepts.label: Sirach 10:12-13
precepts.why:
John says “all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” The lust of the flesh: in America everything is accessible; order it and it's there in twenty minutes. The lust of the eyes: social media, looking at the big butt, keeping up with the Joneses, twerking, the competition of niggardom: I can jump on a car better than she can, I can roll a blunt this big, I can rap about nothing and can't say my ABCs. Our people love the world for those things but fail to love God.

And what is the pride of life? Sirach answers: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That is the pride of life we just read in 1 John. It is when you hate God and retract yourself from the love of the heavenly Father, when you prefer this world, this system and this setup over the guidelines of God, and would rather have this phobia of freedom and be guided by your oppressors.

The scriptures say pride goeth before destruction. When you go contrary to the Lord, death is at your door: “For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that hath it shall pour out abomination: and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.”

Your heart is then removed from the one that created you. “And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof”: Esau's rulership is already ordained to pass away. Will you escape when the destruction comes, or pass away with it?

precepts.label: Psalms 40:8
precepts.why:
John says “the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.” Who is he that doeth the will of God? David shows it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” He that doeth the will of God is the one who delights in his law.

That one abides for ever: you will have everlasting life, and you are going to rule over these kingdoms. Everything you could not see yourself living without in this world shall come to an end, but the one with God's law in his heart abides.

So you must hate this world and everything in it. Brothers, you have to hate even the sight of a sister in pants, to the point where it infuriates you instead of catching your eye. The YNs, the young nuisances walking around in the community, should infuriate you. Bring back the belt. But we have a belt: the God of Israel, and he is doing the whipping right now, and it will continue as long as our people love this kingdom in captivity.

Love not the world. Delight in his law, do his will, and abide for ever.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 4:12
precepts.why:
John is told, “What thou seest, write in a book, and send it unto the seven churches which are in Asia”, and the first of them is Ephesus. Paul writes to Timothy, “And Tychicus have I sent to Ephesus.”

That same Tychicus was sent to Colosse. In Colossians 4, “All my state shall Tychicus declare unto you, who is a beloved brother, and a faithful minister and fellowservant in the Lord: Whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose, that he might know your estate, and comfort your hearts”, together “With Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you.”

Ephesus is right there next to Colosse. The same messengers served that whole region, going between the churches of Asia. So the Colossians were not off by themselves: they were part of that same body of churches in Asia that Christ sent his word to in Revelation.

precepts.label: Colossians 4:16
precepts.why:
Paul tells the Colossians, “And when this epistle is read among you, cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans; and that ye likewise read the epistle from Laodicea.” The letters went back and forth between Colosse and Laodicea.

Laodicea is the last of the seven churches in Revelation 1:11: “Ephesus, and unto Smyrna, and unto Pergamos, and unto Thyatira, and unto Sardis, and unto Philadelphia, and unto Laodicea.” And Laodicea was right there next to Colosse.

Now it connects better. Colosse may not be named as one of the churches of Asia in the book of Acts, but when you put the map up, the churches of Asia are all right there together: Laodicea, Philadelphia, Sardis, all right there by Colosse. So when John was told to send what he saw “unto the seven churches which are in Asia”, it was the same region and the same people the epistle to the Colossians was written to.

precepts.label: Isaiah 57:1-2
precepts.why:
Philadelphia means brotherly love, and that church was a colony of Israelites. Christ, “he that hath the key of David”, tells them: “behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it”. That open door is salvation. “For thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name.” They were under persecution, so he says he will make the synagogue of Satan come and worship before their feet.

Then verse 10: “Because thou hast kept the word of my patience, I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world”. The hour of temptation is Jacob’s trouble, which leads into the world war and Armageddon. The church of Philadelphia will not be there when it happens. Does that mean a force field around them? No. They are at rest.

Isaiah 57 shows it: “The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart: and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.” That is exactly what we just read in Revelation 3:10. “He shall enter into peace: they shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness.” Each one walking: they are not dead.

So when brothers and sisters die and people say, they keep dying, listen: I have a reason. They are at rest. You do your little tears and cry, that’s fine, but the Lord is keeping the righteous from the evil to come, the way he kept Philadelphia from the hour of temptation.

precepts.label: Daniel 12:2-3
precepts.why:
Isaiah 57 says the righteous “shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness”: they are not dead. Daniel 12 says the same thing.

“And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake”. Those that sleep in the dust are the ones that died, and they shall awake, “some to everlasting life”: the righteous brothers and the righteous sisters; “and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

“And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.”

So the saints who died keeping the word of Christ’s patience are only sleeping. They were kept from the hour of temptation that comes upon all the world, Jacob’s trouble, and they will awake to everlasting life. That is why we do not grieve the righteous the way the world does.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 13:5
precepts.why:
Four angels hold the four winds of the earth, and another angel cries to them, “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” The four winds are held back for a reason, and Ezra shows what gathers from those four winds.

“And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea.” That multitude out of number is their military, gathered from the four winds to fight against Christ, the man that came out of the sea.

So the holding of the winds is this: do not let war pop off to the max until the servants of God are sealed. The armies of the nations are held back until the leaders of Israel, the hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes, are sealed with the law of God in Christ.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:16
precepts.why:
The angel ascending from the east has “the seal of the living God”, and the servants of our God are sealed in their foreheads. What is that seal? Isaiah says it: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” That is the seal of the living God: the law, sealed among his disciples, in Christ.

And the ones sealed are “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel”, twelve thousand of every tribe, from Juda to Benjamin. These are the leaders; the 144,000 is just the leading men. In order for them to be sealed, they have to know who they are, at least to some extent.

So how are you going to read that and be confused about the twelve tribes? You just read all of the tribes right there. You can't make this stuff up.

precepts.label: Hosea 1:10
precepts.why:
“After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number”. Now that we are bringing this out, the churches say we are all included, all backgrounds and cultures together. Where was that in 1964? Where was it on the slave ships? That is why the Bible says precept must be upon precept, line upon line, here a little and there a little.

Hosea 1:10: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered”. That is us. The multitude “which no man could number” is the children of Israel, whose number cannot be measured nor numbered.

“And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” The people told they were not God’s people are the same ones called the sons of the living God.

It also shows time has gone by. Moses said “ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”, because they were killing us; Hosea says we would grow to be like the sand of the sea. That is the great multitude standing before the throne.

precepts.label: Acts 2:5
precepts.why:
The great multitude is “of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues”, and the Christian says, see, we are all included. But read Acts 2:5: “And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.”

Out of every nation under heaven, and they were Jews. So “all nations” in Revelation 7:9 does not mean every race; it means the Israelites scattered into every nation, gathered out of them.

That is the all nations of Revelation 7:9: Jews out of every nation under heaven, the same people as the sand of the sea that cannot be numbered, standing before the throne and before the Lamb.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:10-12
precepts.why:
If you have time on the street, add Isaiah 11: “the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people”. Why the second time? Because the first time was under Moses.

He recovers the remnant “from Assyria”, modern-day Turkey, where you have the Afro-Turks; “and from Egypt”, lower Egypt and the Afro-Egyptians; “and from Pathros”, modern-day southern Sudan; “and from Cush”, Ethiopia; “and from Elam”, Iran and India, with the Afro-Iranians, the Siddis and the Dalits; “and from Shinar”, Iraq today and the Afro-Iraqis; “and from Hamath”, Syria today and the Afro-Syrians; “and from the islands of the sea”, like Cape Verde, the Hawaiian islands and the Melanesian islands.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” We are the outcasts of Israel.

That is the all nations right there: the remnant of Israel gathered out of every land they were scattered to, the great multitude of Revelation 7:9.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 2:38-42
precepts.why:
Revelation 7:4 gives “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel”, and then verse 9 gives the great multitude. They say, see, we are all included. Ezra explains it crystal clear.

“Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of the Lord”. That is Revelation 7:4, the 144,000. “Which are departed from the shadow of the world, and have received glorious garments of the Lord”: new bodies. “Take thy number, O Sion, and shut up those of thine that are clothed in white, which have fulfilled the law of the Lord. The number of thy children, whom thou longedst for, is fulfilled”. Verses 38 to 41 are Revelation 7:4.

Now verse 42: “I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised the Lord with songs.” That is Revelation 7:9. The great multitude is Zion, mount Zion.

So the 144,000 are the men, the Israelite leaders of the twelve tribes; the great multitude are more men, women and children of Israel. And “these are they which came out of great tribulation”: so much for the church teaching that we don’t have to go through tribulation.

precepts.label: Revelation 17:5
precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 28:68 says the Lord would bring us into Egypt again with ships, and “there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you.” Nobody can redeem us out of that Egypt, that house of bondage; only Christ, who bought us with a price, can redeem us from this spiritual Egypt.

Revelation 11:8 proves America is that Egypt: “And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt”. The dead bodies are the Israelites. Why dead? Because we don’t know who we are; we are in a dead state of mind; we left off keeping God’s laws.

Where is the great city? Revelation 17:5: “And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” That great city is Mystery Babylon the Great: America. And America is the abomination of the earth.

That is why it is spiritually called Sodom: sodomy goes on here; they legalized it. And it is spiritually called Egypt because, the same way the Israelites were enslaved in ancient Egypt, the Israelites were enslaved and are oppressed here in America: the land of oppression, the land of bondage, the land of slavery. What our forefathers experienced in ancient Egypt, they experienced here, and wherever those ships took us. And as God brought plagues on ancient Egypt, he is bringing plagues on this new Egypt.

precepts.label: Baruch 3:4
precepts.why:
“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”. The “their” is the Israelites. Why does it call us dead bodies? Baruch 3:4 answers: “O Lord Almighty, thou God of Israel, hear now the prayers of the dead Israelites, and of their children, which have sinned before thee”.

When we sin against God, God refers to us as dead. Remember the scripture says, keep my commandments and live. So Israelites living in sin are dead Israelites, even while they are walking around.

“And not hearkened unto the voice of thee their God: for the which cause these plagues cleave unto us.” That is why the plagues cleave unto us. One of those plagues is us going into slavery on ships: the transatlantic slave trade was a plague, one of the curses of Deuteronomy 28. Moses said we would go into tribulation again, this time by ships, and be sold to our enemies.

So the dead bodies lying in the street of the great city are the Israelites, spiritually dead, disconnected from our God, under the plagues that came because we did not hearken.

precepts.label: Baruch 3:10
precepts.why:
Baruch goes on: “How happeneth it Israel, that thou art in thine enemies’ land”? Now we are in our enemies’ land. America is your enemies’ land; they are the ones ruling this place.

“That thou art waxen old in a strange country”: we have waxed old in strange countries, because our land is the land of Israel.

“That thou art defiled with the dead”. What does it mean that we are defiled with the dead? We walk around like zombies. We have broken God’s laws and we are living in these lands not knowing who we are. We are confused; we call ourselves all kinds of different names and titles. We are the congregation of the dead, the valley of dry bones. That is us today.

That is why Revelation 11:8 says “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”: the twelve tribes of Israel, spiritually dead, disconnected from God, lying in the streets of our enemies’ land.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:32
precepts.why:
“Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long: and there shall be no might in thine hand.” Beside it stands verse 41: “Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them; for they shall go into captivity.” It is the same thing said twice: our children given into the hands of other people.

That is Revelation 11:10: “they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another”. Who were the gifts? We were the gifts, passed from one to another, from one generation of slaveholders to the next, like the negro girl about five years old deeded to him and his heirs forever. Merry Christmas. The two prophets are Judah and Ephraim; “these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth” when we were ruling, and when we were given into their hands it was payback.

The paintings from Britain, Italy, France and all over Europe show it: black children stripped from their parents, holding umbrellas, mirrors, birds and music for their masters, serving at the table, a grown sister in Nantes with the iron collar still on her neck. The same in Japan and China, where the Arabs brought us dressed the same way to hold the umbrella. They called us their negro favorites, as with the princesses of France, as Charlize Theron and Madonna have their adopted favorites today. Lucrezia Borgia, sister of Cesare Borgia and daughter of Pope Alexander VI, posed with her black slave boy as Mary with the child. They had black favorites in Russia too, where we once ruled.

The Jewish histories tell the same. Under the Inquisition, when families were taken, the children became wards of the holy office, given to foster parents to indoctrinate them with Catholic dogma and teach them to abhor anything Jewish, to despise all Jews, and to say the Jews killed our Lord and were cursed to perpetual wandering: the same doctrine Christians use on us today. When Jews were driven from Spain and could not pay to leave Portugal within the eight months, they were sold as slaves. King John had all Jewish children under fourteen torn from their parents' arms, dragged into the church and baptized; those under three given to Christians for a Christian education, in other words to be raised as slaves; those from three to ten shipped to St. Thomas, an island run by condemned criminals; those from ten to fourteen sold. The bereaved parents fell prostrate at the king's feet as he left church on a Sunday, begging, and he had them dragged from his path and mocked them as dogs whose whelps were torn from them.

That is thine eyes failing with longing for them all the day long, with no might in thine hand. A Christian education is a doctrine of slavery: Baptist, Pentecostal, Methodist, Seventh-day Adventist, Jehovah's Witness, you are raised as a slave.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 7:10
precepts.why:
“And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another”. Esau rejoiced over our downfall and made merry, as in Merry Christmas. We always thought, we were the gifts, and the history shows it: when Count Frederick von Hanau acquired a large part of what is now Suriname from the Dutch West India Company, he also received as a gift an Angolan man. They sent us around as gifts. Our sons, our daughters, our mothers and fathers were the gifts, because the two prophets, the kingdom of Judah and the kingdom of Israel, tormented them; we didn't play with Esau.

The Ecclesiastes called for at this moment is Solomon's word: “I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.” See that right there. The young Black Israelites in those European paintings were supposed to be the princes over Spain and Portugal, and they became servants to the white man: children snatched from their mothers, baptized and made slaves, holding the umbrella, the mirror, tending the horses and cattle.

So when you go into museums in America, France and England and see a picture of a little Black boy holding an umbrella, don't say, oh, look at that cute little Black boy. Now you know the history as it was: those were their slaves, the Moors, the Black Jews of Spain and Portugal, separated from their parents and given a limited education so they could be dumbed down. Princes walking as servants, and nations making merry and sending them one to another as gifts.

precepts.label: Matthew 4:8-9
precepts.why:
Revelation 13:2 says “the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority.” How do we know that is what it is talking about? Because you can be blessed by God or you can be blessed by Satan, and some people do not understand that.

Matthew shows it: “the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain, and sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them; And saith unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.” What is the stipulation? “if thou wilt fall down and worship me.” Fall down and worship Satan, and he will give you all this power and authority.

That is exactly what we read at the bottom of Revelation 13:2: the dragon, which is Satan in this part, gave this last beast his power, his nuclear power and armaments, his seat, and great authority. The beast of seven heads and ten horns, the European powers with America as the eighth head, took the offer Christ refused.

And people are still taking it. On Venice Beach you have people who want to be blessed by Satan: women run through by every so-called movie or music producer who walks up and down that beach, still waiting to be discovered; a man about 90 years old playing the guitar, waiting to be seen by Rolling Stone magazine. People are delusional.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 6:9-10
precepts.why:
Satan's stipulation is worship, and many of our people will pay it for money. Paul says, “But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.”

“For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.”

That is what Satan will have you do: pierce yourself through with many sorrows, because you covet to be rich in this world. If you covet fame and fortune in this world, you must worship Satan. You must; that is the only way. That is what the Bible is saying.

So the power and the seat and great authority that the dragon gave the beast in Revelation 13 is the same thing he offered Christ on the mountain, all the kingdoms of the world and the glory of them, and the price has always been the same: fall down and worship me. The ones who will be rich take that snare and err from the faith.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 3:18
precepts.why:
John “saw a beast rise up out of the sea”. When the Bible talks about a beast, it is talking about a race of men. Solomon says so: “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” Men are beasts.

So the beast of Revelation 13 is not a monster; it is a nation of men rising up out of the peoples of the world. It has seven heads: Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain, with America the eighth. Its ten horns are European nations: Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, Greece, France, Denmark and Ireland. Upon its heads is “the name of blasphemy”, and blasphemy means wicked lies against God.

And this beast carries the attributes of the beasts of Daniel 7: like a leopard, which is Greece; with the feet of a bear, the Persian and Median empire; and the mouth of a lion, ancient Babylon. The dragon, Satan, gives it its power, its seat and great authority. That is why things in the history of the Greeks, Persia and Babylon are being fulfilled again in these last days.

precepts.label: Revelation 17:15
precepts.why:
The beast rises “up out of the sea”. What is the sea? Revelation explains it: “The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.”

So when John says, “I stood upon the sand of the sea, and saw a beast rise up out of the sea”, he is witnessing the rise of a nation of men out of the peoples of the world. The beast is a race of men, as Ecclesiastes 3:18 shows, and the sea it comes out of is the peoples, multitudes, nations and tongues.

That nation has seven heads and ten horns, the European powers: the heads Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain, with America the eighth, and the ten horns the nations of Europe. One of its heads was wounded to death: Rome, in 193 AD, when Septimius Severus, Rome's first African emperor, took the throne and the Dark Ages were ushered in. The sea is the nations, and out of them rose this European beast.

precepts.label: 2 Maccabees 9:9
precepts.why:
The first vial brings “a noisome and grievous sore.” Noisome means foul smelling, harmful, noxious, extremely offensive to the senses, particularly the smell: a real nasty sore. It is the same plague that came on ancient Egypt, a boil breaking forth upon man and upon beast throughout all the land.

The record shows what noisome looks like on a man. When the Lord struck the wicked king Antiochus, “the worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man, and whiles he lived in sorrow and pain, his flesh fell away, and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army.” His flesh fell off him and his stink offended his whole army.

What could make a man get like that? A nuclear bomb explosion causes severe radiation burns, known as cutaneous radiation injury, that frequently lead to intense itching, blistering and open sores. The burns come in stages: first redness and swelling, then a latent phase, then severe blistering and deep, long lasting necrotic ulcers. When a nuclear bomb goes off and the blast does not kill you, you are going to be rotten, your skin falling off, and it is going to be noisome.

That is how we know this first plague belongs to that one hour, when the destruction comes on America, modern day Egypt: the same kind of sore that ate Antiochus alive falls on the men who have the mark of the beast.

precepts.label: Psalms 91:1-3
precepts.why:
The key thing in the verse is who the sore falls on: “upon the men which had the mark of the beast, and upon them which worshipped his image.” If it is only them, where are we? What happened to us? We are delivered.

Psalms 91 explains why. “He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.” If you dwell in the secret place of the Most High, you dwell in his shadow, meaning his protection. “I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.”

“Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence.” That is the first plague, the noisome pestilence, and the Lord will deliver you from it. That is why the scripture says the plague fell only on those that worship the beast and have his mark: because we are delivered.

This plague is coming in that one hour, and in that one hour, when the bombs are falling, it is not going to come near us. The radioactive waves, the noisome pestilence, the poisoned water will not touch us, because the Lord is going to deliver us up out of here. The same pestilence that destroys America passes over the people who dwell under his shadow.

precepts.label: Ezra 1:3-4
precepts.why:
Between verse 40 and verse 41 of 2 Esdras 13 there is a whole lot of history. Verse 40 is Assyria: “whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive”, before Babylon and before the Persians. Then Babylon took down Assyria and took her captives, and moved down and took Judah. Then the Persians came in. None of that is mentioned in the two verses; it jumps from Assyria to Persia, under Cyrus. So when verse 41 says “But they took this counsel among themselves”, what is the counsel? Ezra shows it.

“Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the Lord God of Israel, (he is the God,) which is in Jerusalem.” It is Cyrus speaking: the proclamation between the Most High and him, allowing Israel to go back and build in exchange for being able to take down Babylon.

“And whosoever remaineth in any place where he sojourneth, let the men of his place help him with silver, and with gold, and with goods, and with beasts, beside the freewill offering for the house of God that is in Jerusalem.” That was what was charged to Israel to go and do.

But the counsel the tribes took among themselves was different: “that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt”. The bulk of them said, we are not staying; we are not going back to build in Jerusalem; we are going to a further country. Ezra and Nehemiah are the first two books of Ezra, and 1 Esdras and 2 Esdras are the third and fourth, and together they detail this history.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 9:26-28
precepts.why:
“For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half”. If it took us a year and a half to get from one area to another, don’t you think we were making stops? Maritime means things connected with the sea, oceans and navigation: shipping, commerce, naval operations. We were running those ports, and even where it was not us particularly, we had understanding with the nations we passed by. The Red Sea and the Indian Ocean connected Africa to the wider world as early as the third century BCE, with trade to Arabia, India, Persia and China.

Solomon had a navy of ships: “And king Solomon made a navy of ships in Ezion–geber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red sea, in the land of Edom. And Hiram sent in the navy his servants, shipmen that had knowledge of the sea, with the servants of Solomon.” Shipmen that had knowledge of the sea: those are the maritime men.

Ezion-geber is at the northern tip of the Red Sea’s Gulf of Aqaba, by modern-day Aqaba in Jordan and Eilat. That is very near the region where the brothers entered into the Euphrates. “And they came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and brought it to king Solomon.” Ophir is not far from those same areas.

So we had maritime trade going on even in Solomon’s time. It was no mystery for us to make it from where we were, out of Persia, over to the Americas, because those ports were there. That is how the journey took a year and a half, stopping at the ports, until we came into the region called Arsareth, the land Columbus identified with America.

precepts.label: Isaiah 13:12
precepts.why:
Solomon’s ships “came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold”. Isaiah uses that same gold: “I will make a man more precious than fine gold; even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir.”

We often read this and keep going, and some will say it is the best gold, but we don’t go deeper into what the gold of Ophir is. The gold of Ophir is an exceptionally fine, pure gold, prized in the ancient world, famous as what King Solomon and King Hiram of Tyre brought in, and its exact location remains one of history’s greatest archaeological mysteries.

That is what the Most High is going to make you men: that pure fine gold. The same tribes who crossed the waters on those old maritime routes, whose record the historians call mythical, are the men the Most High will make more precious than the golden wedge of Ophir.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:27
precepts.why:
“For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you”. That great multitude is what Christ said: you shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. And “they shall take away certain of you, and feed you, being idle”. Idle, i-d-l-e: a person avoiding work; lazy, indolent, slothful, workshy, shiftless, loafing; without purpose or effect, pointless.

In this truth, if you are idle you are avoiding work. Not work in the world: God's work. You are lazy in this truth. You have no purpose; you are just here. Some of you have been here for years and you have no office, doing nothing. You are idle.

“Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teacheth much evil.” Brothers and sisters, when you are idle in the truth, you are learning evil. That is why you spend your time on porn, smoking cigarettes, smoking weed, hitting women up in their DMs. You have idle time, and there is a whole lot of work in this truth to be done.

We can spot that idleness as soon as you come in: the one who sits down and just looks around, looking at the women's side, taking no notes. If this means something to you, you are engulfed in it; you are writing things down and trying to put it to memory. The idle are the certain ones the multitude will take away and feed.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 4:1-5
precepts.why:
The idle will be fed “with things offered unto idols.” Idols in the Bible are statues, figurines, golden calves, and also money, career and power that compete with God for worship. So what is the most idolatrous religion here in America? Christianity. You may think that is biased; Paul identifies the religion.

“Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils”. This is the latter times. Why will some give heed to seducing spirits? Because you are idle; you have idle time. “Speaking lies in hypocrisy”: I believe in God, but I am not going to do anything the Bible says. “having their conscience seared with a hot iron; Forbidding to marry”: what religion forbids men to marry? Catholics; that is Christianity. “and commanding to abstain from meats”: who cannot eat meat for 40 days? Catholics; they call it Lent.

Those meats “God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth”, and the truth is God's law. “For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving: For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” Where is the food sanctified by the word of God? Leviticus 11.

The Roman Catholic Church is the mother church of every Protestant denomination on the tree: Orthodox, Jehovah's Witness, Presbyterian, Lutheran, Methodist, Episcopalian, Mormon, Evangelical, Pentecostal, Baptist, Adventist, Anglican, all the way to Christian nationalism. That is the idolatry the multitude will feed the idle, and they are already saying out loud that they are going to impose it on this country.

precepts.label: Revelation 13:6-8
precepts.why:
What do all those churches have in common? They worship the image of the beast. “And he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven.” Their blasphemy is the perversion of the gospel of Christ, the perversion of the truth.

“And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them”. Esau made war with us: Rome, Spain, Portugal. Pope Nicholas V made that edict to enslave us and force us into Christianity. And they overcame us; they enslaved us. “and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations.”

“And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him”: the same man that overcame us. A book published in 1920, The Pillory, the Tale of the Borgia Pope, says it is an open secret that Cesare Borgia, son of Pope Alexander, posed for the image of Jesus. Salvatore, the savior: that is Cesare Borgia. Even Muslims will tell you that image is Jesus; ask a Buddhist and he will say the same. Everybody acknowledges it as Jesus the Christ.

All that worship him are those “whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” That is the idol the multitude will feed to the idle.

precepts.label: Revelation 12:17
precepts.why:
In every place and in the next cities there shall be “a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.” Revelation shows who is behind it: “And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.”

The dragon is wroth: our enemies see us and they are angry. That is why in France they already said, shut down IUIC; a black Jesus, the Israelites, that is anti-semitic, we cannot allow this to go on. And he went to make war with the remnant: that is physical war, not only spiritual. That is tribulation, Jacob's trouble, persecution against those who keep the commandments and the testimony of Jesus Christ.

Christ warned of the same: “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” You say you would never consent to their religion, but a whip across your back will change some of you, and you will be compelled to blaspheme.

And those who consent will be had in derision. Nobody likes a traitor. Like the apes in Planet of the Apes who betrayed their own and wore the word donkey before they were killed, Esau will use you and get rid of you. The ones who keep the commandments and the testimony are the ones the dragon makes war with; that is why Christ said, if they persecute you in this city, flee to the next.

precepts.label: 1 Maccabees 1:41-50
precepts.why:
“They shall be like mad men, sparing none, but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.” We read the book of Acts and think that could never happen again, but Paul himself said, “being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.” The prophecy says it is going to happen again, and it happened under the Greeks too.

“Moreover king Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom, that all should be one people, And every one should leave his laws: so all the heathen agreed according to the commandment of the king. Yea, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.” That is what is going to happen again. It happened in the time of Paul, in the time of the Maccabees, in Babylon when they tried to get us to worship the false god. That which has been is that which shall be; there is no new thing under the sun. Idolatry: leave that God and come worship this god.

They sent letters “that they should follow the strange laws of the land”, profane the sabbaths and festival days, sacrifice swine's flesh, leave their children uncircumcised, “To the end they might forget the law, and change all the ordinances. And whosoever would not do according to the commandment of the king, he said, he should die.” You think they cannot make a Sunday law and say, that Sabbath thing, no, worship God on the day we say?

The same thing we read in the Maccabees is what Rome, Spain and Portugal did to our people in the Inquisition; read Jews and Moors. And you say it can never happen, this is the United States of America? It happened during slavery. The same thing.

precepts.label: Hebrews 10:34
precepts.why:
“For they shall waste and take away their goods, and cast them out of their houses.” They did it in the time of Rome, when the Pharisees did it with Rome's guidance. Paul tells the Hebrews, “For ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods, knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.”

Ye had compassion of me in my bonds: when Paul was in prison, they supported him. And they took joyfully the spoiling, the robbing, of their goods: their homes and houses, lands and properties. Those Israelites sacrificed their whole livelihood. They knew that supporting Paul would reveal them, and whatever they had would be taken.

Are we prepared for that? Do we really think about it? The cushy side of the room: I'm so comfortable, I got my new house, my new car, my new hair, my new nails. Are you ready for what the scriptures say is going to happen? Are we willing to lose everything, knowing we have in heaven a better and enduring substance? That is another level of faith we have to build ourselves up to in the short, limited time we have.

Even the world is warning that if a crisis comes and the government says get on a bus for your safety, do not get on: prepare your food, water, power and shelter so you do not have to rely on them. We have been telling our people that for years.

precepts.label: Matthew 10:32-33
precepts.why:
“Then shall they be known, who are my chosen; and they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.” That verse is very important, because it goes back to what Christ said: “Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven. But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.”

Christ is talking about tribulation, persecution, Jacob's trouble. So what will the chosen be saying about Christ in that day, will they deny him or confess him? They are going to confess him.

Why does it say “Then shall they be known”? Because right now everybody says they believe in the Lord. Women say it; men say it. But when this starts to happen, you are going to see who is real and who is fake. On that day the ones who confess Christ before their tormentors are the ones known to be his chosen, tried as gold in the fire, and he will confess them before his Father.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 3:1-6
precepts.why:
The chosen are “tried as the gold in the fire”, and Wisdom gives more detail. “But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them.” Christ said we will be afflicted, so what does no torment mean? That is the lake of fire. That torment will not touch us.

“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery, And their going from us to be utter destruction: but they are in peace.” Christ said, fear not them which kill the body; fear him who can kill body and soul. Man cannot touch your soul. They seem to die because the body died, but the real man, the real woman, is not dead. We keep falling for Esau's craftiness: it's all over, we're finished. It is not over. They are in peace; that is sleep, rest.

“For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality. And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded”. Jacob's trouble is just a little chastisement. “for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” God is going to prove us. Everybody says they believe; he will say, let that one get caught early and see what they do. He found them worthy because they confessed Christ before their tormentors.

“As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.” The death of the saints is as a burnt offering to the Lord. Christ gave his life, and he said if you will not take up your cross and follow him, you are not worthy of him.

precepts.label: Matthew 10:38
precepts.why:
Wisdom says the righteous are tried as gold in the furnace and received as a burnt offering. Christ said, “And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.”

Christians say that means you cannot pay your bills and you have to carry all your problems on your back. No, that is not what it is talking about. When Christ was carrying the cross, where did it lead him? To death. He is saying the same thing for us.

We have to be willing to sacrifice ourselves. That is what Wisdom of Solomon was just saying: the souls of the righteous who die for the truth are in the hand of God. If you cannot confess the Lord, even unto death, you are not worthy to be his disciple. That is the cross, and that is how the chosen will be known.

precepts.label: Acts 12:1-15
precepts.why:
“Hear, O ye my beloved, saith the Lord: behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliver you from the same. Be ye not afraid neither doubt”. Why neither doubt? Because doubt comes. My mama just got put to death, my children, my wife; Lord, are you going to save us? Remember John the Baptist when he was imprisoned; that little bit of doubt crept in. Acts shows the situation.

“Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.)” James was beheaded; Peter was in prison. The angel brought Peter out, and he went to “the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying.” That was a safe house where Israelites were hiding and praying. When the damsel knew Peter's voice, “they said unto her, Thou art mad”, and “Then said they, It is his angel.”

What did they think had happened to Peter? That he had been put to death. It shows you could not go visit him. There was no visitation, as there are prisons like Guantanamo Bay in Cuba today, with no lawyers and no visitors, and they are building more like it. So do not think, the brothers don't care about me, the sisters didn't come visit me. There will be places nobody can visit you. It is not that we do not care; we cannot get to you. All the saints could do was pray.

And Peter was on the run, a fugitive from the government the rest of his life. The Lord intervened for one and gave him more time, and the other, James, was killed. It is going to get like that, brothers and sisters. That is why we study, pray and apply: knowing ahead of time is supposed to strengthen your resolve, so that you are not afraid, neither doubt.

precepts.label: 1 John 1:8-10
precepts.why:
“for God is your guide, And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down”. Why say, let not your sins weigh you down? Because we do sin, and churches love to try to trap you with it. “If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.”

Christians on the street will say, do you sin, my brother? Yes. But my sin cannot justify you continuing in sin. Verse 9 is the key; verse 9 is the difference between me and you.

When we start cutting them up, they say, you think you're better than us? Do you sin? Tell them yes, and go right here and show them the difference. They are liars, because they teach that you can sin with no consequences. We teach that if we do sin, the black Messiah laid down his life, if we believe on him, so that we can fight to stop sinning. Simple answer; don't let them jam you up.

We do make errors and fall into folly at times. Confess it and keep fighting, and let not your sins weigh you down.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:11
precepts.why:
“let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” “Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins”. When you keep entertaining that sin, eventually you will be bound by it. Peter says, “Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul”.

This is a spiritual war, a war for your soul. Take porn. Brothers say, I got it under control; it don't bother me. No, you don't have it under control. Picture a hallway of doors. A lot of you say, I only watch straight porn, like it is a good thing. That is door number one. Then the threesome, then the train. After a while you get desensitized; that does not excite you anymore, so you go to the next door down: chicks with dicks, then bestiality, then scat, then lesbian, then pedophilia. That is where the doors lead.

It is not normal. And you know it is the devil: when the Bishop was a little kid, his father had magazines hidden up in the drop ceiling. How did two little boys know to get a chair and climb up there, when they never saw their father do it? Playboy, Hustler, then VHS, then DVDs, and today easy access in your hand.

That is how iniquity lifts itself up until you are bound with your sins, covered like a field with thorns. Abstain from fleshly lusts; they are at war with your soul.

precepts.label: Romans 6:14-16
precepts.why:
When you keep entertaining a sin, it binds you. Paul says, “For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.” We are not under the law of sacrifice, but under grace. “What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid.”

“Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” His servants ye are to whom ye obey. If you wake up thinking about porn, go to work thinking about porn, and go to sleep thinking about porn, that is your god. You are its servant.

Grace is not a license to keep sinning; it is so that sin shall not have dominion over you. Christ laid down his life so we could fight to stop sinning, not so we could be bound in it. And when you are bound, there is no magic scripture that will release you; you have to want to be released.

precepts.label: Hebrews 6:4-8
precepts.why:
“Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns, that no man may travel through! It is left undressed, and is cast into the fire to be consumed therewith.” Hebrews says the same thing.

“For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance”. Those who were once enlightened, who came into this truth, and fall away back into their sin or back into false religion: it is impossible to renew them again to repentance.

“For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.”

That is the field of 2 Esdras 16:78, covered with thorns, left undressed and cast into the fire. The ground that drinks in the word and brings forth fruit receives blessing; the one bound with its sins and bearing thorns ends in the fire.

precepts.label: Revelation 13:17
precepts.why:
Tobit had a decent job in captivity, over the king’s accounts, and while he was well off he did good: “I gave many alms to my brethren, and gave my bread to the hungry, And my clothes to the naked”. When Sennacherib came back from Judea, where an angel killed 185,000 of his men, he came back mad and took it out on Ephraim, throwing them off the walls. Tobit would sneak and bury them: “I buried them privily”. He was not supposed to; the king wanted to see those bodies, “but the bodies were not found, when they were sought for of the king.”

Then he got ratted out: “when one of the Ninevites went and complained of me to the king, that I buried them”, he knew he “was sought for to be put to death” and became a fugitive. “Then all my goods were forcibly taken away, neither was there any thing left me, beside my wife Anna and my son Tobias.” Everything he had, they took from him.

That is what Revelation 13 means when it says no man should buy or sell. All the positions and things you have here: the time is going to come when you go against this system, teach against it, and do not support the beast, and everything you have they will take from you. Tobit is the example. They took his possessions, and most likely his wife and child were taken too, imprisoned, because he was considered an enemy of the state. That is the consequence for serving God, and the time is coming when you will have to make the choice to serve God.

But the Lord spared his son and wife. Within fifty-five days Sennacherib’s own sons killed him, and Sarchedonus set Tobit’s nephew Achiacharus over the accounts. “And Achiacharus intreating for me, I returned to Nineve.” His nephew was cupbearer, “keeper of the signet, and steward, and overseer of the accounts”, next unto the king, and he spoke for his uncle. Then “my wife Anna was restored unto me, with my son Tobias, in the feast of Pentecost”: he was keeping the feasts in captivity, not in Jerusalem.

Tobit stayed faithful, and he was not alone out there being righteous. He looked out for his people with the status he had, fed the hungry and gave alms to those keeping the commandments in captivity, and when it came back around his nephew did the same for him. The Lord looked out for him as he looked out for his own people.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 33:14
precepts.why:
Moses blesses Joseph: “Blessed of the Lord be his land, for the precious things of heaven, for the dew, and for the deep that coucheth beneath,” “And for the precious fruits brought forth by the sun, and for the precious things put forth by the moon”. Joseph's sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, dwell on islands: the Puerto Ricans and the Cubans, among others.

The precious things of heaven are the rain; the deep that coucheth beneath is the oceans that give riches beneath the waters. There are certain fruits brought forth by the sun, and certain things that come forth only by moonlight on those islands, like the coquí frog, which is nocturnal and comes out especially under the moonlight, making its noise.

That blessing points to the moon at its peak, what they call the full moon today, which is actually the new moon. That is what leads into Ecclesiasticus 43:6: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.”

precepts.label: Leviticus 23:1
precepts.why:
The moon serves “in her season for a declaration of times”. Leviticus 23 shows what those times are: “Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of the Lord, which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.” Convocations means gatherings.

The first holy day God tells Moses to list is the Sabbath: “Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest”, instituted from Genesis 2. Then: “These are the feasts of the Lord, even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.” He did not say seasons for the Sabbath, because the Sabbath is all year round. The ones that follow are seasonal holy days.

“In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover”, in the spring. Then the feast of unleavened bread on the fifteenth day; Pentecost, counting fifty days; “In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall ye have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets”, which is the seventh new moon celebration; the day of atonement on the tenth day of the seventh month; and “The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles”.

So the “declaration of times” is the high holy days. “From the moon is the sign of feasts”: every feast is counted from the new moon, when it is in its brightness, because that is how it was in the kingdom.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 6:9
precepts.why:
What is “a sign of the world”? One answer given from 2 Esdras 6:9, that Esau is the end of the world and Jacob the beginning of the world that follows, is that the sign of the world goes into our rulership and their destruction. That is not 100% wrong, and it should not be discounted.

The fuller understanding is this. The moon at its full is when we were in our full power and full understanding, in the kingdom. As it wanes and gets dark, it is us going into captivity, into full darkness. And once it gets back to fullness, it is us going back into our glory, back into the kingdom. That is the passing from Esau's world to Jacob's.

The moon's phases represent the stages the world is in: “a light that decreaseth in her perfection”, “increasing wonderfully in her changing”. And in the kingdom it will not wane again: “the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun”, and the sun has no phases. When Jacob's world follows Esau's, there is no going back into darkness.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:1
precepts.why:
“Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.” Arise means wake up; shine means teach; and the light that is come is Christ, who said, I am the light. “For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people”. We are in the grossest of darkness; we have lost our heritage and lost everything. When you see the moon dark, that is what it represents: darkness has covered the whole world.

Psalms 82 shows the same darkness. “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” The little g is us. Asaph, with the Holy Spirit upon him, records what we did wrong as the gods of the earth: “How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked?” We were to defend the poor and fatherless and deliver the needy, but “they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” “But ye shall die like men”: our godhood was taken from us. “Arise, O God, judge the earth: for thou shalt inherit all nations.”

Something in the heavens is out of course because of our sins. God made “two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night”. But in the kingdom, Isaiah 30:26: “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” The sun has no phases; in the kingdom the moon, the sign of the world, will not go dark again. And the sun we call so bright is not bright at all next to that.

Binding up the breach is Amos 9:11: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”, gathering the twelve tribes of Israel back again. That is when Isaiah 60:1 is fulfilled: our light is come, the moon is back at its fullness, and Israel is back in the kingdom.

precepts.label: 2 Maccabees 5:6
precepts.why:
Under the Greeks, “the merchants of the country, hearing the fame of them, took silver and gold very much, with servants, and came into the camp to buy the children of Israel for slaves”, and Syria and the Philistines joined in. Others helped the Greeks, and so did one of our own.

“But Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, not considering that to get the day of them of his own nation would be a most unhappy day for him; but thinking they had been his enemies, and not his countrymen, whom he conquered.” Jason was an Israelite, and he hated his own people. We think our people love themselves; no. He treated us like enemies, because he wanted to please the Greeks. Don't be surprised when you see black men and black women do all they can to please the enemies of our people. They will be worse on you than white men.

Read on: “for all this he obtained not the principality, but at the last received shame for the reward of his treason”. He was a treasonous negro, and the Most High cannot stand a traitor. He was “fleeing from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws, and being had in abomination as an open enemy of his country and countrymen”, and “cast out into Egypt.” Imagine being banished, unable to come back to your own country because you were a traitor.

“Thus he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land”, thinking to find succour among the Lacedemonians, where Sparta was. “And he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor any solemn funerals at all, nor sepulchre with his fathers.” What goes around comes around.

precepts.label: Colossians 3:25
precepts.why:
Jason drove many out of their country and perished in a strange land; he cast out many unburied and had none to mourn for him. That is the law Paul states: “But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done: and there is no respect of persons.”

Negroes do evil and think there is not going to be a big payback. You are going to get it. It does not matter that Jason was an Israelite; there is no respect of persons. He slew his own citizens without mercy to please the Greeks, and he received shame for the reward of his treason.

And it was not only Jason. When the king heard of it, he thought Judea had revolted, took the city by force of arms, and there was “killing of young and old”, fourscore thousand destroyed in three days, and no fewer sold as slaves than slain. The Greeks were selling us as slaves long before the slave auctions we know today, and the ones among us who help the enemy against our own people will receive for the wrong they have done.
